GTA V is going to be a landmark game for the 2010s, with how many copies it's sold, and the game itself. Grand Theft Auto has always had an affinity for films and cinematography (note the near useless 'cinematic mode' you can use when you drive) and this is the most cinematic entry in the series. The game follows a 'Crime/drama/liar revealed' type story, one that hasn't really been done in the series so far. One of the characters is more or less washed up, an old veteran in the crime scene. Trevor, even after being exiled is still heavily involved with serious crime, even more so than Franklin. Franklin would be the most 'GTA' of the trio, as he's just a gangster trying to work his way to the top. The story really kicks off when the three of them meet.
To talk about the gameplay, it has been improved, and feels and looks better than GTA IV. The driving especially has been changed for the better, going from floaty and realistic, to tight and video gamey. The gun play is more or less the same, except now all the guns don't sound like you're hitting a plastic bottle against the floor. The set pieces in the story are especially fun to play through, my favorite being the boat mission, and the shootout through the recycling plant.
The music in this game is stellar, icey synths over stuttering percussion on the loading screen, to big band brass when you're playing through missions, to even some other genres that characters will use the radio for (the mission where you blow up the O'neil brother's meth house). This game feels very very modern most of the time, but will sometimes dip into the 80's or 90's.
One of the most glaring flaws in the GTA franchise is still very prominent in this entry; you can't meaningfully interact with the large, beautiful world rockstar has built for you. People will run you over, they'll attack you if you look at them for too long. This open world serves only as a hub area for missions, and collectibles, and any wacky stuff you want to do in your free time. These wacky killing sprees can be written off easily if you play as Trevor, or even micheal, where as in GTA IV it would create a sort of ludo narritive dissonance when put up against Niko's character.
Dispite this, I still love GTA V, it's characters, it's story, it's gameplay, and especially it's music and visuals. 9/10

I have not played the strategy portion of this game, so I will only review the FPS part of it.
Heroes and Generals has the right idea and concept.  Unfortunately, the execution is awful.  Quite simply, Heroes and Generals is an attempt at what could have been a phenomenol game.
Balancing:Unless you play the 'Encounter' mode, you will almost certainly meet enemy vehicles.  The problem is, these vechicles are way too powerful.  Often, you will spend entire matches being sniped by tanks, spawncamped by planes dropping bombs, and getting run over by trucks and motorcycles.  The game is noticably tipped in a sniper's favor, with subpar graphics (will be discussed later) making it difficult to spot any enemy at all. 2/10
Graphics:The graphics, are, to say the least, mediocore at best.  No matter what graphic setting you are at, objects in the distance will shimmer, plants appear 2D and flat, and lighting is often off.  This is the result of the developers deciding to build their own graphics engine, which shows an admirable effort, however, the efforts have not paid off.  Call of Duty 2 from 2007 in my opinion, has comparable or better graphics than this game. 6/10
Gameplay:Heroes and Generals features massive maps, which, while can at times provide an amazing time, is also a cause for bitter disappointment.  You will often spend long times running to a faraway objective, only to be shot by a sniper you did not know even was there.  However, large maps often make for large and exciting battles, so this can go both ways.  Spawn protection is mediocore.  There is noting protecting you in the spawn except for an invisibliliy shield that is turned off as soon as you walk into the 'combat area', making you easy pickings for spawncampers.  Gunplay is horrible.  The gun mechanics feel clunky, and the game uses a health bar system, making the player with the more expensive and therefore superior weapon almost certain to come out on top in a firefight.  Movement in this game is good.  The movement is easy to get used to.  The physics are horrilbe.  Planes do not stall, ragdoll physics are implemented for infantry, tank turrets rotate too fast, bicycles turn themselves upright, etc. I have not yet experienced issues with lag, only being put into high ping matches.  You will often join a battle that ends 2 minutes later, which is not too big of a deal, but is very annoying when you just want a match quickly.  The sounds in game are very nice, with realistic gun sounds, and the ability to hear other player's footsteps is a nice touch.  The animations are smooth and nicely done.  6/10
Economy:Heroes and Generals will force you to buy better guns and upgrade them.  In additon to this, you must 'maintain' all of your weapons using in-game currency.  You unlock better equipment through the use of ribbons, which, unless you are willing to pay for premium accounts or buy in-game currency, will quickly turn into an insufferable and agonizing grind.  In short, it is the player who has money to spend on the game that can buy all the best equipment and win.  Heroes and Generals is most certainly, a pay to win game. 1/10
Developers:The game has subpar developers.  Often, the community will ask for features that take years to be implemented or do not get implemented at all.  They have designed an economy system that is designed for unreasonable amounts of money to be spent on the game, although, they DO have to pay themselves somehow.  However, the pay to win aspect of this game is utimately what has ruined the game for me, making it more of a chore rather than a pasttime.  The developers are also very slow to implement bug fixes. 6/10
Optimization:Horrible.  The game takes more resources than Battlefield 1 to run.  I have a GTX 1050Ti, a rather capable graphics card.  I have above the recomended specs, yet I will often get massive frame drops.  Sometimes it will go as bad from 80fps to 30fps. 5/10
Community:The playerbase is okay, with many people willing to help and explain aspects of the game to you.  However, teamwork in most matches is nonexistent, and there is a fairly large population of 'trolls', who will teabag you as well as sending you caustic messages through the feature of naming guns.  However, much of the playerbase remains mature. (most of the time)
(you will see the name of the gun when a person kills you with it).  7/10
Overall:Heroes and Generals is great if you want a World War II themed arcade shooter with little to none historical accuracy.  One or two matches can be very fun, but you will quickly realize that the game is just a subpar game that you have to put many hours into the actually somewhat enjoy.  If not for its flaws, then Heroes and Generals might have been a great game, with massive battles with lots of players.  Keep playing it if you enjoy it, take a risk and get if you want, but as for me, it has not been a stellar experience playing this game.

I am one of those people that look at a free game and don't expect to be able to be given an experience equal to a game that you pay money for. I see a lot of people calling the devs incompetent, who must all be very succesful developers with a laundry list of succesful games with active communities. You've played this game, some for 100s of hours, clearly they did something right. To pretend that you know more about how the game SHOULD, only being able to view the game from the perspective of a player is ridiculous.
People who contribute to keep the developers in business are going to recieve benefits, the only thing that even makes sense to give people in a game like this, will most likely give them an advantage, this is a World War II FPS, they're not gonna give you shiny skins or loot boxes.
I appreciate this game for the older weaponry which is less powerful giving your avarage soldier a longer lifetime on the field. There's much more strategy in positioning and moving throughout the level.
There are problems and things that are aggrevating, even as the best player you find things to blame when you're not doing well, valid or not.
Also I see a lot of mention of the grindy aspect, which I for one appreciate. It's called actually having to put in the work to acquire better gear. And it forces players to specialize in a certain playstyle, letting them fit into a certain role.
If you can play a match and just be happy with how you did on a personal level, understanding that there will be a difference between people who pay or put in thousands of hours and you and just focus on the fact that no matter how you do in match, you're still progressing in the game, which, because of how long it takes, instantly is more valueable than a game who gives you everything after playing it for half an hour.

I am a huge Wipeout fan (especially Wipeout HD, for the PS3) so I had great hopes for this game. But after waiting and waiting they are still not getting there. Not to mention: Anyone who dares to create an arcady racing game without splitscreen mode gets a full doze of recentment from me!
If you miss something like Wipeout and like me refuse to buy a PlayStation to play just that one game, then I recommend Redout instead... However, it lacks splitscreen as well! What is this? The anti-social evolution of gaming? Gaah!... However, Redout at least feels good, even though the colour palette in Redout makes my head fuzzy after an hour playing. But this review is about Formula Fusion, right, back to it... not worth it. Maybe later, but I seriously doubt it.
Do I really have to get my wallet out and buy a PS4 just so I can buy and play the newest iteration of Wipeout? Really PC master race? Throw me a freakin' bone here! Console companies: Stop enslaving our games!

Having played Wipeout since it was on the Sega Saturn (and PS1), I've been looking for something to fill the gap that Sony left when they in cold blood, murdered Wipeout, and cutting the last thread that held me to Sony's consoles. I've played Redout, but it just didn't do for me what Wipeout did... Though in VR, Redout is something completely different, but we won't get into that.
I bought Formula Fusion with a bit of skepticism. There's a bunch of Wipeout players around who say this doesn't hold up to the standard or the legacy... WIPEOUT IS DEAD, YOU CAN'T REPLACE PERFECTION!
After about 30 minutes of playing, I can only say that this about what I would have expected if we were in another universe where Wipeout still existed, and this was the next Wipeout for the PS4. No, it's not the perfect game Wipeout HD and Wipeout Fury were. No, it doesn't quite handle like Wipeout. No, it's not a full color 1990s cyber spectrum of blinding rainbows that Wipeout sometimes was (I'm happy about that, it's annoying in the Wipeout Omega Collection.)
It's not the exact same game. It can't be, never will be... but as a new franchise, it's clearly the next of kin to Wipeout, even it doesn't have the medals that Wipeout earned itself, clubbing F-Zero (seriously... F-Zero games are awful) and all others to death.
--- start edit ---
I do want to note that unlike Wipeout, Formula Fusion has a garage for tuning your engine, handling, brakes, etc. Having reduced my anti gravity and added split brakes (THIS is essential for the Wipeout feeling!) , the game starts to feel and handle a lot more like Wipeout than it does starting out.
--- end edit ---
I'll probably mute the music eventually and just load up my own playlist in the background. Wipeout music was sometimes good, but it was usually only a couple of songs at best I liked. To each their own though.
If you're really in need of Wipeout, I guess you'll want the Wipeout Omega Collection on the PS4. Would love to see it come to PC, but Gabe Newell has promised to announce Half Life 3 before that happens!
Hopefully this continues to evolve!

About the game:
This game is a slow-paced game, as reflected by the slow story expansions released since 2007 (7 yrs is long time in the gaming world).  It took 7 years to reach Two Towers storyline and it doesn't really have much emphasis on PVP action. It's your traditional quest/crafting MMORPG.
My experience:
I played LOTRO for a fair bit of time. I started off to be F2P but soon realized I just cannot make any reasonable progress after reaching Moria. The most important issue was travelling. It just took too damn long given it's such a big virtual world and especially in Moria area where you can easily drop off cliffs if you're not paying attention. You need premium accounts to unlock many travel points. Without fast travel, you can easily expect watching yourself traveling for 10+mins. It just doesn't make sense for this day and age.
Pros:
- It's Middle-Earth!!
- HUGE world, lots to do and explore
- Friendly community, it's one of the best online gaming community I've met for all the games I've played
- Classes are well balanced
- Crafting system is cool, class system restricts what type of raw materials you can harvest/refine so you're going to have multiple characters for sure in this game
Cons:
- Horrible, sometimes buggy in-game purchase interface. Too slow and often resets.
- Progress is too slow, both in leveling and providing storyline
- Really difficult to complete some quests without a good party
- Traveling is a pain
- Because of travelling cost, quest planning also is a pain because you want to clear all the quests in the same small area
- Mapping system needs to be improved, I like the maps following the literature artwork. But practically speaking, I need to be able to zoom in/out to really see where I need to go!
- Quest grinding, too many of the quests are collect-style quests.
- This game takes TIME
Conclusion:
I only really enjoyed the game when I had the premium subscription. In the long run it's just too much $$ (expect to invest $100+ in the long run). It just isn't a good investment to me, especially recent explosion in F2P games. On the other hand, I can pay Dragon Age $50 upfront knowing I won't need to keep paying to unlock slightly more gameplay.
Therefore, sadly at this current date, I cannot recommend this game unless they overhaul the game mechanics/graphics to provide more action/$ and quality/$. It is getting outdated compared to other MMORPG. One or two yrs ago, I'd recommend this game. If you're rich, then go for it, full premium players enjoys this game a lot more.

SurvHive seriously caught me off guard - until the moment Dread Central's news flash appeared on my Twitter feed, I was totally oblivious to existence of this title. Belgian 1+ (one man operation with additional helping hands) dev team Rocking Hamster announced SurvHive will be multiplayer horror experienced inspired by John Carpenter's The Thing and that was it - there was no other way but to try it.
SurvHive is asymmetric horror experience pitting surviving humans against shapeshifting aliens who thrive on infecting other life forms. The goal's pretty easy - if you're human, survive at all costs. If you're alien, infect/kill them all. At the beginning of every round, all players are informed who they are, but there's no way knowing who are the others players (except little tricks which you'll find out as you play the game). Everyone spawns on random locations throughout the map.  Each player can choose a class which differs in various traits players earn while playing. All these traits are helping with objectives on the map, meaning you can do the objective only if you've mastered a certain trait.
Now, objectives are the horror of it all because they usually pit a large number of people in the same room and that's when paranoia kicks in. There are many different objectives, but almost all of them require players to come close together in the same room.
SurvHive provides its players with supreme feeling of paranoia and dread, even in this Early Access phase. Game is multiplayer only with no bots, so all the games I've played so far had different outcomes because beside the fact everyone's hiding (and preying), people were literally arguing over chat to prove they REALLY ARE THE HUMANS! It fits The Thing niche nicely.
Humans and aliens are distinct in many ways, but in this game one can make you die easily and the other is super cool. Humans have a sanity level which drops with bad decisions and killing fellow humans. As your sanity level drops, you'll start hyperventileting which will let nearby aliens know you're human. Also, aliens go 2001's Alien in this one - when you shed your skin and explode into superior lifeform, you're able to wall climb. I find this feature super fun if you're into human hunt just as much as I am.
Game currently has two maps available. Both maps are wide, very SF inspired, lot of System Shock II hints. Although there are only two, dev is promising more and these two will certainly provide a lot of fun for the players. Graphics are not really the selling point of this game, alongside animations which seem crude, but I've never ended up stuck somewhere or unable to move which is fine. Also, I really don't give a flying ♥♥♥♥ about graphics if the game makes me want to play it over and over again - I'm the dude playing DOOM 2 online. It will certainly get better or it will not, let's just hope the atmosphere and fun stick around. Hit detection is a bit off which can annoy if you're an alien trying to infect a person, but in a strange way it makes preparation of every sneak attack a really complicated feat. Which, as it turns out, is a good thing.
SurvHive is definitely a diamond in the rough and fantastic gaming surprise. It needs a lot of polishing, tweaks to classes and traits, more weapons, better animations, better sounds, more disgusting aliens (YES!), but so far, I've had nothing but GREAT fun playing it. It's shaping to be a great game and it needs more players and bigger input from fanbase because, judging by the first few hours of playing, it delivered more fun than Evolve and Dead By Daylight combined. Sorry, big boys.

Trine 2 is a 2.5D side-scrolling puzzle platformer, featuring 3 very distinct adventurers; Amadeus, the Wizard; Pontius, the Knight; and Zoya, the Thief. Each have different useful abilities, such as the Wizard being able to conjure blocks, or the Thief being able to grapple onto wooden platforms. You'll run from left to right, switching between characters instantly if in Single Player, or in the case of Multiplayer, having up to 3 people in the same game.
The first thing that will strike you, however, is the absolutely stunning visuals. Never have I seen such incredible depth in a side-scrolling platformer. The main game, which slowly progresses through dark forests, to dawn-struck beaches, is certainly something to catch your eye. If you're lucky enough to have the
, you'll traverse through even more dynamic environments such as bleak deserts, eastern-inspired cloud temples, and even through the innards of a large beast!
Trine 2 isn't just a pretty face (thankfully), as it does have some challenging puzzles to solve along the way. You can set how long you want before one of the characters voices a hint, but for most of the time, you'll be able to nut it out. There are generally multiple ways to go through a section, depending on what character you use at the time. Although this doesn't lead to replayability, it does make for some great emergent gameplay.
All in all, a good (and usually cheap!) game to have under your belt as completed, especially for those who love to take a screenshot along the way.

Loving this game! Only about 50% through, I'm guessing, but wanted to post this review for anyone considering purchasing this while it's still on sale. Can't stop playing, and my 360 and PS3 are getting dusty -- and I've got Skyrim, Dragon's Dogma, Dark Souls, Demon Souls, etc., all of which are great but are now on hold!
Pros:
* Well-written story, and location, item, and character descriptions are compelling and not too long or short.
* Turn-based combat, assuming you like that.
* No loading screen more than 3 seconds -- lightning fast, which means area transitions and other activities are never discouraged. This seems like a minor point, but it isn't. It makes the game feel quick and responsive like driving a Porsche (even though the game looks like a Kia).
* Some (although not consistent) decent challenge here on occasions, especially based on what creations you choose to bring with you on your adventure. Strategy is rewarded nicely.
* Love the graphical interface -- almost all information is on the playing screen, which means most (but not all) commands are one mouse-click away.
* Very low computer demands, playable on old machines.
Cons:
* Minimal graphical treats, very basic map and character and monster animations. However, in my opinion, this adds to the charm of the game, and also makes the game easier on the eyes. After a few hours, it becomes the new normal.
* Minimal audio treats, no voice-acting (so far) that I can remember. The audio for combat, door slides, and other events is adequate but limited.
* No cut scenes (so far) that I can remember.
* Interface could be improved by allowing the same key that opens a pop-up menu to close the same menu when pressed again. Other fans have mentioned this but Spiderweb for some reason has resisted making this improvement.
* Would be nice if clicking anywhere on screen other than a pop-up closed the pop-up. Would be nice to have the right mouse button select player character and all creatures, instead of forcing player to find and punch the "0" on the keyboard every time -- a minor but constant irritation.
* Would be nice if the hotkeys were customizable.
Note on how to enjoy:
* Read everything! The material is enjoyable, short, and well written. If you get tired, play something else until you are ready again to read everything. In this game you will create your own mental image and interpretation of the game world, based on what you read, unlike most games in which you will be shown a more explicit graphical representation of everything.
* Don't read a guide, stay away from forums. They're not necessary (so far). Use trial and error. You can save anywhere.
* Don't worry about trying to make the perfect build or to select every optimal decision in dialog choices. Immerse yourself in the world and let consequences just happen. The game is not so tough (so far) that you will get stuck.
* Even if you don't finish this game, or for some reason don't like it much, it should be at least interesting to see what a very small but talented development team can accomplish with limited resources.
Enjoy!

Amicabley described as a "PC game from the early 90's" in its graphical-style and spirit. In general, your only goal is to get stronger by means of earning skill points. Skill points are earned through questions, dungeons and bosses while getting/customizing equipment to improve your efficiency in combat. That being said, this game isn't recommend if this doesn't sound interesting since the game can be easily described as a "grind" for these reasons. While there is multiplayer, it is limited to 2 player co-op with no plans for more. Although having 1 other player is fun in getting to know people, I would have enjoyed the chaos of a larger number of players and factions duking it out.
Outside of these standard activities, it is possible for players to have a minecraft-like experience in building structures. However, the speed at which building can occur is a bit limited due to the complexity of building a "rectangle" at a time at any angle. Overall there's a simple joy in completing quests, distributing skill points and obtaining progressively stronger equipment in a colorful and angled world.

Having been at ground zero when the first Deus Ex was released, I come to this 'review' with many hours devoted to the Deus Ex games and games of this genre in general. First off, Mankind Divided is a great game, worthy of the Deus Ex title and if you are in any doubt about buying this game, don't hesitate.  Ok, it's not going to be a reinvention of the Deus Ex wheel and it's never going to be as good as the original, I doubt any game in this genre ever will and thats why the original still receives plaudits after so many years, it was a masterpiece.  However, DX:MD, is a worthy game that fits with the original games lore perfectly.  It does not thrust the original game protagonists in your face, i.e Joseph Manderly and Bob Page, but the subtle plot lines that run through the games main quest are great and help fill in the blanks the Original game left open.
Graphically, It's a stunning game with loads to explore and find.  The side quests are also great and the pacing is just right.  The soundtrack is also great with many memorable tunes that build the atmosphere.  The Task Force HQ music is a personal favorite and reminds me of a 24 esq Ops room as you wander around hacking computers.
Gameplay mechanics are also great and you have a great feeling of verticality throughout. Almost a nod to other great titles in the genre like Dishonoured.
This game is not as biblical as the original and quite honestly, i'm glad. I've recently started playing Deus Ex again and I still love it.  Will i play this game in 10 years, perhaps i will.  My only gripe with this game and the same can be said for all games in the recent decade is the amount of handholding that takes place.. developers have bowed down to the console generation and games no longer need you to think laterally, people who play these games arent casual gamers, we are devoted and do everything the game has to offer.  You will have plenty of prompts and tips to make sure the thinking and difficulty are at a minimum.  My advice, turn off most of the game play notifications, put the difficulty up slightly and enjoy a Deus Ex game at a difficuly and will leave a lasting memory.
Overall as a guy who has played games for 27 years and was lucky enough to play Deus Ex and Half Life before the hype, I enjoyed this and feel the Eidos team has created something unique and enjoyable.
Cheers

Honestly I think they're all pretty good in their own way, and most of them are pretty cheap too.  Formula Fusion probably has the most detailed graphics but it's an industrial grunge style so it doesn't necessarily look as good as the neon futuristic visuals of Wipeout Omega or the crazy colour of Redout. I backed this game on Kickstarter way back in 2015 and am very pleased with the finished product. If you enjoy the Wipeout games then you'll probably enjoy this too.
There are currently eight tracks and most have a few variant toggles (day/night/reverse/mirror or any combination). There are five craft and five different speed classes, ranging from beginner through to elite. Ships are customisable in their appearance as well as stats. The expected game modes are all present too, such as a standard race, time trials and elimination rounds. There is a single-player campaign as well as online multiplayer, but at the moment there is no split-screen support. More content is expected to arrive over the coming months.
Pros:
- Feels fast and fluid
- Track design is fun and interesting
- Ships look cool
- Great visuals
- Runs well overall
Cons:
- Many of the tracks are set in urban industrial environments, which can make them feel same-y after a while.
- Some minor technical issues that will hopefully be resolved in future patches
- Can be hard to find an online game due to a low playerbase
Verdict:
If you're a fan of anti-gravity racers such as Wipeout, F-Zero or Redout, you're sure to find something to like here.

I’ve only played a couple of hours at this stage, up to level 10.
The storyline and lore was fairly immersive apart from the occasional out of place line of dialogue, the graphics are definitely low budget so don’t expect too much out of it.
As for the gameplay itself, the character that I played had standard WoW style combat with channelled spells, instant casts and a ‘white damage’ melee attack.
Movement and camera control was almost identical to WoW too down to the num lock for auto walk.
I guess that you could say that the learned biases they utilised allowed me to jump right in without much learning, but it also made the experience feel like a cheap independent version of WoW.
In a good free to play model the ‘free’ players are used as tools to drive the in-game economy or gameplay, add value for paying player. For example Valve uses free players in TF2 and Dota2 to drive demand -through trading- for paying players to open chests (See Steam Dev Days for more info). In this respect free players are valuable in both a commercial and community sense.
But as a new player only a few hours in, it feels like free players are not valued at all. From what I've seen, in-game purchases are in your face within the first 10 minutes of play and it just gets worse from there.
In conclusion The Lord of the Rings Online feels like a $5 independent title trying to bleed you dry, with its only redeeming features being the large amount of content. It is also incorrectly labelled free to play, it’s more like a demo for a subscription game with mandatory DLC expansions and pay to win mechanics.

I wrote a review of this mod last night ... but I'd had a few "drinkie-poohs" and it seems I didn't post the original review correctly.  Thus, I have forgotten some of the pithy stuff I'd prepared while it was all fresh in my head.  Sorry.  Review based on what I can remember 24 hours afterward ...
I really enjoyed this mod.  It actually was quite short.  I have no issue with this.  A speedy little adventure.  What I most appreciated were (1) the modifications to the gravity-gun ... a bit of a TF2 twist and (2) another piece of HL2 originality, I think was the use of light/dark and fluoro paint ... which housed another aspect of darkness which I won't clearly mention because it could be a spoiler.
There was sufficient ammo if you're prepared to look for it.  I was happy with the difficulty ... but I'm not sure if I was on Easy or Moderate.
I liked the end-game with striders and Combine.  It seemed to naturally *require* the use of the modified grav-gun.  I feel the whole game was well balanced and I recommend it as a quick jaunt back into the Halflife universe.
The use of Z-key for "decoding" QR codes was, as far as I'm aware, original for HL2 mods too.  There gnome reunification achievement was a challenge.  Use of physics and environment was nicely catered for with a couple of battle scenes.
Play this mod!
**Another couple of mods I'd like to mention...**
I'd like to state too, that there was another HL2 mod that had an original take on a classic weapon/ability.  It may have been "Mistake of Pythagoras" (MoP).  The original take was a "line-of-sight" anti-grav ability.  Come to think of it, it may have been the Z-key for "zoom" instead of a weapon.  It isn't available on Steam as far as I can tell.
might be the best place to get it from.  "MoP" may also be the mod that featured a lot of buildings designed by a classic French architect who may have been famed for use of the "golden ratio" in his designs.
Probably my favourite HL2 mod though was "MINERVA: Metastasis".  Do yourself a favour and give it a go!  It was tight, not buggy, and the most HL2-like of all the mods I'd tried.  Intense in some bits.  8)

It's not the greatest Grand Theft Auto, but it still very well made video game.
Tons of content both for single player and multiplayer.
The story personally I didn't like, was very disappointing that they took the comic direction more than the dramatic one that we loved in "GTA IV".
I don't think it was the greatest Idea to do 3 characters simultaneously, interesting for sure but I had trouble to connect with anyone because of that, one minute you playing Michael and just when you get interested in his life we cut to Trevor's story and then Franklin's, maybe people liked it but I personally didn't think it was the greatest idea.
The graphics are awesome and the map is big and beautiful but not the physics of the game, the car driving is absolute childish and unrealistic (I know it doesn't supposed to be but hell, in GTA IV it was great, yeah it felt you drove a drunk car but at least it had a good racking mechanics and it felt real), here you barely can destroy a car when you crashing it and just standing right beside some people can make them call the cops on you for some reason (what the hell?).
And the most importantly; killing and having a police car chase is really boring, especially when you 5 stars wanted and the cops try to run you over like mad people (I mean... It isn't me who supposed to be the bad one here?).
it's not fun and I stopped doing that after couple hours of playing, which is sad because the main reason people play these games is because it's fun doing that thing.
Online part on the other hand is very troubling subject -
The main problem is the loading screen time... just... my god you waste 70% of your time on these incredible long loading screens for no good reason, just a shame, if it was made technically faster I might have played this for a longer time.
Also the robbery was really disappointing since they were advertising it like the "really big thing of the game", it just ain't... it involves a lot of waiting (again with the loading problem...) and unskippable long cutscenes that really aren't that great in the first place, and if someone f**ks up or dies you wait like 2 minutes to start over, that's just absurd, and I don't have a problem for games to be difficult and hard but here it's just annoyingly bad and awful executed.
I do recommend this game because it was very well made and you can see they put a lot of effort into it, but its still not a very good GTA game in my opinion (funny it comes out from a guy who played it for more than 200 hours but that's only for the achievements in my defence),
if you want a good story and game mechanics you should check the previous titles like GTA IV or Vice City or SA (that I  personally don't like but it's still more fun and holds up more than this one).
Anyway, not that bad but I was still really disappointed when it came out (mainly because of the weak story line), but hell, at least radio rock radio is great! :P

This game is about atmosphere and the stories you come away with. So here's my tale.
I awaken in the sleeping quarters. The ship's computer telling me some kind of alien organism is on board. I scramble out the door, waving a pistol down both ends of the corrider. Seeing nothing I take off running down the metal decks of the ship, my foot steps echoing much louder than I'd like.  I turn a corner and meet with a couple of my crew, Brice and Joe. The three of us know the alien can take on human form, so naturally we point guns in eachother's faces.
The stand off is cut short though as machine gun fire is heard rattling off in the distance. We three immediately lower our guns, an instant truce being formed. We take off sprinintg to see where the gunfire is coming from, and as we spin around a corner we are rooted to the ground at what we see. A frantic marine is pouring round after round into what I can only describe as a 'Thing'. The marine is decimated, the gore covering the bulkheads. The thing whips its terrible head around to us and charges. We open fire. Bullets tear through the charging beast and it drops just short of Brice's trembling feet.
As we take a breather a larger group of 5 crew members shows themselves from a far off corridor. They have no trust of the three of us. Brice approached them and  tried to reason with them, that we need to stick together and that the threat, for now, lay dead. But he's shoved back by a paranoid looking mechanic wielding a make shift flamethrower. He was right to be paranoid. We are led to the canteen of the ship under gun point. Meters from the entrance a horrid scream erupts from beside me. Joe lays dead. Behind him a sickly alien appendage has erupted out of the chest of a member of the other group. One of THEM was infected! The paranoid mechanic's mind breaks, he panics. A torrent of flame washes over alien and human alike. Waves of intense heat firing out in random directions as he tries to burn his fear away.
Brice yells at me to get out of here so I take off running with him. A scientist. and a couple of marines follow along behind us. We regroup in the machine room and it's not long till Brice and I are backing away from the other survivors. The scientist sensing the tension annouced that he's got a way of testing to see if someone is really who they say they are. We all agree to let the doc try it out and take off running for the med lab, our eyes sternly watching eachother as much as the dark corridors around us.
At med lab me and Brice tell the others to stay in the corner while the scientist does his work. One of the marines mentions a sentry gun could be placed covering the only hallway into med lab. Keeping an eye on him me and Brice allow him to set it up. Med lab is locked down and it's only a matter of holding out and waiting for the blood test. A couple of those creatures tried getting down the hall, but between the sentry and our rifles they stood no chance. Things seemed set.
Klaxons started, emergency lights swirled, and the ship's computer calmly announced a fire had started on the bridge. We all panicked, that fire had to be put out. Brice picked up an extinguisher and sprinted out of med lab. No one else followed, so cursing I ran after him to back my friend up, running away from the safe zone. Brice was ahead of me and not slowing down one bit. As I tried to keep up with him the ship's lighting grew dimmer in these sections. I faintly heard the sound of the sentry gun kicking off back in med lab, but I was already committed to my task. Smoke started filling the corridors and with the lack of lighting I started to feel disorientated. I forced myself on, barely keeping track of the twists and turns Brice took as he grew further ahead of me. To hell with the others I thought, me and Brice are the ones risking our lives to put this fire out, we deserve to be the ones to survive. The hanger isn't far from the bridge section anyway, we can do this.
Still running I turned a corner and slowed. At the entrance to the bridge Brice just stood there in the stygian smoke holding the used extinguisher. The computer announced the dangerous state of the bridge had been contained. Excitedly I walked over to Brice and told him we had to go! The fire was out, we can get out of here now! He turned around to me, dropping the extinguisher and said ''I was waiting for us to be alone''.
A slithering jagged mess exploded out of his chest impaling me. I slumped to the cold metal floor. The last sight I had was seeing Brice walking toward the hanger to get in the escape shuttle. Of course I know now, that it wasn't Brice.
SOOOoooo yeah, that's the game. That ended up being much longer than I thought, but fun to write.

First off, this is my first review I have ever done, being a person that tends to hide and not let the world know my opinions, that should show how much I appreciate these games. I have been a long time fan of Spiderweb's games for the last 6 or 7 years, I grew up playing these games, given that they were the demos from the Spiderweb website, but I never got bored of the limited length of them. having seen the 45$ 13 game bundle, I jumped on it. I have already beaten most of these games, and am thrilled to have them all now.
As far as having an opinion of this game, first and foremost you should remember that this is one of their earlier games, and that it is an indie game.
Now for the highlights of the games, though the artstyle might have that dated feel to it, it is a charming and unique style the developers have not strayed too far from, each of their different series have slightly different but similar art stlye, that, while simple, are quite intricate.
The combat is, as others have said, turn based and based on speed stats which can be altered based on skills, items, or gear. The wide variety of companions you can summon makes for a large part of the tactical aspect of the game. You can choose between an average strength army, or a couple strong warrior creatures to assist you. I noticed some people didn't like the game based on all these different areas that have 'monsters so strong you can't beat them' or 'monsters killing me in one hit' but that is the fun of this game, the idea of it is, if you can't win, look for a different path, or try later, or use a different tactic. As long as you don't stick to running in with the same strategy 30 times in a row, dying each time, it shouldn't be too rough.
Now, I might be placing this a little far down the list, but from the get go, you can pick several different characters based on your overall desires of game play, they are all rather diverse and skilled in their own special ways, but as such their skills might cost more or less skill points to learn.
The depth of the story is all narrated in text, which in my opinion, I found to be more in depth then a cutscene, depending on how fast you read, it can be agonizing or delightful, the choices are almost always going to influence people and potentially anger them, or make them approve of you more.
Dispite all my praise I am willing to give the game, no true review would be complete without admitting some flaws with the game (Personal opinion I feel) and so I will list several of the downsides to the game.
First and foremost is, that if you ever learn of the little hidden cheat console you can access, it will remove all the fun of the game if you overuse it, I used it once and managed to clear most of the game in about an hour.
Some of the area's do get rather tough, I will admit, I have managed to get a bit stuck in several areas. But there are generally about 4 or 5 areas you can go to at that time, or quests you can finish. With that said, all you need is a little side trip to finish some and you will manage to gear or level up to reach your needs for that challenging area. It is very easily a frustrating game with it's scaling, but worth every moment.
The noises and sounds, while short and sweet, memorable and appealing, do tend to grate on the nerves after listening to them through the hours of play.
In conclusion, if you have made it this far, you are either an avid reader of reviews, or you are truly interested in this game, and if you haven't purchased it, I would strongly reccommend it, that is, if you enjoy a nice text based turn based rpg with hundreds of choices and many outcomes. This game has a beautiful art style for it's time, and a long well thought out story that I can only imagine took many months to think out and many more to fine tune and decide upon. A truly unique gem to have among your collection.

harkens back to a time when games had higher standards, a time that lived its' last days perhaps a decade ago or so.
When you get this game, you'll see that everything's in there already. Very few modifications or fixes need to be done. This is a stark contrast to the current blockbuster games which attract large numbers of buyers whilst [initially] containing very limited content.
The major curse that has befallen this game is precisely one of numbers. Namely, too few people are playing it. This makes most parties pretty much empty. And yet, the game is still enjoyable enough to be played in a 3v3 scuffle. I see that most buyers have resorted to handing out negative reviews because of that, and this is hardly fair in my book. I have not played the strategy portion of this game, so I will only review the FPS part of it.
Heroes and Generals has the right idea and concept.  Unfortunately, the execution is awful.  Quite simply, Heroes and Generals is an attempt at what could have been a phenomenol game.
Balancing:Unless you play the 'Encounter' mode, you will almost certainly meet enemy vehicles.  The problem is, these vechicles are way too powerful.  Often, you will spend entire matches being sniped by tanks, spawncamped by planes dropping bombs, and getting run over by trucks and motorcycles.  The game is noticably tipped in a sniper's favor, with subpar graphics (will be discussed later) making it difficult to spot any enemy at all. 2/10
Graphics:The graphics, are, to say the least, mediocore at best.  No matter what graphic setting you are at, objects in the distance will shimmer, plants appear 2D and flat, and lighting is often off.  This is the result of the developers deciding to build their own graphics engine, which shows an admirable effort, however, the efforts have not paid off.  Call of Duty 2 from 2007 in my opinion, has comparable or better graphics than this game. 6/10
Gameplay:Heroes and Generals features massive maps, which, while can at times provide an amazing time, is also a cause for bitter disappointment.  You will often spend long times running to a faraway objective, only to be shot by a sniper you did not know even was there.  However, large maps often make for large and exciting battles, so this can go both ways.  Spawn protection is mediocore.  There is noting protecting you in the spawn except for an invisibliliy shield that is turned off as soon as you walk into the 'combat area', making you easy pickings for spawncampers.  Gunplay is horrible.  The gun mechanics feel clunky, and the game uses a health bar system, making the player with the more expensive and therefore superior weapon almost certain to come out on top in a firefight.  Movement in this game is good.  The movement is easy to get used to.  The physics are horrilbe.  Planes do not stall, ragdoll physics are implemented for infantry, tank turrets rotate too fast, bicycles turn themselves upright, etc. I have not yet experienced issues with lag, only being put into high ping matches.  You will often join a battle that ends 2 minutes later, which is not too big of a deal, but is very annoying when you just want a match quickly.  The sounds in game are very nice, with realistic gun sounds, and the ability to hear other player's footsteps is a nice touch.  The animations are smooth and nicely done.  6/10
Economy:Heroes and Generals will force you to buy better guns and upgrade them.  In additon to this, you must 'maintain' all of your weapons using in-game currency.  You unlock better equipment through the use of ribbons, which, unless you are willing to pay for premium accounts or buy in-game currency, will quickly turn into an insufferable and agonizing grind.  In short, it is the player who has money to spend on the game that can buy all the best equipment and win.  Heroes and Generals is most certainly, a pay to win game. 1/10
Developers:The game has subpar developers.  Often, the community will ask for features that take years to be implemented or do not get implemented at all.  They have designed an economy system that is designed for unreasonable amounts of money to be spent on the game, although, they DO have to pay themselves somehow.  However, the pay to win aspect of this game is utimately what has ruined the game for me, making it more of a chore rather than a pasttime.  The developers are also very slow to implement bug fixes. 6/10
Optimization:Horrible.  The game takes more resources than Battlefield 1 to run.  I have a GTX 1050Ti, a rather capable graphics card.  I have above the recomended specs, yet I will often get massive frame drops.  Sometimes it will go as bad from 80fps to 30fps. 5/10
Community:The playerbase is okay, with many people willing to help and explain aspects of the game to you.  However, teamwork in most matches is nonexistent, and there is a fairly large population of 'trolls', who will teabag you as well as sending you caustic messages through the feature of naming guns.  However, much of the playerbase remains mature. (most of the time)
(you will see the name of the gun when a person kills you with it).  7/10
Overall:Heroes and Generals is great if you want a World War II themed arcade shooter with little to none historical accuracy.  One or two matches can be very fun, but you will quickly realize that the game is just a subpar game that you have to put many hours into the actually somewhat enjoy.  If not for its flaws, then Heroes and Generals might have been a great game, with massive battles with lots of players.  Keep playing it if you enjoy it, take a risk and get if you want, but as for me, it has not been a stellar experience playing this game.

I am one of those people that look at a free game and don't expect to be able to be given an experience equal to a game that you pay money for. I see a lot of people calling the devs incompetent, who must all be very succesful developers with a laundry list of succesful games with active communities. You've played this game, some for 100s of hours, clearly they did something right. To pretend that you know more about how the game SHOULD, only being able to view the game from the perspective of a player is ridiculous.
People who contribute to keep the developers in business are going to recieve benefits, the only thing that even makes sense to give people in a game like this, will most likely give them an advantage, this is a World War II FPS, they're not gonna give you shiny skins or loot boxes.
I appreciate this game for the older weaponry which is less powerful giving your avarage soldier a longer lifetime on the field. There's much more strategy in positioning and moving throughout the level.
There are problems and things that are aggrevating, even as the best player you find things to blame when you're not doing well, valid or not.
Also I see a lot of mention of the grindy aspect, which I for one appreciate. It's called actually having to put in the work to acquire better gear. And it forces players to specialize in a certain playstyle, letting them fit into a certain role.
If you can play a match and just be happy with how you did on a personal level, understanding that there will be a difference between people who pay or put in thousands of hours and you and just focus on the fact that no matter how you do in match, you're still progressing in the game, which, because of how long it takes, instantly is more valueable than a game who gives you everything after playing it for half an hour.

3089 Is a FPS with mixxed RPG elements in a randomly generated open world. You Collect Gear and weapons, manage your inventory, heath and energy. Your main objective is to impress the overlord into thinking your a model worthy of mass production. In your journey you are aided by underground Organic Brains that are plotting to retake the surface through manipulating you.
The controlls are standard for many fps / rpg players, wasd left / right mouse.
Graphics are colorful and well eneuph not to take from the experience. No notable errors or tears.
Game is very stable in both single player and Co-op play.
Gameplay is simple but fun. You have a indicator to let you know how close to or if you are discovered by the enemy. Once an enemy detects you they go strait for you and randomly strafe while firing on you. Enemy are on land in are and by sea. They can follow you for a very long time if they maintain sight, or they lose interest quickly if you duck behind cover. There is some vehicles like hover boards and planes.
An rpg system that caters to the players skill level. Skill points as quest rewards with several different skills to choose from. Melee and Range weapon combat. If you're having a hard time progressing just do a few quests in a lower level area. It punishes you for dying and rewards you very well for your efforts. Dying removes a random item from your inventory.
There is a plot that sets the game and gives you an idea of whats going on. The story quests lead you through the games progression which ended for me when i was gear level 25. I killed the story mobs in 2 hits at this point. The game claims to have multiple endings, the 2 endings i know of left me feeling like there was no arc, pinnacle or final boss to overcome.
All things considered, The enjoyment and Value is definitly there.
9 out of 10.

If you're getting turned off by the graphics, you're going to miss out on a great game!
Like most people, the first time I saw this game, my initial thoughts was - "cute game... very retro, 1980s style but crap graphics by today's standards". I doubted it was any good. I mean.. RPG? Sandbox free roam? With graphics like that? Gotta be kidding me! (yup, usual pre-conceived notions about a game just by "first looks").
Beneath the "blocky and pixellated graphics" lies a free-roam world, where you can explore and try stuff on your own. You can follow the main quest, or not. You can take sidequests, or not. Beneath this simple blocky world lie a hidden world of depth and exploration. Crafting is very simple... you find stuff, put them together...You break apart stuff, you put other parts together and see what you get. The items are in very discrete units - body, handle, barrel etc etc... but the combinations you put together buffs or debuffs you. This is so unlike other usual more "mainstream RPG" where you have to find "ingredients" and "materials" to craft, for example. You waste a lot of time just getting 20 ores and 50 wood just to make that cool gun or armour, or 2 roses 3 leaves and 1 root to make that potion.
The premise of the game is simple - you are a robot, dropped onto the planet Xax for a "final evaluation". Then, you are left on your own with only 1 suggestion - "Do quests". That's it. From here on it's up to you to follow the main quest or just do your own stuff.
While this game might present itself as an "FPS", it is anything but. Imagine this as a blocky version of Borderlands, You can play it like an FPS but you'd get better mileage out of it if you play it as an RPG.

Going into MegaTagmension (MT) as a newcomer to the Neptunia series, I was thinking that I would be playing some sort of visual novel with hyper-sexualized content under a metaphorical cloak of story progression. Or maybe something with such prolific fan service that I'd have to worry about someone walking in through the door. Little did I know that I was getting myself thrust into a world bathed in 14 different flavors of cuteness. Maybe I've been playing way too many outlandish anime games, but this VN fused with action elements managed to show such a refreshing sense of originality and style that I couldn't help but swoon at its characters. At its core, MT is a fully voiced VN with a little bit of beat em up/hack & slash thrown in, not too dissimilar to the Dynasty Warriors/Musou series. These battle sequences are relatively short and aim to enhance the story's sense of credibility, but ultimately plays a backseat role in expanding Idea Factory’s Neptunia universe.
In this newest release, a small band of girls who seemingly represent their entire academic population are uniting to save their school, Gamicademi, from closing down. In the opening scene, Blanc overhears her sisters being attacked by ghoulish zombies. To her surprise, the zombies are actually actors cast by Neptune in an effort to create a high profile movie with the hopes that it'll be the school's saving grace. Naturally, Blanc decides to join in on the fun and direct the movie herself; however, in a rather ludicrous turn of events real zombies end up getting involved, even if they are neglected between shoots. It is now up to these heavily equipped Powerpuffs to make sure Gamicademi lives to see its grand return to the spotlight.
Now saving Gamicademi may be of the utmost importance to Blanc, but some part of me did not allow myself to proceed without first changing all of the girls' outfits to their torn counterparts… Moving on, I began to notice important personalization options other than cute costumes and accessories. Japanese and English voice options are available, to my surprise, helping me solidify my stance to support the original dubbing. For the non-purists out there, the English VAs are actually much better than the average folk employed in domestic dubs, and I even found it to be less cringy and sensual than usual. Either way, I definitely liked the ability to pick audio languages, and feel a need to commend whoever was responsible for that decision. Delving further, MT also lets players have a choice in who they cast for each scene event or fight. This ends up creating "alternate cuts" depending on who you cast, as the resulting scene's dialogue and special events system follow your decisions to an extent. This responsibility puts you in Blanc's shoes, creating the story direction of your choosing in a much more immersive manner.
Regarding MT's Warriors/Musou-like combat system, various aspects regarding its design makes it to be the weakest mechanic of the game. Really poor camera tracking impedes fluid movement and makes positioning more difficult than it should be. Worse is when there is a boss around that can fly and perform diving maneuvers, compounding to create a slightly debilitating combat experience. Furthermore, most of these battle sequences will be completed within a handful of minutes, requiring very little variability to overcome. As the game progresses, combat ever so slowly feels like tedious exercises in mindless button mashing. It’s a big shame since advanced maneuvers are incorporated, such as taking advantage of animation cancelling, invincibility frames, or aerial combo strings for evasion, but they aren’t necessary at all to beat the game. MT's tag-team mechanics, plentiful amount of unlockable combos, and visually appealing SP/EXE Drive skills help make up for the combat's grievances and keep these portions slightly enjoyable, just much less than ideal.
MT’s combat oriented multiplayer aspect seems to be the game’s biggest wow-factor when comparing it to other Nep titles, as MT is the only game so far to contain such a system. The ability to group up with 3 other players online in a mode featuring new enemies, bosses, arenas, and VN events not seen in the campaign, add major play value. There are tons of quests separated by Star difficulty, providing rewards and experience to level up character stats that carry over to the story mode. Also, unlike story mode, the multiplayer aspect unlocks every character and transformation from the beginning for use, along with changing some of the combat controls to incorporate online player joint attacks. Strangely, I found the multiplayer mode really enjoyable, even while playing solo along with the fact that the multiplayer combat system is the same as the story mode’s system. It’s most likely attributed to the lengthier and tougher quest challenges, unimpeded by tiny segments of dialogue. Unfortunately, MT’s multiplayer mode seems to have been plagued with connection issues for many players ever since launch, but since I haven’t seen any such problems myself, the only experience I have in multiplayer is a fairly positive one.

Although the story was a bit absurd, it seems to be what defines the style of the Neptunia games. Plenty of funny jabs at the girls’ own ridiculous situations closely flirt around breaking the fourth wall creating a neat sense of relatability, and Blanc’s “extortion” scheme in obtaining MagiGirl Idol’s support is comically hilarious. What started off strong ended up petering out throughout the second half of the game, as the story essentially kept walking around in circles without introducing any real major changes. A new character here or there with a backstory blended in with something zombie related is the extent of MT’s narrative. It’s a bit of a shame since the game is much shorter than its RPG sister titles; so stretching MT’s story thin is pretty problematic. Worse is the alternating nature of the VN and battle sequences. When you get involved with the VN’s story, you’re forced to fight 2 minute battles, just to watch a 2 minute dialogue and repeat the process (up to four or five times in one scene with multiple loading screens for each transition). It’s hard to get attached to either aspect when the game switches gears so often.
Regardless, as a casual fan of anime and visual novels, I didn't find the newest installment in the Neptunia series too eccentric to take in, or alienating as an entry point. There weren't too many inside jokes or references, and the iconic song and dance summarizing previous important world aspects is present. After wrapping things up with Blanc and friends, I still found myself wanting to delve more into their world, especially as I only seemed to have observed them in such a confined environment. If you are a long-time Neptunia fan, I’m afraid that my verdict may not be very enlightening or relatable from my perspective. Just know that MT is much, much, shorter than the main series games. But for those that are weary of this as an entry point into the series, I can say that MT seemed to be rather welcoming, and is definitely enjoyable as a VN experience all on its own. There is a desire for improvements in the combat realm, but the multiplayer and VN aspects proved to be commendable enough to make checking out MT, or at least other Neptunia games, rewarding, especially during one of Idea Factory’s deep publisher sales.

State of the Game July 2017
Performance
The game performs well on hardware that was popular at the time of release, it's entirely possible to maintain 60fps with very reasonable graphics options if you avoid some of the GPU hogs. The Audio engine contains bugs that cause the GTA to crash on a wide range of hardware due to discrepancies in settings, some Audio hardware allows for high bit-rates, GTA runs at 16 Bit 44.1KHz. Higher settings will make the game crash after some arbitrary amount of time.
Options
Many, only notably lacking direct support for extended mouse buttons, which have to be configured by mapping to keys in some instances.
Relevance & DLC
GTA V has remained semi-relevant with help from its online multi-player updates, some have been excellent, some interim fluff. Notably story mode has been neglected with the exception of adding a few cars here and there.
Overall Game-play
The mechanics and physics are excellent when they work, often humorous when they don't. Lag between players can cause a host of physics anomalies especially with traffic, something dedicated servers would help fix.
PvP
With the latest update comes in my opinion the death of PvP in GTAO, Explosive rounds have positively affected the ability to get rid of Hydra Trolls, but also transformed how cancerous players now spread around their play style. There's little to no skill in a normal gun vs thermal scope and explosive rounds battle. An alternative could have been airborne Merryweather strike called in by phone with the precision of the jet that attacks by the airport. GTAO Lacks any credible ranking system, or ability to enter sessions with rules sets such as disabling near blips, if tracking people down meant completing objectives for brief intel on peoples activites vs simply looking at the map & throwing explosives at them during PvP missions, the activites would perhaps be more satisfying for all parties involved
Exploits, netcode and controversies
The Achilles Heel of GTAO. There are few that will tell a truthful story about the modding scene as it relates to GTA. In essence the netcode is essentially born of a lan game further developed from how it was in GTA IV that now routes player actions through a server acting essentially as a router to hide actual IP addresses and coordinate basic session duties. There is still no in-session detection of exploits, only RockStar's feeble attempts to scan the many stats they collect combined with reports that can be cleared/blocked. And a system that attempts to scan memory for known exploit code. Yet with each update the hacks return in just a few days. Many who blindly support modding, leaving negative reviews on all Rockstar's games will state that TakeTwo's action against OpenIV was wrong. Supporters of the OpenIV community who have developed software to catalogue game assets and function hooks fail to understand that this knowledge is a large contributing factor in the creation of the mods by less responsible developers subsequently used for creating an unfair advantage in PvP, or generally being abrasive. Thus what we really have is an awkward situation for Rockstar. We have OpenIV who don't make software that affects online play, and we have people who build on that work to be asses. Resulting in people who actually play rarely playing in open sessions with random people, this further amplifies the remaining pool of lavatory waste in the remaining open sessions who actively want to be in open sessions to cause chaos. Having said that, I'm not against the modding scene, if GTAO had a place, or specific sessions modders could do what they wanted, I'd welcome that. Combined with better team building tools (max members <100? team chat when not in session, team events, team session settings, in-team factions/gangs.
Lastly, perhaps the worst of the modders are not those who blow people up without engaging and attach eggs to your head, but those who subtly add a small amount of weapon damage, regenerative health, or targeting / bounding box aids to give skill-free advantages.
PvE
The standard cash grinding missions while plentiful at launch have been neglected in favor of multi-player missions, that still offer little cash reward but offer some entertainment value.
Recommended? yes definitely… play with friends.

Performance issues are a major, serious problem with this game. I can max settings very comfortably in time trial mode - race against other people and the frame rate fluctuates so violently that it becomes more or less unplayable, regardless of how powerful your rig is. Handling is dissatisfying compared with the original Wipeout/2097 games, and the tracks are constructed in such a way that the game does NOT recapture the amazing feeling of having threaded your craft through the eye of a needle whilst barely lifting from the throttle. The game feels bland and uninspiring. If you have not played the original Wipeout series, have a go with this, it will provide some novelty value but I have to agree with other people that this feels incomplete and my feeling is this probably qualifies as a 50%-off sale purchase. One other word of warning - I had to reinstall and whitelist after my AV wrongly identified the .exe patch update as IDP.generic malware - was quarantined and could not be restored. The patch made NO discernable difference to performance - frame rate frequently falls through the floor on a rig that will comfortably run 2015-2017 AAA titles at high/ultra settings.

Sadly game is broken framerate wise (even after patch) and gameplay decisions make it simply fun.  Let me know when you fundamentally fix this unfinished game and I may relook.  In truth the only reason is I am not demanding my money  back, is because I believe you can fix it all and 6 months away you will have a really good game.
Ok firstly I have a really meaty PC .. i7-6700 3.4GHz with NVIDIA GeForce GTX 1060 6GB.
The system runs every game I have thrown at it APART from this one.
Now I am not a frame or res junkie...I am all about the gameplay for me.. But I have tried this game on several lower resolutions and it is still stuttering all over the place mid race... Now this isn't the kind of stutter that makes you say oh  well thats a shame.. but the kind that makes you crash horrifically into a wall ending your chances of any hope of doing well in the game.
Ok .. so right now the above in my mind makes this game still unplayable and shouldn't have been released in my opinion.. but I expect it will get solved by the R8 team soon.  So I am not too worried right now about that.
My far bigger concern is the fundamentals of the gameplay.  Now I am a huge fan of the WipEout series, so I am fully aware how hardcore the series has always been.  But you should always have a chance of coming in the top 5.  This game demands the perfect race to even achieve that.  Having where you have to start a race simply because you didn't do the perfect line through a corner as the computer controlled craft always do is simply not fun to me.  This game need more human like AI, that do make mistakes to give us mere humans a fighting chance.
The other concerns are the weapons... damn they are dull and unimaginative and do little to really affect the game in any way... In a lot of ways they are almost a waste of time, especially as you need to contantly run over power ups to have any hope of being a race contender.
Also the tracks layout could do with some rethinks (actually WipEout series has always has this criticism  for me)...I think a lot could be learned Yu Suzuki and how he only had certain angles on the track in Out Run 2 because crashing isn't fun for the player.   A smoothed out, less punishing track design in places on certain corners would make a massive difference.
Ok a lot of negativity there... Good points of the game.. The tracks look wise are simply gorgeous, the music is great.. the craft design is also nice/
In summary this game has a lot of potential... But you can see that its been rushed out with out proper testing on PC to make money.. But I guess this is because R8 will simply concentrate on getting this to work on the consoles and they treated this as a money boost for them.    Still fix the frame rate issues (Still fundamentally broken despite what you say)  and give less hard core modes with easier AI to beat and this could be fun.   Right now though (as muchas it breaks my heart to says so) I would advise people against this game sadly.

So first off this game visually is gorgeous. Exactly what I was looking for and expecting in that regard. Soundtrack is repetitive but still solid. My largest complaint has to be the mechanics surrounding how your racer responds to impact with the walls. It is extremely unforgiving, a slight rub generally results in a speed reduction of 30% or more. Really any contact at all causes your racer to catch and lose significant amounts of momentum. This makes facing off against the COMs (who never hit walls and almost always hit boost) in career incredibly challenging. I understand the game may take some time to master and I understand assigning the higher classes a less forgiving mechanic for wall impacts but as it is now it is very hard to pick up the game and enjoy it. Instead you race again and again to consistently place between last and 3rd to last. To me this game would be fantastic if the impacts to walls were adjusted to have less impact on the speed of the racer, say between 5-8% for rubbing and 10-15% for higher angle imapcts. As it is sits now, I find it very discouraging to play despite visually being a grandslam. An update to this wall/racer mechanic, especially on the lower classes would for sure push me to recommend.

I wanted to love this game, but only ended up just liking it. While not a bad game, "Mankind Divided" stands as the worst in an otherwise amazing series.
+ Visually, MD looks fantastic.
+ Hacking is still a blast
+ More opportunity for stealth play
- The world isn't nearly as varied and "alive" as HR; The subway system of travel actually makes the world feel much smaller too.
- The new augs are bland.
- The story feels way too short and boring thanks to a lackluster story and single generic, one note villain.
- Most of the NPCs and their subplots are forgetable.
- Most levels are well designed, but some feel far too redundant and generic.
- The new voice for David Sarif is just, well, terrible.
- There are no emotional stakes.
- Jensen's new supporting cast stinks.
- Some of those new stealth opportunities feel tacked on.
- The final boss is WAY too easy. Repeatedly snipe him from an air duct and he's toast.
Overall, MD feels like a decent entry in the series, but doesn't nearly push the franchise in a new direction. Even the more polarizing IW raised the bar and changed up the game. MD does very little to push the narrative; We are no closer to 2000's original than we were with the last game.
HR was a bouncy love letter to Robocop. Unfortunately, MD is a fairly humorless and soulless entry that just kinda sits there. MD scratches that "Deus Ex" itch, but doesn't nearly add enough to the franchise to be considered a must have. At best, it feels like more of the same - HR 1.5. At worst, Mankind Divided feels phoned in and forgettable.
Mankind Divided is a C+ game in an A+ wrapper. Dissapointing. Buy it, but only if it's on sale.

I expected about 20 - 30 hours more out of this game. I was sadly dissapointed.
Reader beware, spoilers follow here:
MY BACKSTORY:
I am a massive fan of the Deus Ex games and have played all of them. Continuing from the success of Human Revolution, I could not wait for this game.
SIDE MISSIONS:
The game started of good. A few graphics issues that was patched quickly and did not really bother me as I was more into the story line and side missions. I started playing the side missions and REALLY enjoyed it. The side missions are this games strong point. I felt that there was an insane amount of detail put into the side missions, perhaps a lot more than the main missions. When I started playing the game, I ended up so far invested into one side mission that I played almost 10 hours to complete the one side mission because it was really fun and immersive. The attention to detail in the side missions are really what makes this game, and also points of interest that you randomly encounter. You break into someone's apartment, hack their computer, read their emails and all of a sudden you feel like you can realte to the person, you feel like you want to help the person and before you know it, you are hours into a trail you are following because you are just interested. That I really enjoyed.
MAIN MISSIONS:
There were a couple of good main missions, and by a couple a mean literally only a few, however, it was over way too fast. On the loading screens, you keep seeing images of awesome looking places like the city built by the augmented and another one of a facility built inside of the ocean. A lot of cool places that you never get to see or play. I couldnt wait to go to the city built by augs, however you only get to see the aug slums city. You also hear about a facility in Switzerland where it seems that Megan, your ex, apparently works and it seems she is part of the group who created the "orchid". So I thought to myself, cool, Ill probably end up there some time later to shut the production of this weapon down. Nope, wrong, you never even go there. Then, when you use the augmented reality chair in Millers Office, you see the Chinese Billionare who is actually responsible for the killing of Talos Rucker. So you never get to fight him and you never even go to Hong Kong ?! You bascially go to prague and then you go to the slums right outside of prague and then you go to london for your first boss fight and then the games over.
To be honest, it feels wrong giving this game a bad rating because I am a big fan of Deus Ex and I really liked some aspects of this game, however, I expected at least another 20 hours of gameplay where you actually find out the rest of the story line. You are left with so many untold narratives leaving the player completely confused. When I saw the credits rolling I was shocked and was very dissapointed. To be honest, when I was fighting the only boss, I was thinking to myself, cool, when I kill him I'm probably going to head back to prague and then have a mission debrief and then try to track down the chinese billionare responsible for this. I thought that me, Alex and Janus were going to work as a team to track the rest of the "bad" guys down and put an end to them. Nope, apparently not. I am really dissapointed in the lack of storyline in this game.
A LITTLE BIT OF CREDIT:
I must give ferral interactive credit for making a pretty good linux port, I guess thats one good thing that came out of this. The graphics is amazing, especially the faces, and once they patched the issues, it performed pretty good. The attention to detail on the side missions was the best I have ever seen in any other game I have played.
TL;DR (Spoilers)
The side missions are great and practicly make this game. The main storyline is great and has a lot of potential, however it ends abruptly, with only a few main missions, leaving the player confused with tons upon tons of unanswered questions and untold storyline. Only a single boss fight. The only reason I have 43.2 hours on record is because of the side missions. I guess only about 15 hours of that was spent playing the main missions.
