Revisited review after the latest update.
Formula fusion is a very, very long running project(several years ago it was suppose to be futuristic formula one racing, judging by the design back then) made by a small team of 12 people. It takes no rocket scientist to tell the goal here was to make a worthy successor to Wipeout HD and thus Wipeout, which equals putting the bar astronomically high. The project has been halted for a while due to the budget running thin, but got back on track after an investor provided the necessary funds. So here we are.
Is Formula Fusion as good as Wipeout HD? No. Definitely not. Is Formula Fusion worth a purchase? I would say yes, even though not my most convincing recommendation. If you have never played any anti grav racers it's definitely worth the purchase due to it's refreshing nature - if you can relativize it with previous contributers to the genre it might be a bit pale in comparison.
So what does Formula Fusion do well?
>It looks good
>The ship design is top notch
>Visually, the maps are nice
>Plenty of customization options, which aren't fully fleshed out yet
>Menus are nice, since the newest update
>Visually it very much looks like Wipeout HD

I had an EA review up here but am doing another one for full launch-

Ever since I sold my PS3, I've always missed Wipeout. But, I can safely say, it has not gone anywhere.. Or at least, the developers.
In it's current state, it's Early Access and some people in the reviews seem to forget that, reviewing it unfairly. At the time of writing this, I have 20 minutes game-time, so take this review how you will. Obvioulsy, it's nowhere near a complete game, so I will not be judging it as one. The controls are pretty solid so far. I noticed that the air brakes are pretty harsh, and even a quick tap can slow you down more than intended. If anyone remembers on Wipeout HD, air-brake sensitivity WAS an actual mechanic. While it doesn't look to be implemented (yet), I wouldn't doubt that it soon will be, making it much better getting in some clean laps.
I read that people thought the tracks were a little 'tight/narrow' which I could somewhat agree with. I did also read though that the developers are addressing that. So, maybe we'll see some slightly wider tracks in the next build. The 4 tracks that I played were really fun. I really felt like I was playing Wipeout again. HOWEVER, if you're looking for insane elements in tracks, I don't think they've really pushed the boundries as well as they could on some of them. (I did just try the first 4, so maybe they're more 'beginner friendly' tracks?) There's still enough razor sharp turns for anyone that likes quick reflex racing. The ship selection is interesting. From what I could tell, the model for all the factions is more/less the same, but with different paintjobs. I highly believe that will change at a later date.
As far as the stuff that doesn't affect game play at all. The menu is pretty simple and easy to navigate (but still has a pretty cool futuristic feel to it though). The music is rippin! I love the music. Wipeout always had stellar soundtracks, and this is soundtrack does not dissappoint.. Graphics are rad and one track had a pretty sweet rain wheater going.
For a game still in very early stages of development, it's fun. Simple as that. In a time where it's raining 'early access games', it's easy to forget THAT THEY'RE STILL IN DEVELOPMENT. Some people would be happier than a MF'er to tell you Redout is a better game, and the correct answer to that is; They're two different games in different stages of development. One is mindnumbingly chaotic and one is a little more smooth. Neither is a better game than the other. Remember to enjoy them both. AG Racing is a very niche style and they don't come often. So just enjoy both as seperate games that are there to offer us entertainment.

Trine 2 is a 2-D puzzle platform game. Unlike games like Braid and Vessel, there are multiple ways to solve each puzzle. Overall it is a lot of fun, there is a good mix of thoughtful puzzle solving and fast-twitch action and platform jumping. There are three characters with different abilities. Most puzzles are obviously designed for one character, but in a lot of cases you can solve them with multiple characters. It is fun to figure out the "knight" solution to a "wizard" puzzle. Also, there are additional challenges in addition to progressing through the game: experience pickups and chests. You can win extra achievements by getting all the experience pickups and chests for a level. There is a decent amount of replayability, although I had enough playing it through once. There are an obscene number of achievements available for this game, overkill if you ask me. There is a lot of content here, I have played ~19 hours so far without going back to replay any of the levels to pick up more achievements. The background graphics are very pretty and imaginative, althoug they obscure things sometimes. Overall I can recommend this game as a fun 2-D puzzle platform game, with a low price and tons of content.

Mortal Kombat X is a superb game. As a versus fighter it's far ahead of its predecessor MK9, and it feels very much like a modern fighter. When you play MKX you'll be tempted to think that this game will age very well.
MKX has lots of strengths.
It has solid gameplay mechanics, solid enough to be featured in EVO. Traditionally gameplay has often been a problem for MK games, but not MKX. Behind the blood, gore, and over-the-top action there is actually a very good fighting game here.
It has a ginormous cast of playable characters, 100 to be precise (including DLCs). Thanks to the new variation system. This makes it very hard to get bored with the game, as there are always more characters to explore and learn.
The graphics is jaw-dropping. Period.
The story mode is short but interesting. Most other fighting games don't even feature a story mode.
The online play wasn't very good when the game came out but the Oct '16 patch fixed that. It's quite good now.
The difference between good and great is often in the details. MKX definitely shines in the details.
If you were ever a fan of MK then this is it. MKX is the ultimate MK game that the devs always promised but never before delivered. Just hop in and have a blast.

This is, without a doubt, one of the best video games I've ever played (and I've been playing since the SNES came out). It's a short puzzle game that won't take long to finish. I highly recommend blotting out the world and playing the whole game in one sitting (be careful not to be spoiled!). It'll only take a few hours, but it's absolutely worth it for the emotional rollercoaster you'll have undertaken.
The game starts out simple and sweet with a fairly cliché premise. As you learn the controls (and it's highly recommended that you use a controller), the game progresses both in complexity and story. The characters, whose names you never learn, grow on you and the way you work the controls as well as the style of the game does much the same. The graphic are pretty breathtaking with views beautiful enough to wish you were there to sit on a bench and watch for hours. ♥
The puzzles themselves are neat, if fairly simple, but it's the ingenuity and creativity behind them that's compelling. Along the way you meet several loveable characters and there's a bit of humor and unexpected darkness that'll have you drawing back in surprise. I really can't recommend this game highly enough. It's worth the price and is decidedly affordable.
Note: Yeah, I know, it looks like I haven't played much of it. I played it offline, so Steam wasn't able to record my play-time on it. If you check my page, I have all the achievements for the game. Even aside from that, I originally purchased and beat the game years ago on both of my consoles. It's just good enough to play again and again. So get to it! : )

My Nomiation for The “I'm Not Crying, There's Something In My Eye” Award.
Played it with a friend. She cried her heart out.

1. This is a walking sim but you get to control two players at once so it is kind of two games in one. What a bargain!
2. The single player "co-op" is a gimmick and adds little to experience. There are times when it makes sense to control both characters at once and there are times when it makes sense to control them one at a time. Forcing you to do both always is an annoying mechanic at best, adding no challenge and occasionally some frustration. Sorry you had to hear it from me.
3. (If you want to see this mechanic done in such a way it actually adds to gameplay, check out
by Cabygon Software. That is some mind bending business right there.)
4. People will say this game has puzzle elements but the puzzles are along the lines of: "There is crank right there. Bet you can't guess what you have to do next!"
5. This is not really about gameplay but atmosphere and storytelling so 2 and 3 are kind of immaterial in a sense but still worth mentioning.
6. This is set in sort of a high fantasy setting with tutor houses and trolls and things like that. Good times. This is not a super technically intense game graphically but it is still very pretty.
7. Sound works well enough. Soundtrack is mostly atmospheric and I felt like it could use something a bit more punchy from time to time. That is just me though. Thing is, I'm right.
8. The characters speak in either gibberish or Norwegian or something. It is all the same to me, not gonna lie.
9. Despite what you may have heard, there is not much of a story here. A father falls ill. His sons go off to get him medicine. Adventure ensues. Characters become more mature. Not exactly Pulitzer material. Again, I'm sorry you had to hear it from me.
10. Going back to controls, there are parts where you've got to hold down the shoulder buttons for way too long and it makes my tiny, baby hands cramp up. Maybe I just need to gym more often... Or maybe they should have made it so you don't need to hold down the shoulder buttons the entire time you are clinging to a ledge.
11. There are two things I'd consider boss battles in this and only one of them was remotely challenging. The other one was more dramatic from a storytelling perspective. I feel like we could have had both elements twice but maybe I ask too much.
12. For the duration of the game, I could not help but to thinkg: I hope my sons are smart enough not to go risking their dumb butts to save my old, decaying self.
13. Who has two thumbs and recommends a game even though he seem only to have negative things to say about it? *Points thumbs at self* THIS GUY!

For those who say the keyboard controls don't work: There are a few keys that are different from what's listed in the manual. For the F1-12 keys, you have to hold the fn button while you press them. LIkewise, press alt + a to toggle animation (in an ambush on multiple warships or when evading multiple depth charges, the animation will quickly ♥♥♥♥ with your program, so.) and alt +s to toggle slow speed/save game. As far as I can tell all other keys work as described in the manual. The full manual is available here but even if it weren't, you can find the PDF online.
Another tip: at the startup screen, choose NO joystick and NO digitized speech. According to an old forum post I found that was written years ago, there's some line of code that makes the digitized speech come out like unintelligible buzzing. Or, if you're literate in that sort of thing, you could go tweak the code and report back here how you did it. :D

A pretty solid life simulator. I guess i'll just jump into the pros and cons. I have nothing witty to say here...

Almost infinite gameplay

Most of the better content is in DLC.
The game crashes every couple hours if you dont have the most amazing computer.
DLC is expensive as hell, id reccomend only buying dlc during a sale when its like, 5-10 bucks.
Bridgeport (city added in late night dlc) has horrible framerate.
Load times are slow, and adding a minigame to do while waiting makes them 10x slower.

I had to start skipping the story mid game, because the battles can be really short. You're sometimes faced with 3 minutes of story, literally 30 seconds of gameplay, then another minute of story, then starting a new mission you may get even more story before you get more game play. If the battles were longer, this may not have been such an issue.
Megatagmension has very little challenge if you learn to use all of the controls. Once I started blocking, and sticking with one character I flew through the game. A lot of the missions you will beat in 10seconds-1minute
A large part of the game are the multiplayer missions, which you can start at any time, at any level. The multiplayer missions end up significantly harder than the end boss of the story mode. During my play time, players couldn't connect to me, and I couldn't connect to others, it is/was a wide spread issue. You may have to plan on playing the multiplayer missions solo. I was able to beat all the multiplayer missions on my own, and think it might be more fun that way, it's just not challenging enough with more people.
I think a lot of my gripes with the game are because of design choices based on it being developed for a portable system (PS Vita). Short missions are good for on the go systems. You can't always depend on being able to play multiplayer so it would be nice to be able to play the other half of the game without internet. Consider 2 years from now, how many people are going to be playing the multiplayer anyway..
Despite it all, I had fun with it, which is why I'm giving it recommended status. But this game is not for most. If you've never played a Neptunia game, I recommend the first game: Hyperdimension Neptunia rebirth re1. If you've had your fill with Neptunia U, you can skip this one, it's not different enough.

Mortal Kombat X is a superb game. As a versus fighter it's far ahead of its predecessor MK9, and it feels very much like a modern fighter. When you play MKX you'll be tempted to think that this game will age very well.
MKX has lots of strengths.
It has solid gameplay mechanics, solid enough to be featured in EVO. Traditionally gameplay has often been a problem for MK games, but not MKX. Behind the blood, gore, and over-the-top action there is actually a very good fighting game here.
It has a ginormous cast of playable characters, 100 to be precise (including DLCs). Thanks to the new variation system. This makes it very hard to get bored with the game, as there are always more characters to explore and learn.
The graphics is jaw-dropping. Period.
The story mode is short but interesting. Most other fighting games don't even feature a story mode.
The online play wasn't very good when the game came out but the Oct '16 patch fixed that. It's quite good now.
The difference between good and great is often in the details. MKX definitely shines in the details.
If you were ever a fan of MK then this is it. MKX is the ultimate MK game that the devs always promised but never before delivered. Just hop in and have a blast.

An amusing riff on publishers' attempt to over-monetize their titles contrary to the actual artistry of the title. DLC Quest is a one-joke game, but it's a funny joke and it fortunately knows when to let it go. It succeeds where other similar satires fail (I'm looking at you, 2004 Bard's Tale!) because rather than drag on and on trying to milk that single joke into a full-length game, DLC Quest is - wisely - a very short experience As in, less than an hour long to get to the end. As such, it is barely worth it's price, especially since the gameplay is that of an uninspired platformer. Still, it's rare that a game gets me to crack an honest smile so even if it does seem a bit overpriced, I'll forgive it because it actually was funny.

The Geneforge Saga is made by Jeff Vogel, a man who's been making a living off of being indie, long before it became fashionable.

Spiderweb have been developing intricate old school titles for quite some time.
Ever since the Exile series in my infancy I have been content to order crude sprites around, mostly to kill other crude sprites.
The Exile series achieved a number of impressive feats: Mechanically competent gameplay that offered a variety of approaches, the coveted feel of open world exploration rife with secrets and side quests, a well-executed story, culture and competent descriptive prose, and a scope that contributed to a sense of journey, progress and achievement - even some elements of long-term choice and effect. All this put together in the early to mid 90’s and your customizable party (of all Sliths specializing in polearms) was in for a great time.
Most of these features - including turn based action-point combat - seem to have been translated more or less to the Geneforge series. Rather than races, a party and free point allocation, Geneforge sees 1 character (and possibly an army of pets)...
Along with the "Blades of Exile" series, the "Geneforge" series are one of the best, ultra, old-school, hardcore RPGs out there.

--== Early Access Review ==--
The good
Beautiful realistic graphics, lots of different teams to choose from, fitting music and responsive controls. This game is not exactly a new Wipeout. You don't collect any weapon from the track. Before the race you'll have to choose two types of weapons that you'll be able to use after an offensive pick-up. There's also a deffensive pick-up which will reload your shields. There are also boost "places" on the track that will boost your speed, like in Wipeout. You can also boost your speed using a KERS system.
The bad (most of which will be fixed in the final game as I guess)
Some places in the tracks are too narrow. The "boost pads" and pick-ups could occupy a larger place so they wouldn't be missed easily. More sound effects are needed for the races. The screens need more polishing (that's not so important actually).
I'd suggest this game to anyone who liked the good old Wipeout (although it's a bit different in its gameplay) and AG racing in general. Even as it is now, in this (not so) early access state it's a very good game!
The world's final reminder of what a next-gen Wipeout could be.

I finally got around to playing this and...wow...what an experience! It's a very short experience, just about 3 hours long if you don't mess up too much, but I will say that the story told here is very much worth being experienced. I've never seen a game that controls the way this does, whereas you control two brothers simultaneously, one with one joystick, and one with the other. It's basically single player co-op, and it works surprisingly well despite it being rather tricky. I wouldn't call the game difficult though as they ease you into each mechanic perfectly without the use after any direct instruction. Your controls consist entirely of movement via joysticks, triggers for interacting with the environment for each brother, and shoulder buttons to rotate the camera...that's it. Gameplay consists of solving various puzzles using mechanics revolving around the two brothers, meanwhile experiencing the rather breathtaking story. It evokes a wide range of emotions within it's story, and without spoiling it, it touches on some pretty mature themes and can be quite sad. The game is voice acted, though here's the kicker...it's all giberish. That's right, it's only there to convey emotion. The entire story is devoid completely of english or any other language. It absolutely amazes how a game can tell such a mesmerizing story without language. The music is also amazing and atmospheric, and although the graphics aren't the greatest, there were moments where I marvelled at the artistic vision. This is an example of the whole being greater than the sum of it's parts. It's far from perfect, and replayability is pretty much non-existent, but this one will stick with me for a while. As for the big question, is it worth the price? Well, here's what I'll ask you...would you pay $15 to see an excellent movie in theater? If yes, and if you're willing to interact with that excellent movie to progress the plot, then I'd say yes. This is an interactive story unlike any I've experienced, and I can almost guarantee you will agree.

This game has such a bad rating without deserving it! Just like how it had happened with Mass Effect 3. After reading all reviews, I wasn't sure if I would like it and wanted to skip DEMD first. Until I stumbled over a Steam Key via eBay (23 Euro). That's when I bought it and I'm glad I did! Because the game is not even close to what the reviews here makes it look like.
And that's why I want to offer my own opinion about Deus Ex Mankind Divided. I'm not really into writing reviews and seldom do but this game deserves better than 64 %.
The Mankind Divided story is a lot better than Human Revolution. In HR, it was mostly about Jensen's ex-girlfriend and the attack leading to her "death" came only second - while MD is mostly about conspirations, double agents, sleeper agents working for the Illuminati, augmented human rights and extremists on both sides (augs, pro-aug and anti-aug).
The graphics are impressive. Just as the level design. There's so much content to interact with. And virtually everything can be hacked! DX12 is still a bit wonky/glitchy (beta) and resource heavy. I'm playing on DX11 with high settings, with textures on Ultra, and the game runs without stuttering or any significant lags.
The gameplay is freestyle, eg. every mission can be solved how the player wants. There are always several solutions for everything. And not every solution is plain obvious. I had a blast finding ways to enter buildings without being spotted or finding ways into apartments on higher levels. The best and truly lifelike experience I had:
I was supposed to enter an apartment on a first level. But the doors into the building couldn't be opened. There was a small ledge along the next building and a private garage next to it. But no means for me to reach the garage roof. So I hacked the garage door, opened it and placed a heavy dumpster next to it. Then, I climbed onto the dumpster, on the open garage door, onto the garage roof and from there, I made my way along the ledge and jumped on the balcony surrounding the apartments windows. AWESOME. No more silly pathfinding workarounds no sane person would ever do.
Crafting system - loved it to bits. I was hunting down crafting parts everywhere to build my own ammo, multitools and biocells.
The game has a "normal" ending, with an epilogue and a conclusing narrative about the decisions the player has made. The end is neither sudden nor unsatisfying.
The storyline itself provides only one ending, a good and a bad one. The path leading to the endfight is very diverse, it's really not important how the final fight is handled. It's just another fight, only the enemy is bigger than the others.
Besides, a game doesn't need bossfights to be entertaining. Button-mashing crazies should stick to stuff like Mortal Combat instead of polluting the RPG scene, tbh.
I liked Alex Vega and the story arc about Jim Miller was really great.
Characters from Human Revolution had cameos: there's a whole sidemission about Eliza Cassan. Megan Reed has a short appearance via recorded phonecall and a few characters and organisations from Ion Storm's Deus Ex (2000) are making an appearance this time as well: Joseph Manderley, Morgan Everett, NSF and: Silhouette will be founded in France right then (epilogue narration). Stanton Dowd was mentioned in the "The Rift"-DLC.
I wouldn't be surprised if the next game about Adam Jensen will end with the founding of UNATCO, thus bringing the whole Deus Ex experience full circle.
-----------
conclusion:
I played the main game (stealth playthrough) for 60 hours, Desperate Measures (1 hour) and System Rift (5 hours) and had a blast doing so. I started a lethal playthrough as my second playthrough two days ago and I doubt that I gonna stop there. I like Mankind Divided so much better than Human Revolution. Adam Jensen was one-dimensional and uninteresting in the first game. Now, he'd got a personality and he turned into a believeable person instead of being just another stereotyped, taser/gun-wielding cardboard hero.
I'm really looking forward to the next Deus Ex!
Oh, and a few words about that infamous shop:
The micro-transactions shop is NOT ingame. It's just part of the menue - nothing more. I really cannot understand the outrage concerning the shop. No one's forced to buy stuff for real money. I'm not bothered by it. In fact, I don't mind a shop being part of the game; everyone's including micro-transactions nowadays. And instead of leaving nasty reviews out of spite, ppl simply shouldn't buy any creds/praxis kits to make a point. Because money is the only thing that makes the world go round.
---------
And a few ingame details:
Adam can switch his vision between HUD and no HUD. This cannot be influenced by the player but it's a neat detail nonetheless.
The characters finally have decent teeth...
And Pritchard chews his fingernails...
The ingame hair looks also great.
The new augs are nice.
The CASIE interactions have improved visually.
The loading screen is animated; a train ride, and with the city being under martial law, he walks the distance to the next station. On the track.
The characters are of different height.

Silent Service and Silent Service II are among my all-time favorite PC games. In my opinion these are still the best submarine simulation games I have played. They have the right mix of simulation and playability to give you the feel of being in crontrol of a sub without some of the minute details that make some sub sims unplayable. For instance, you don't need to worry about running aground and sinking when you are on the big map, though you do need to keep an eye on your fuel tank. These games date back to the early days of computer gaming. The first copy of Silent Service which I owned ran on a 5.25" floppy disk in one floppy drive with the DOS OS running from a similar floppy in the other floppydrive, for in those days hard drives were still unknown. Windows had not been invented yet and there was no such thing as a computer mouse. A lot has changed since those days, but these games are still very enjoyable if you are able to go through the learning process. There is no tutorial such as we know tutorials in modern games. Back in those days the operating manual was the tutorial and you learned the game by reading the manual and trial-and-error. For those who, like myself, played this game many years ago and remember it well, you can skip to the back of the manual and refresh your memory on the keyboard controls and be back stalking convoys with very little time practicing to refresh your skills. For those new to the game, it is well worth spending some time to look through the manual and at least skim some of the basics. A thorough read will give you some very useful information that will help you get up to speed faster once you begin play. I was not able to get the game manual link in Steam to work, but you will find .pdf files containing the English and German versions of the original game manuals in the installation directory once you have downloaded the game. On my PC running Windows 8.1 the path for the SS2 English game manual is "C:\Program Files (x86)\Steam\SteamApps\common\Silent Service 2\Manual (English).pdf" Good hunting, Commander.

Today I will critique Torchlight II. My review will cover character classes and development, storyline, graphics, and playabilitiy of the game.
The feel of Torchlight II is similar to every action role-playing game (ARPG) availible in the current gaming market. The storyline and plot of Torchlight II feels original and fresh. Torchlight II continues the story of Torchlight I, and fans of the original will thoroughly enjoy the conclusion to this story. You have the four basic classes of Engineer, Outlander, Berserker, and Embermage.
* Engineer: a heavy melee type fighter
* Outlander: a ranger type fighter that uses ranged weapon and also uses low-level spells.
* Berserker:  is some type of off-brand fighter that uses quick attacks and animal-themed special powers.
* Embermage: is a wizard and a highly trained spell-casting class with elemental attacks.
The graphics are not going to blow you away, and for a game that was released earlier this year, it looks like a game that belongs in the early 2000's.
The pros: This game is geared more towards a casual fan of RPG's. In-fact, I'd say this game is more suited for someone in the age demagraphics of pre-teen to teen (10 yrs old to 13 yrs old)
The cons: If you are an avid RPG gamer, I'd recommend skipping this game. Torchlight II does not require endless hours of grinding, the story and gaming time are fairly short. Since the story is too short for my tastes, others might get endless hours of enjoyment from the online PvP. In the end, the bottom is spend the $19.99 plus tax on a more indepth game like Elder Scrolls.

LOTRO is an excellent "visualization" of J. R. R. Tolkien's Trillogy - The Lord of the Rings. It is based solely on the books, and therefor differs from the Peter Jackson movie version -- which took significant liberties with the books. There is no "Dwarf Tossing" or "Shield surfing" in Helms Deep to just pick two glaring examples.
The world of Middle Earth is huge, and contains many "easter eggs" from both the books and Tolkien's life.
At present, November 2014, LOTRO has no "end-game" - it has only just begun the third book of the Trillogy, and will probably not reach the Black Gate until 2016. But while we hope Sam and Frodo reach Mount Doom on their own, there is much to do to clean-up Sauron's deviltry in the rest of the world.
There is much to do in Middle Earth. 29 Servers provide a wealth of opportunity for players to create different characters for each of the four races - Dwarf, Elf, Man and Hobbit; and in each of the classes - Hunter, Champion, Guardian, Captain, Minstrel, Lore-master, and with the appropriate expansions, Rune-keeper, Warden and the just introduced Beorning. Players can create characters on each server!
The Fan-run website:
provides a wealth of information about the game, from items and quests, to background lore.

Geneforge 1. Feel the retro! The game is relatively good, if you can take the old school. The graphics feel old, the play control definitetly feels old, and the dungeons and difficulty will kick your butt if you don't play carefully, even on Normal difficulty. Which can be good and bad. Further, the strategy elements are actually fairly well done. I started out with a pair of fire spitters, and using the whole "move and cover" thing actually works out just about right.
As a note - if you go for minions, do not let the AI control them. The AI isn't bad at it, but it will drop the ball occassionally with pathfinding and enemy choices, and it tends to go looking for trouble if there isn't an immediate threat.
If your in the mood for it, few Steam games can scratch that old school rpg/strategy itch better than Geneforge. If that isn't what your after, try Geneforge 3 or 4 for an upgraded version instead.
Reminds me a ton of old Mac shareware RPGs I used to obsess over... or, in other words, Baldur's Gate with an ugly(er) art style, no polish, and no budget. Good for a curiosity.
A unique storyline with a very interesting battle system. I played this game when I was younger and it is still one of my favorites in the rpg genre.

The Geneforge games are some of the best RPGs ever (with the first and the fifth games in the series being highlights, although all of them are good).  Massive worlds, lots of old-school stats, tons of different ways to play (the character build system has much more variety than most RPGs, and the ability to create companions to fight for you is a nice touch), many different factions to join, ignore, or fight, and lots of freedom to act in a world where your choices actually affect the way the game plays.  Plus, the setting is a refreshing mix of sci-fi and fantasy and, at times, is genuinely strange, as opposed to just the same old boring Tolkeinisms found in most RPGs.  If you can get past the admittedly rough graphics and less than beautiful aesthetics these games are awesome.

Despite being released in 2001 this game lacks the graphical sophistication of titles of that era. Do not let that fool you though. Geneforge's graphical style is a throwback to those glory days of early pre-console gaming; a visual feast of animated pixels. What we have here is an incredibly immersive RPG reminiscent of the days when games kept you playing not because the last achievement is to kill a bajillion goblins but because it's genuinely interesting. The plot is original and offers multiple endings based upon the many decisions you'll have to make while playing and the turn based, AP driven combat system allows you to play in a variety of styles as suiting your character choice, be it a warrior, rogue or summoner. Throw in a well thought out stat system and this feels less like a video game and more like a DnD adventure with bonus graphical interface. With all 5 titles in the saga available for £16.99 (yes, it's a bundle) how can you not be playing this?

The three things that some might find appealing is the humor (boring), the easy achievements to get (for achievement hunters), and the speed run competition.  This game is so dang easy that anyone can participate in a speed run.  Even if you don't make the fastest time, you can still land yourself on the board without much challenge.  All in all, it simply lacks in every part of what makes a game challenging, but it isn't completely broken.  I didn't care much for it.

DLC Quest is a very literal take on the way some companies (*cough*EA*cough*Capcom*cough) exploit DLC in the way that some things that should already be in the game are purposely removed from the finished product and later sold at a price, separately from the game, which is just incredibly insulting to the people who have spent their hard-earned money on the game.
DLC Quest involved you paying for incredibly hilarious things such as being able to jump, being able to move left, and to even pause the game.
DLC Quest on Steam is a short but sweet game, and it comes with both DLC Quest games, including the sequel "Live Freemium Or Die", so for the price of £1.99, it's a bargain, and cheaper than most DLC's themselves!
Overall, I would highly recommend DLC Quest to anybody who wants two short but sweet games, pick this up!

This game is beautiful and moving.  It is fairly short but the brevity adds to to the poignancy.
In essence this is a game that celebrates the concept of family, from happiness and joy to profound sorrow. The familial bond is further reinforced by the concept of team work.  I would urge people to play this game on a 360 controller because unlike other games where you need to set "character A" up on the a pressure pad then switch to take control of "Character B" as you move her through the door, in this game you are able to control both characters simultaneously using the thumb sticks and running two people in different directions at the same time adds another level of challenge and enjoyment.  I fairly certain I lack the coordination to pull this off with keyboard and mouse though.
In a world where films drag on with little thought to plot, with their pointless explosions and shakey-cam and the need to drag out scene beating you over the head with them, you need Brothers: A tale of two sons to remind you the art of story telling is still alive.
Definitely nominating for “I'm Not Crying, There's Something In My Eye” Award. Wish the game just keeps going on and on for ever.

Alright, so Mortal Kombat X was an amazing game at the beginning and still is! The problem that I see is that whenever I go online, I can either never find a match, or I find someone who acts like he plays 24/7 and hits me with 13 hits in a combo. This makes me hate the game very much, although it is just because I don't practice enough. Another thing that bothers me which was added a while ago, was the Kombat Pack 2. It is 20 dollars for 4 characters, kold war skin pack, goro, and 2 classic fatality packs. Everything here is previous content besides the four characters introduced in this. I have all the items in pack 2 from before kombat pack 2 was realised. If I were to buy it, I would have just used twenty dollars for 4 characters really. Same thing when you buy the characters by itself. It literally is 4 cents cheaper just to get the four characters. I understand this is how the game makes money, besides actually buying the game, although it is just very bothering that it is twenty dollars. A lot of people will disagree with me and attempt to lecture me on this, but I am ok with that. Share your opinons if you would like to do so. Anyway that is just the dlcs and the online gameplay. The actual game itself is amazing. The story mode is very nice to play, although some parts can be annoying. I really enjoyed the game when I first started out on story mode. Then I moved on to practicing combos. What I learned is that the keyboard is very hard to do combos in practice mode and singleplayer. I also find that many people use controllers, so I plugged in mine, and the combos would mess up considering when you actually perform something as (up down left right) it would mess up and for example, register this move. (Up down slide) This didn't bother me so much, since I got used to it. It really didn't happen often, but it happened when I needed it most to not happen. Next, the practice. There isn't much to say, except it is fun to actually spar with bots and practice your combos, fatalities and whatever the fatalities are called before you kill them. Like you don't drain their health and you perform something to do a cool fatality. Anyway, a cool feature I noticed on practice, the hard and very hard mode, the bots can stick 8 hit combos, which really interested me to get better. I haven't played in a while, so don't judge me if this was implemented a long time ago. Really the game is amazing, apart from the difficulty of finding matches, the cost of characters, and how there isn't like a skill thing to implement who you fight against. I understand why it's a good and a bad idea. The good idea is that you can fight people your own skill level, and actually hope to enjoy the game, with no rage if you win, and feel normal if you lose. The bad thing is how iit would take quite a good amount of time to actually implement this, and people would forcefully derank themselves by losing matches, just to fight against people worse at the game then them. Anyway I hope this review was helpful, and have a great day.

Simple gameplay mechanics meet elegant level design.  Shadow bug is a 2D action puzzle platformer with NO JUMPING.  In this game, you can only jump by attacking enemies, which are strategically placed to create a path through the level.  Each level does a good job on building up mechanics previously taught through the levels proceeding it.
The visual and audio aesthetics are both on point, and exceptionally well made.  They help this game achieve an almost zen-like type of flow.  Shadow Bug is well priced at $5, it's not the longest game, but it has a fair amount of replability through level challenges.  If you're looking for a nice game to sync your brain with for a few hours with a bit of challenge this is the one for you.

This game was fantastic. I wasn't expecting very much given that it is an indie game for 5 dollars from a new studio, but Shadow Bug delivered everything I wanted and more. The unique movement mechanics of the game play extremely smoothly, and the levels are designed to be difficult despite the fact that a large portion of your movement is in straight lines between enemies. There is a secret collectible in every level, and a reasonable amount of flexibility in how you move through the game.
Additionally, the art and sound design is beautiful, and really adds to the intensity of the game's many tense platforming sequences.
Muro Studios has managed to take a very simple concept and execute it perfectly, creating an intense and challenging experience. With 37 levels, my only real complaint about this game is that there isn't more of it.

Wow, I just noticed I am nearing 800 hours in GTAV. I think that calls for a summerized review. Okay, I am sure I am going to take heat here for going against the current trend of negative reviews for this game. That is okay I love speaking my mind, I can handle any criticizm that anyone has. To be frank, no one of us is right or wrong in our reviews. A review or critique is just a matter of opinion anyways, and I am just sharing mine. I respect everyone else's since freedom of speech and personal expression should be a right for every human.
Okay having nearly 800 hours played here, I have to definitely recommend GTAV for anyone who is a fan of the series and somehow has not bought it yet or if you are a fan of sandbox/multiplayer games in general. I don't work for Rockstar and am not a fan boy, I happen to have over 30 years of experience as a gamer. I have had the blessing of watching the birth of the gaming industry and watch it become what it is today. I know there is a lot of anger right now toward Take Two and Rockstar over their new stance on modding. My review is based only on the vanilla game. I have never used a mod in the game and I have nothing at all against modding in a single-player offline setting. Now the single player mode while good, to me the story in no way compares to the depth of GTAIV. I like all of the characters  especially Tevor, but not receiving any additional DLC for the story mode like in the previous games leaves me wanting more.
Now where GTAV falters a bit in the story mode, the online mode more than makes up for it. I am fortunate to have a vast number of good and trustworthy friends to play with in online mode and let me tell you there is no online game on any platform that gives you the play variety of GTAV online. You can race in a huge variety of vehicles, environments, and modes. Do you like shooting? There is such a huge variety of modes where you can team up with your friends or go in an all out deathmatch it will make your head spin. Oh man, I am just getting started! You even have tennis and golf. While simplistic and not perfect, these modes are also a blast to play with friends. The quailty while not perfect, definitely is better than a mediocre stand alone golf/tennis game. Want more? Go play some darts, run some CEO missions, Call some friends to do a challenging prision break heist! There are hours and hours upon missions and events in free mode there is not enough room here to list them all. Suffice to say, there should be something for everyone here. I know I know, a lot of the nice things are expensive in GTAV. I like that. In real life, you have to work hard to earn things like that nice home, or a nice new car. Things earned though effort bring about appreciation and satisfaction. I know this is just a game, but too often now days people look for the easy way out...say money drops on everyone in the session. The modding online was getting to be so ridiclous you could spawn in a public session and get modded instantly. Modding people that don't want it is wrong and unfair not to mention cheating in a PvP environment gives you a fake sense of satisfaction if you ''win.'' They may have went a bit far when they banned mods in the offline mode but something had to be done to restore the original playing experience the game was intended to provide online. That is final thought on GTAV. Knowing every weekend I get to do 100's of different events with my friends makes me feel satisfied I bought this game. It is a must buy, but wait for a sale. The price of $59.99 USD is way to high for a 2+ year old game.

Too bad the online community has become cancerous and a waste of time. Between the spawn killing kiddos, spawn menu "hackers" and people trying to do money drops on you to get your account banned, it is just a sucky experience all around.

I've been playing this shortly since it was released on Kongregate, and like some others, decided to completely start over for the Steam release. Basically, the hours/achievements I have on here don't actually reflect my full extent. Anyway, on to the actual review.
The game has definitely improved a lot- the balancing issues aren't nearly as bad, the milestones seem more stable, and they're still adding more features. A lot of the typos have been fixed, too, and personally I haven't noticed any more.
The art is cute enough and the girls aren't carbon copies of each other. And Bearverly! She started as an April Fool's joke, but now that she's an actual part of the game, I think that's really precious. It's good that developers can have fun with jokes like that.
Though I wouldn't call this an amazing idle/time management/etc game, I do think it's one of the better ones that I've seen. Having to balance hobbies and jobs is interesting since it can be hard to decide if you want the money or the girls quicker. There's still work that needs to be done, but I'm glad that I've been able to see the development of this game to 'literally impossible to obtain' goals to 'this can be done in time' goals.
Also. I enjoy the little references like Iro and Rainbowdash, and Alpha and Hatsune Miku.
TLDR; Play it if you like cute girls, diverse personalities, and like seeing games develop further.

Having watched this game for months (and as a huge fan of both the wipEout and F-Zero series), I had built up some substantial expectations. Many of them were actually met, which is fantastic. In other areas, Formula Fusion was lacking (which I'm attributing to the Early Access status).
The game is beautiful, and the controls are smooth. The machines feel heavy, which adds an element of realism. Another realistic aspect that I'm not quite as fond of is the relatively low speeds. The game is fast-paced, don't get me wrong, but the huge environments and small tracks don't feel like you're rushing through the arena at mach 7, they feel like a speedy Gran Turismo.
The small tracks. With how slowly the machines turn, they definitely need to be wider. At this point, there are some pixel-perfect turns in-game, which is a fun challenge in one respect, and a frustrating design flaw in another.
My only real complaint, though, is the lack of a local multiplayer. This is a game that would be amazing pulling an all-nighter with friends and pizza. We always play F-Zero X or wipEout, but they're increasingly dated games. This would be a great next-gen addition to the repertoire. Just saying, I'd be more inclined to recommend people get it if it had local multiplayer.
Lastly, I'm looking forward to new content. Especially with weapons. This is a great opportunity for some creativity, guys. Even just a homing missile would be an improvement (or maybe there is one, and I've just not found it yet).

I come from the tradition of the old f-zero, then podracer for the n64, then f-zero for the gamecube, and finally fatal inertia for the xbox, as opposed to the majority of people who played wipeout, so I have a different perspective on anti-grav racers than most of the reviewers.
That being said, I like this game, it has promise, but here are my impressions.
I played the useless tutorial and then two practice races. I lost my first practice race and then I won my second one by literally a minute and a half distance between me and second place. The AI is clearly currently bad. (But again, I've been playing anti-grav racers since I learned how to read, so that could have something to do with it.)
Four tracks is a small number, but it is early access, and I like the variation in them, so this is fine. However, some of these four tracks within themselves could use a bit more variety, they felt more like leisurely drives than perhaps what an anti-grav racetrack would be like.
The airbrake is worse than useless, it actively slows you down and doesn't help you corner faster. That's an easily fixed problem though, and could help with the "leisurely drive" issue, since you have something to do other than push the stick gently to one side.
The graphics are beautiful. My aging laptop has a time keeping up, but I love how the world and racers look. Engine effects could have a bit mor umphff, but that's knitpicky. It does a fairly good job of giving you the impression of speed.
Overall though, if you want a game like the ones I cited up there and won't compromise, pass on this, it feels much too caged and repetitive compared to those, and the meager distraction offered by the boost pads won't feel like much compared to dodging trees, rocky rivers, and flying down active volcanoes.
If you're a sucker in general for anti-grav (me), then this is a good buy, so I give it a tacit recommendation. And when the race is close, it's pretty damn fun.

I nominated this game for "Best Ludonarrative Assonance", in the "We Didn't Think of Everything" category for the Winter 2016 Steam Game Awards.
"Ludonarrative Dissonance" is a concept that game critics use to talk about how a game's narrative (e.g. talking about how selflessness is good) and a game's gameplay mechanics (e.g. exploiting NPCs for personal gain) are often out of sync. This game, however, has one of the greatest examples of ludonarrative assonance I've ever seen -- explicitly using the game's mechanics and controls to drive home an emotional and narrative point.
I can't say more without spoilers, but I can honestly say that this game is beautiful, novel, and well worth your time.

Brawlhalla is one of those games games that feels like it was an attempt at doing Super Smash Brothers with improvements and tweaks, but Brawlhalls works, like REALLY well. As said before, it's a SSB style game, 4 players fight on a random stage in a stock or time match, but there's much more content than just that. First off, the weapons system. Every character you can play as has two weapons they can equip by grabbing swords that drop onto the field periodically. While the weapons themselves are somewhat copy/paste, the characters moveset becomes different with very weapon. Then, there's online play. Like Smash Bros, you can join into a lobby with other people to duke it out with other opponents. Not to mention how little waiting there is between searching for a match and joining one. Finally, there's the leveling system. Every time you play with a hero, you get EXP for it allowing you to level up. This can unlock you new weapon skins, color pallets, or even entirely new "stances", which are basically a different distribution of the character's stats. The only real problem I have with Brawlhalla is the attack spamming that comes up from time to time, but with how frequently this game is updated, I don't think that'll be a problem for too much longer.
Brawlhallla gets a 9/10, it's nearly perfect, but a few things need to be fixed here and there. Oh, and did I mention that it's completely free to play?

Well... Been playing this game since release day. Purchased the whole thing last winter inc the whole downloadables thing. Why? Because I love Deus Ex!

Yes I am doing a comparative analysis here because I love both games and both were parallel in development in playability. The second installment of Hitman was a major jump in playability. I have played the second over and over. Invisible War suffered the same controls issues that I didn't care for in the Original Deus Ex.  The Deus Ex Human Revolution was given to us. Wow. The contols were spot on for what the game wanted you to do and wanted to let you do. The player was immersed in a future cyber punk sci fi world that was a place I could get absolutley lost in. So the controls I was able to operate making Adam my extension. My avatar. When the controls are good you can just fall into a game. When they aren't the controls keep jerking you out of the game and you have to concentrate on the controls more than the game. I hate that. Oldie but goldie. This game was among the first of the Warhammer 40k series I've ever played. The hours I had on vanilla, Winter Assault, Dark Crusade and ultimatelly Soulstorm were priceless. Singleplayer campaign designed to give you a feel for the grimdark of the setting, throwing you into diverse encounters for vanilla, only to turn to a province control campaign for Dark Crusade was quite a journey.
Multiplayer however made for me and my friends the real fun. Last stands versus insanely hard AIs, spread across fortification control maps or even objective capturing. The AI was really well made to give you a challenge if you went for Hard and above.
My only regret is that Dawn of War 2 did not follow up on the diversity of race playstyle. Because that was one of the major pro points the first Dawn of War serie had against the second. Pitty tyranids are only obtainable through Ultimate Apocalypse (which is a highly recommended mod if you ever get bored of the same old scenarios with the 8 factions. Although that's a slight bit unlikely).

Alright, so Mortal Kombat X was an amazing game at the beginning and still is! The problem that I see is that whenever I go online, I can either never find a match, or I find someone who acts like he plays 24/7 and hits me with 13 hits in a combo. This makes me hate the game very much, although it is just because I don't practice enough. Another thing that bothers me which was added a while ago, was the Kombat Pack 2. It is 20 dollars for 4 characters, kold war skin pack, goro, and 2 classic fatality packs. Everything here is previous content besides the four characters introduced in this. I have all the items in pack 2 from before kombat pack 2 was realised. If I were to buy it, I would have just used twenty dollars for 4 characters really. Same thing when you buy the characters by itself. It literally is 4 cents cheaper just to get the four characters. I understand this is how the game makes money, besides actually buying the game, although it is just very bothering that it is twenty dollars. A lot of people will disagree with me and attempt to lecture me on this, but I am ok with that. Share your opinons if you would like to do so. Anyway that is just the dlcs and the online gameplay. The actual game itself is amazing. The story mode is very nice to play, although some parts can be annoying. I really enjoyed the game when I first started out on story mode. Then I moved on to practicing combos. What I learned is that the keyboard is very hard to do combos in practice mode and singleplayer. I also find that many people use controllers, so I plugged in mine, and the combos would mess up considering when you actually perform something as (up down left right) it would mess up and for example, register this move. (Up down slide) This didn't bother me so much, since I got used to it. It really didn't happen often, but it happened when I needed it most to not happen. Next, the practice. I highly recommend Shadow Bug, and I am somewhat disappointed that there are not that many reviews (and maybe not that many players).
Shadow Bug is an action platformer with something different in the mechanics. The game does not let you walk and jump just by pressing the keys. In fact, your character cannot do a normal jump at all. The only way to get off of the ground is to "select" an enemy or object on the screen, and Shadow Bug will lunge and fly directly at it, usually in a sharp angle. The bug will then slash the enemy or object, destroying it, and do a little leap after the attack. Then it starts falling back to the ground, unless you choose something else quickly.
Because of this mechanic, you have to be extremely good with timing, and also make sure you figure out what is the best order and direction to go in. For instance, as the game goes on, traps that will instantly kill you will start showing up more often. And in some places, if you attack enemies too quickly, you will fly right into a trap because you didn't wait for the right angle.
The mechanic may sound simple at first, but it definitely requires some work to manage. For myself, the game seemed like it was second nature for me, surprisingly, and I did very well at it. But I can definitely see many people having difficulty with it.
One more note I will say about the mechanic is that I find playing with an actual mouse to be the best way to go. I tried a controller at first, and thought it was a horrible idea, because you have to move the cursor with a joystick, slowly, and press a button to select. Because you have to move quickly, using a mouse just makes sense, as you can move the cursor at whatever speed you want.
Now, the game has 36 levels in it, with 6 of them being boss levels. Most of the levels are actually not that long once you get the hang of them, but will require some practice. In fact, I would say that the majority of the levels could be speed-run in less than 2 minutes per level, except for maybe a few levels towards the end, or some boss levels. But the game took me over 5 hours to 100% complete, and the game is only $4.99 in price, so the fun I had is worth it to me.
Each level has 3 goals: the actual completion of the level, a time limit, and the number of shiny point items you found. The items look like white orbs that are apparently called “spirits,” which are hidden around the levels or even drop when you destroy some enemies. Each level also has an “epic spirit” which is a single spirit that contains a bunch of smaller ones, and they count as actual collectibles, while the small spirits are mainly for points.
After each boss level, you wind up in new areas that bring up new types of puzzles and new types of traps, such as a sewer area that has acid pits that sometimes have fish enemies leap out of them. Many of the puzzle goals are finding ways to hold switches or finding keys to unlock doors and continue onward; but the actual methodology to do so heavily depends upon how well you get adapted to the mechanic and if you know how to set up your movement in order to reach necessary places.
The art style of the game is great, I believe, and the sound is pretty good too. None of the music or effects bothered me if I heard them over and over while trying a level.
About the only downside I would say for the game is that the game suddenly spikes the difficulty in the last 2 levels by an extreme amount. Despite that, I ended up simply giving up for an evening, and I came back the next day to try again and was able to complete them with all of the goals.
So in the end, I think Shadow Bug is definitely worth a try, and I hope more people on here end up buying it. I would like to see more from the developers in the future.

As a single player experience I could highly recommend GTA V, it has a few flaws in that there are very few ways to make money outside of the big heists and crucially, there has not been one single piece of single player dlc since its release. But largely the game is incredibly engaging and very very good looking.
Where his game fails is it's online mode which has taken over completely and continues to receive free updates fairly regularly. It all started very promising and as you can I have enjoyed this game immensely having put more hours into this than many other titles in my collection. But the GTA online community is rife with cheaters, hackers, trolls and all manner of useless people who are absolutely set on ruining your experience of this game. The other party intent on wrecking an otherwise AAA title is R* themselves. They do seemingly nothing to prevent or deter people hacking and ruining this game and mechanics that punish honest players remain in place since day one (if someone runs you over repeatedly for example and you decide to destroy their vehicle, your player must pay a % value of that players car for the privelage). The game continues to protect trolls and cheaters who do not earn their money and so do not care to play fairly or feel the effects of the puny punishments the game has to offer undesirable behaviour. New content comes with increasingly larger price tags, whilst the methods of generating money do not seem to scale accordingly, again rewarding cheaters with brand new game balance destroying tools at no cost to themselves.
GTA online is an mmo which requires a lot of time invested to enjoy all it has to offer, but you a routinely punished by the game or its player base making for a largely unenjoyable experience. I have spent the past 6 months playing GTA online, completely solo, as other players are simply guaranteed to wreck your hard work. I think this should speak volumes about the game, especially considering there are forums and tutorials on how to deliberately join a public lobby (which you need to do to take part in most activities) whilst simultaneously blocking other users from joining you.

All in all: worth trying.

I'm kind of in the (really) lower spec range for this game (i7 2600, R7250, 8GB) and the game runs quite nice here (I think?) running at about 30FPS @ 720p on a normal race, save for the "Atol" track, which is kinda heavy (FPS drops to 15~20), so I can't just say "oooh the game runs so smooth and rocks here", but if you have some better specs, I can totally recommend this game and say it's just as you would expect for a modern AG racing game like the original Wipeout trilogy (which I've played a LOT)!
Even though I just purchased this one now, I've been keeping an eye on the development of this game and the developers are doing some pretty nice work on it! The game is beautiful and fast, track designs are great, as the ship design! Also, it's great to see TDR taking part in it too! :D
The controls, and overall feeling of the game, have that "Wip3out" feeling (maybe because the developers worked in it? :P).

Note: Steam doesnt seem to record game time while offline. I actually spent about 6 hours on this game, prior to review.
I recommend this game!
The gameplay is solid and fun. The menu navigation was swift and intuitive. The races feel like fast paced roller coasters with loops, twists, and sharp turns. I really liked the upgrade system, as it allows you to spend exactly how much you want in each aspect of your ship. Upgrading has a big impact on your ship, such as how well it handles, how responsive the breaks are, or how defensive/ offensive your ship is. It feels truly rewarding to upgrade your ship. I have one big complaint… or you could consider it a recommendation. R8 games has something unique going on with Formula Fusion, but the multiplayer is either deserted or broken. The multiplayer also seems to be a bit shallow featured. I feel if they fix or populate the multiplayer and make more competitive features and modes, it would add a whole new feel to the game. I think R8 game’s biggest chance with this game is putting multiplayer on the top of their priority. Aside from that, there’s nothing else too bad about the game. The controls are good and responsive as long as you use an Xbox controller (or something similar, I used the NVIDIA Controller). Lastly, the music wasn’t quite my taste… but that’s probably just me.
The graphics are beautiful. The ship models are especially amazing. You can tell the developers really took time on the graphics and models. Each level is colorful and feels different than the last. Sadly, the screen seems to look fuzzy and grainy when going full speed. Other than that, there’s nothing else to complain about as far as visuals are concerned.
My specs are GTX 960 (4 GB ddr5 VRAM), Athlon 880K (Over-Clocked to 4.2), and 8 GB of DDR3 ram. For reference, I run Star Wars: Battlefront on custom MED/HIGH settings at about 30-33 FPS. I ran the game at “EPIC” settings and got about 25-30 FPS. I didn’t see any FPS/ performance change when adjusting the settings.  Keep in mind there are sparks, thruster flame trails, basic lighting, and some nice shadows. I’ll let you be the judge of how good the optimization is. There is always room for improvement when optimizing a game.
I only had one Bug. When I exited the garage the game froze and everything became fuzzy. Sound continued to play. I was forced to CTRL-ALT-DEL and restart my PC. Other than that, it’s been hassle free.
In conclusion, the game is worth the $20 dollar price tag as long as R8 games really support it and do regular updates and bug fixes. I really hope they take my advice in expanding the multiplayer features. I feel a competitive multiplayer update would really make Formula Fusion stand out from all the other generic sci-fi racing games. Who knows, maybe Formula Fusion will be the first big racing E-sport?

After testing out the big Update, which came out yesterday, I can assure you the following:
It's the successor to wipEout, not perfect in it's current state, but it's going in the right direction.
The gameplay is mostly positive, except for some things:
- The airbrakes still leave a useless impression, you can get through the courses without them, except for the new FF2000 Class, Python.
- This brings up the next thing; you're glued to walls. Crash into one and have fun getting off of it again. Most of the time you manage to get off the wall, you'll ride into the next one, because the crafts feel clumsy sometimes.
Keep in mind, it's in early Access, so these things'll probably get changed over time.
Still, in it's current state, it's not generating the same fascination like wipEout 2097/XL did for me;
Braking before the curve, so you can glide smoothly through it, the crafts nose nearly tipping the wall. Scraping the wall with back of the craft, hearing that fulfilling crunchy sound. The floaty feeling of the crafts etc. If you've played 2097, you'll probably get what I mean.
In my opinion, even to this day, 2097 got the best handling in the wipEout series, especially when flying a Quirex craft on Phantom class.
I'd like to see the same handling making a return in Formula Fusion, even though i don't believe this'll happen.
But a man can dream, right? ;)
Buy it if you love wipEout and want to support the devs, it's totally worth the few bucks!

[Updated June 3rd, 2017]. Launch is here, and the (day 2) performance patch has resolved any core concerns.
First and foremost, the game looks beautiful. You can tell this was made with love towards the original WipEout series.  However, the environments are lifeless.  They need more motion to seem real.  But great variety in track layouts, lots of fun and not too over the top in design.
Handling and controls are really good. One of the most solid handling anti-grav racers in this current rebirth of the genre.  Balance is pretty good, and the vehicle upgrades are a nice touch.  Upgrades are very important, must be considered to succeed at higher levels. AI is unforgiving, but in a good way, as there is no rubberbanding at all (advantage or disadvantage).
Progression to unlock tracks, vehicles and classes should be reviewed further.  It's not a quick process, and the campaign is very linear.   Some tweaking is also needed in the endurance and elimination races, as they're quite long (6-10 laps).
Overall it's been a long ride from TPP, to Early Access and now to the 1.0 release.  But the dedication to this game has been great.  I really hope the devs keep with the updates, with a little more polish this will easily be the best anti-grav racer available.  Long live WipEout.

Just started playing and I can already see the wipeout series blossoming in this game. I honestly hope ex-psygnosis devs are in this. I grew up with that company, and that time they forget there was only young gamers and nobody's got money. Now that we're all grown up in adulthood making our own money, please take my money and make this the wipeout reborn that was a long time coming.
On review, the initial frustration was typical, though I hated it in the beginning, turning before the bends come, aiming precisely on the boost pads, they remind me the mastery I had slowly garnered almost ghostly reminiscent of the classic wipeout. I am still a fan of the wipeout series and and yes, at this stage, with 3 tracks, I can recommend it to players of the wipeout series. I can also recommend it to new players because you are probably gonna pay less before the release and I can tell you, no faster more adrenaline packed racing game is out there compared to the wipeout series and this one is steadily rising above its former champion of the genre. By this week, I eagerly await the garage and a few more tracks and multiplayer because I never played multiplayer on wipeout but now I have a chance to not only pay my due respect to psygnosis and the devs of formula fusion but to enjoy the most action packed racing on multiplayer I never did before, killing two birds in one stone...I guess it was my calling to buy this game.
To you out there, the demo itself will tell you how fast this racing game is gonna be, you will automatically practice tunnel vision because the speed of this racing is like nothing you have ever experience in a racing game, but add to the fact that weapons,shields and craft cuztomization will be added later, I can only surmise how much they are able to do with this game. You can decide to wait and check it out later or be like me, owing psygnosis a fond memory i could never forget and have never experienced outside the wipeout series and pay them for being a kickass company that has restarted finally a wipeout game so badass with new graphics and dope music, they deserve the money not only for this game but for the wipeout they made in the past.
Pros:
- The badass music is back with more fitting genre of the century
- Almost ghostlike reminiscence of the wipeout feel and adrenaline action. A speed no other racing game have ever been able to replicate
- Graphics and camera effects have been rejuvenated to fit the new era
- A learning curve that can be mastered enough to be not too hard or too soft but at the level you'd expect from a wipeout-like series
- Best of all, I can go in and out of the game and races with a few clicks, short loading time, and quick race beginning, then a few clicks out. To me thats what I truly want in a racing game, something I can rejuice instantaneously, enjoy a few moments and leave craving for it again another time.
Cons AND Suggestions (Hence a longer explanation):
- New camera follow is rather misleading, I dont get to judge my path because being too left or right of the track brings your craft too side of the camera, making it harder to judge your turns as the camera fixes on the center of the track
- Interface is still rather light as ♥♥♥♥ hinting that the previous wipeout game itself would be laughing at it
- The hud doesnt display important details as bright as wipeout making your tunnel vision a much harder feat to accomplish. The Hud should be remade so that I can have both tunnel vision and bright details for my speed, shield and weapons
- The boost pads should have variable speed boosts with different colours and please make the weapons more improved. Right now that flimsy glittering floater is just sad to see, try making it another ground pad with sticking out weapons that is picked up on path lining, like a deployable on auto hook so that the craft looks different on the outside indicating the armed weapon type and that your craft is not able to pick any other weapon. Once fired, the enveloped weapon rig should be auto-dismantled dropping scattering scrap metal and associated dust fallouts.
If i remember correctly, previous wipeouts also had longer and harder boost durations, Lets try pushing this game to its speed limits, BAH! As if there ever was one....
Edit Update 26/7/16:
The garage is out, multiplayer is out, and 3 different crafts are out along with a new handling or shicaine based track is out (Reminds me of monaco). These are the giant features of the new update.
Pros:
- The 3 different crafts brings back the mode of racing you would want to play based on the track. I'm assuming one is heavy (Takes alot of beating but slower with higher handling), the middle apollo like craft (The middle craft with all specs on average with a slight speed advantage) and the lightweight (Focuses on max speed but poor handling and low shields).
- 4 new weapons are out: Mines (Annoying but useful for drafting trailing crafts), Energy bolt (High dmg but requires high precision), Gauss Cannon (Your everyday minigun with more ammo and spread but low dmg), Shockwave (Front disabler that slows all crafts ahead of you at a certain range and does minor dmg)
- They've removed the camere fixating on the center of the track, I can now judge my turns way better, finishing 1st on all my quick races from the get go, needn't even have to use airbrakes
- They've added a new monaco like track for those handling and tank based crafts to have an advantage with lots of shicane and snake bends
Cons:
- Due to the garage being available, all previous max attributes including your competitors have been reduced, slowing the game's pace at starting out phase of the game
- Rewards feel rather dull and unmotivational. If your not planning on higher credit stakes, either do a bet system to raise the reward or provide a storyline clip based on the track, waiting for others to finish while your craft is on autopilot can become too monotonous and unrewarding
- Weapons are fixed from start to finish. What made wipeout unique was the different pickups you'd get in the middle of a race, expanding your options, forcing technical manuevers just to obtain a weapon or shield and made each race dynamic, if you fix the weapons system to a set standard from start to finish, you'd take away dynamism and repeatability for the 13 to 33 tracks you are planning making FF rather easy to get over.
- As I was forced to master wipeout and the early version of FF, now, it feels the skill level has dropped. I'm doing so well because I'd have to practice turning before the bends, tunnel vision and air-drifting, that the game feels a little cheap at the moment, as though to appease me to keep playing the game, the difficulty setting is reduced. Maybe If I upgrade all to full, I'll get back that feeling of overdrive wipeout and early FF gave me, at speeds so fast, you'd be afraid to hit the sides because of the damage it might do to your craft
Further suggestions:
- Do a visual effect cgi when entering mach speeds, air shockwave, shattering glass, sound dampening after sound blast
- Make weapon pick up different
- Make starter speeds high, and then add some more with upgrades of speed that becomes dangerous to turn so that people upgrade only when they dare and when they are prepared. Also blows up your eyes with those kinds of speed
- Make a pit, every formula racing had a pit, especialy one that can blow up your craft mid track because your shields were down
- Add more ramp tracks with immense heights. If its one thing anti grav racing shines on, is the feeling of zero gravity whilst tunneling through the atmosphere
- Instead of autopilot, make a 'sidetracker' pick up that deflects the craft and pushes it forward when too near the sides of a track. Also have booster pick ups.

I've always been a fan of the Army Men games by 3DO, so I decided to do a leap of faith on this game. For a game under $10 there is a healthy ammount of quality content.
The maps are very unique in their layout and design aesthetic. I never got the impression of content being recycled. Each map is used for a different game mode, so the second you load into a map, you know what the main objectives are going to be.
On a GTX960 the game achieves over 100fps even with the settings maxed. Visually the game looks amazing, materials have the proper sheen and movement animations have a natural flow.
Matchmaking is fast, I can easily get a quick game in during my lunch break.
On a final note, the soundtrack is outstanding. Each piece is well performed and properly fits the battlefield it's set in.
The only flaw here is the small, playerbase. While I've never had a problem getting into a match with other players, often there are only 2-3 servers with people in them. This can make playing a specific game mode difficult from time to time.

Pros= Fun lighthearted shooter, balanced weapons, maps are detailed and unique, music is awesome, reminds me of Sarge's Heroes
