I was surprised at how short this game was - I got through it in about 80 mins on my first playthrough, and that's including replaying some bits and puzzling through some optional stuff.
That aside, I enjoyed more or less everything else.  Straight out of the gate you are faced with physics puzzles which are comparatively difficult to what you might encounter in the first couple chapters of a Half-Life game, and that threw me off balance at first.  As well, there's a dearth of ammo scattered around the first couple areas, which forces you to think creatively about how you're going to handle some situations.  I found myself starting over because of that.
Then, once the (rather unusual) physics puzzles are done, you are immediately faced with a fight on the level of Half-Life 2: Chapter 11 "Follow Freeman!"  This, without any sort of ramp-up and with no clues as to where you should find enough ammo, certainly makes things challenging.  I was in sort of a desperate panic as I fought off Combine and navigated around Striders, trying to find enough rockets to take them down.
The overall quality isn't quite there, and you can tell that Valve didn't work on this one themselves.  But its a great effort.
All things said and done, I'd recommend any fan of the franchise to give this one a playthrough.  It'll certainly help scratch the Half-Life itch, if only temporarily.

It's exactly what it says on the tin. It's a dating sim and a clicker/idle game. Nothing more nothing less. So let's just get down to it.
Pros:
+ Gameplay, while inherently simple, is fairly interesting with the addition of the dating sim elements, and a time block management. So you need to train up stats and earn money to actually be competent at wooing the girls, instead of just mad clicking skillz (autoclicker). The game also makes it clear that it is only storing your idle activities for up to 7 days. So you can schedule ahead if you're that type of person.
+ Clear requirements for getting the girls. So the game has you wooing the ladies in a couple of "stages", and each stage has very clear requirements, like needing to give her a drink as a gift, or going on two dates with her. It makes progression feel special in its own little way and does just enough to stave off monotony. That said, this system also comes with its own drawbacks.
+ The girls are cute, and the way they get introduced to you can be mildly funny, that said don't expect much from the personality department. They're archetypes and that's that. Their dialogue can also give you a chuckle or two though.
+You can prestige ASAP and the speed boosts from that prestige reset is nothing to sneeze at. Way more generous with this than most clicker games are.
+ It's free and everyone likes free games.
Cons:
- So that drawback with the requirements system? Well, the requirements are gigantic. There is a huge leap in requirements from stage to stage and it gets kind of ridiculous and grindy because of that. I know you can leave the game to idle so that it grinds up stats and money for you, and that's the point, but seeing the numbers go from around 100 to 8000 in one stage transition can be very discouraging. In fact the clicking requirements will get so huge that you probably will need mad clicking skillz (Autoclicker) in the end, or you know you can just leave it for a week and maybe you'll have finished it all.
- Another big problem is that the game will only give you idle clicks on the girls if you fulfill a stats that they like. So girls who like Buff guys will not get idle clicks if your Buff stat isn't up to par. It's never explained in the game so you might miss it and go back to your game after a couple of days expecting a full heart but getting jack all instead. The game also doesn't make how you go about fulfilling these stats requirements. So you don't know if you need to have like 8 Buff or just 3 Buff for the girl to start getting them idle clicks. It does look like that you just need at least 2 or 3 though to get the idle clicks. Which leads to another problem...
- Idle clicks can never be improved. So yeah you have 3 Buff and you get 1 idle click per second for the girl, and that's it. Even if you have 16 Buff you still only get 1 idle click per second. So then what's the point of raising the skills? Well just to meet the stage requirements that's all. That's kinda where the game starts to wilt, when it becomes grindy like that, and it doesn't take too long for it to get to that point. Also, the prices of gifts are ridiculous. Again, huge leaps from item to item, which only makes the grinding waaaay more apparent and tedious.
Overall, I do like the game though, and I can recommend this to anyone looking for a lighthearted anime clicker. It can get tedious after a while, but it's one of those games that you can just leave and come back to whenever you feel like it. Its mechanisms work quite well together and there does not seem to be any major bugs or issues from my experiences. It's also still in Early Access, so the game might be improved later through patches and updates, and for an Early Access title, it's very functional. I have not encountered any major bugs or issues so far (which is probably not that far but eh).

I think the weapon description for the Bow encapsulates this entire game perfectly. While I can't remember the entire paragraph, one sentence basically reads: ''It has Neon, therefore its a bow of the future''. The description summarizes two things about this title: it has a ♥♥♥♥load of neon, which means its an 80's dystopian vision of the future; it's really laid back and almost comedic in its approach to everything. At one point in the game your concierge tells you about something and how you have to accomplish a task, and our protagonist is left confused and wondering what the hell she's talking about or what's going on. Her response? ''Oh, I didn't tell you about that?''. It immediately became obvious that the creators didn't want you to overthink the plot or worry about the details. Just kill♥♥♥♥♥♥
Gameplay boils down to taking over bases, doing the unlocked missions (usually two, sometimes one) after taking control of the garisson, and finding collectibles. Collectibles are worth it, since they unlock weapon upgrades. Unfair? Not really, since you can, after freeing up a set amount of garissons, unlock maps in the store that display locations of collectibles on the map. Does that make collectibles ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥, since they TELL YOU where they are? Nah, my take on it is that they're set up so that you travel the island, encountering enemies and dragons along the way. It's not finding them that matters, its getting to them.
Even with the side quests its a short title, so you'd think it has very little to offer. In fact, it's pretty much a bite-size version of Far Cry 3, with neon and a ♥♥♥♥♥in' 80's soundtrack. The latter makes it worthwhile; the game has enough style and personality of its own to be a fruitful endeavour. It doesn't overstay its welcome, carries itself comedically and refuses to take anything it does seriously. If you've played Far Cry 3 before, odds are you've seen a lot of this already. But the new paint is good looking enough to warrant a second drive through the much smaller island of Blood Dragon. If you HAVEN'T played a Far Cry title before, ♥♥♥♥ing buy this already. For veterans its familiar territory, albeit with a different coat of paint. But for newbies, it's an enticingly retro foray into open world first person shooting. Whether a veteran or a newcomer, capturing bases stealthily is still as fun as ever. But now you get to do it to sounds of the 80's.

There was a lot of hate for this game and I see the reason why. People were expecting another "Call of Duty" first person shooter. I actually enjoyed this game. I bought it on sale because $10 is more reasonable than $40.

Why did I buy this game? Maybe because it was on sale and I wanted to see for myself just how bad this game was. But at around £10, I felt ripped-off. Everyone has already said what needs to be said about this game but I'm going to do it anyway.
This game is an on-rail shooter with no innovations. If the developers didn't want to do anything new, they should've just developed a generic FPS game (like Call of Duty) or something. At least that way, you're able to move freely and more effort would've been put into developing the game. "Stealth" sequences are just QTEs and there are even QTE sequences for entire levels, which you can auto-pass with the first "perk" you unlock. Yes, you can complete missions by doing nothing.
"Perks" and "abilities" are pretty much useless in this game and guns have very little differences. No light gun support and cutscenes are awful. Ripped straight out of the first three Rambo movies, it would've been better to just put the actual scenes from the movie itself as cutscenes because the voice-acting in this game is terrible. There are multiple bugs and glitches that causes the game to randomly crash and stop game progression (sort of). On one level, when I "moved" to the next section, there were no enemies. Because of that, I couldn't pass and threw a grenade at myself to start from the last checkpoint as oppose to restarting the level from the beginning.
The graphics are awful, the game looks like it was made in the early 90s. I don't demand the most beautiful, cutting-edge graphics in modern video games but since this game came out early this year, the graphics are way below average. Character models are some of the most laughable I've ever seen, and for some reason, John Rambo is the worst looking. He looks mentally deficient, like the puppet of Matt Damon in Team America. The trailer misrepresents the kind of game this is. This game is not a "John Rambo" experience. That's even a difficulty mode, the "hardest". Don't bother with it and just stick to Green Beret. The game will often "move" to sections where you're completely out in the open and can't cover, so you'll take loads of damage. That's why using Wrath Mode is very important in this game because during Wrath Mode, you heal when you kill enemies.
This game is so easy until the last mission. It's not even difficult, they just throw waves of enemies at you because the developers think that that's "challenging". You're going to die a lot and often duck for cover, with a cover system that doesn't even work (bullets often go through) and it's one of the most frustrating experiences ever in gaming (even on normal difficulty). That's why you should avoid John Rambo mode, the difficulty is the same except you get more points on higher difficulty and you get only one more try in John Rambo mode. You get three more tries in Green Beret mode, five more tries on normal and (I assume) seven more tries on easy (whatever easy and normal modes are called in this game). Because you die often in the last level (or last two levels) having only one more try after you die is not worth it. You'll have to restart the whole level so even if you get past one wave of enemies, the game throws even more at you, making the game feel endless. There are no achievements for playing the game on John Rambo mode anyway (or any incentives to do so) so don't. If you're looking for a challenge in this game, you're not going to find any because on higher dificulty, the AI is exactly the same.

This will most likely be updated to an upvote once the game is complete.
By that I mean, this seems to be a highly polished third or quarter of a game. There is a single boss fight - at the very end - and very little character development. By the end of the game, it feels as though they've just set up the table for where the real story is supposed to start. Even though I have 72 hours on record at the time of writing the review (which is not bad value), it seems that I somehow didn't get very far in the storytelling during that time.
Gameplay is smooth, polished and generally feels well calibrated. Environments are beautifully crafted, but seem less diverse, seeing as you spend your entire time in one city, spare a few side missions.
There are a lot of "monetization" efforts and bolted on, tacky extras. The seams between the real content, and the stuff that is merely there to make the publisher extra money, is so jarring that it could only have been designed by someone in a boardroom wearing a suit.
Overall, this game is about 40/60 recommended vs not recommended. The two main things that make it dip is, as stated: unnecessary bolted on crap that detracts from the main experience, and that it seems plotwise unfinished: not enough conspiracy heavy character and plot development to make it worthy of a Deus Ex game.
Granted, Human Revolution has left big shoes to fill.

Let me start by saying that I was extremely hyped for this game before release. My hopes were really high, especially when it comes to story. So when I say that main story was a bit disappointing for me, I want you to know, that it is still quite good. Just not all that I wished for.
For me, Deus Ex was always about the story. In "Human Revolution" we got engaging, complete and complex story, full of conspiracy, twists and interesting interactions with other characters. Unfortunately, the latest is missing in "Deus Ex: Mankind Divided". Sure, there is a lot of new characters, some of them are maybe even interesting, but there is no connection, no evolving relations like there was with characters in "Human Revolution". There is simply not enough time and not enough interactions for such connection to be created. Also, lack of "familiar faces" from previous game was a lowlight for me (I'm really eager for the DLC and reappearance of Pritchard).
Main plot feels a little rushed and incomplete. Sure, due to nature of presented events the "rushed" thing is understandable, but the story feels "small", especially when comparing to Human Revolution. It is still a good story though.
Fortunately, side quests and general world exploration provide entertaining addition to the main story and create very engaging world, worth being explored. Also, side quest chains present in the game are interesting stories on their own, definitely worth chasing. Also, due to multiple ways of completing them, Deus Ex: Mankind Divided has really good replay value.
Gameplay and controls are easy to master, especially when one had previous experience with Human Revolution. New augmentations are fun to play. I would even say that some of them make the game easier than originally expected (I'm looking at you, Remote Hacking) - it is still fun to play.
To wrap things up: Not as good as I hoped for, but it is a solid 8/10 in my opinion. Graphics are nice (even on medium), story is good, however I prefer side quests over the main story - both are worth recommending though. Overall Deus Ex: Mankind Divided is a good game. It has its flaws, sure, but the positive significantly outweighs the negative here.

An MMORPG is only as good as the guild you're in to a large extent. Lord of the Rings Online is a good MMO with a good Freemium model, in fact it was the first hugely successful Freemium model and several other games have taken queues from it. I think of all Freemium models, LOTRO did it the best. The story is engaging and has you crisscrossing over the paths of the Fellowship across Middle Earth. The zones alone are well worth it for the big lore nerds out there. If you can find a good guild, this game has a lot to offer, but it also falls victim to the same shortcomings of all MMOs.
Is it worth playing? If you're a Lord of the Rings fan looking for an MMORPG, absolutely. If you're looking for an MMORPG that does something hugely different, move along, this does nothing groundbreaking.

As a veteran of MMOs (and MUDs before that) I would have to recommend this game for several reason.
-F2P: Its actually free to play. The RMT (real money trade) store items are mostly cosmetic. There are some that effect gameplay convenience wise. However, the RMT currency (Turbine Points) can be also earned in game in many different ways. Basically, the game gives you RMT currency as a side result of playing.
-The Community. The community is not the typical MMO trollfest. MOST players you come across are more than willing to lend a hand, give advice or even (sometimes) free items etc. They are very friendly and generally tend to help the new players out.
-Social MMO. Despite this game having boatloads of grindy combat like any other MMO, there are many  unique social aspects to this game. Making/playing your own musical instruments in a band, player/guild housing etc.
-Massive world. The gameworld in this is rather big. While certain areas are locked out until you purchase the expansion, there are equivalent zones for the free (budget) player.
-Customer Support is very ... human. And tends to be helpful with the player rather than absolute sticklers to policy.
-Mounted Combat/Legendary Weapons/Raids/Dungeons/Crafting/Typical MMO stuff etc., etc.,
CONS:
-I had performance issues on my budget laptop. The game can get very laggy with xpacs and infusion of players.
-WoW ruined any mmo without flying mounts ><
TL:DR give it a spin if you like mmos. While it doesn't break any new ground in the genre it is a solid game with unique social aspects.

I’m playing with an increasingly miserable lvl 58 elf huntress.
She wants to see all of Middle Earth, but she won’t. Because I am broke.
I feel like writing this review in caps lock and yelling at the top of my lungs “pay to win pay to win pay to win”.
Middle Earth is beautiful. Beginnings are sweet as you’re not engaged in battles straight away. You start in Eriador, and exact place depends on which race you chose to play with. Crafting is soothing, exploring is fun, everything looks amazing. When you get a horse, things get a lot easier and you find yourself immersed into the world and enjoying it so much. It leaves you curious for other parts of Middle Earth and you want to level up to enjoy them all. Music is great too and fits every scenery beautifully.
But then, around levels 20-30 you realize you need to purchase a quest pack to play the next area on the map. That's fine, so you do that, still being into the game. Then you grind grind grind, until you face the same thing again. So you buy another area. And so on.
Thing is, I didn’t even mind purchasing packs to see more. What I really did mind though, is how boring and repetitive quests became while levelling in parallel became increasingly harder and frustrating. I'm starting to think the best way to play this game is getting a horse and just riding like there's no tomorrow until you reach Mordor. Noro lim Asfaloth, noro lim!
Unless on top of all those purchases you want to buy experience tomes. Thanks Turbine, but no thanks.
Community used to be better too, but I’m guessing a lot of people left for which I can’t really blame them.
Also in walks my biggest regret, and that’s starting my toon on a non RP server which is extremely boring and has very little activity. However, if you do the same mistake and want to try another server with the same toon, Turbine offers you to transfer it for 20 €. What a surprise, I think I'll get a heart attack.

Still, there were times when I was so desperate I was willing to put all that aside and give it another shot. Then server started crashing. Guess it’s not meant to be, Lotro.

It's a decent enough MMORPG when you start out. The problem arises when you start to want things like auction house slots and the removal of the extremely hindering gold cap. Almost all of the things you would expect from a game like this have been locked behind a pay wall or restricted to paying subscribers. Turbine Points are the in-game store's currency and are almost essential when playing this game, and they can either be collected by completing "deeds" (tasks which require hours upon hours of grinding) or bought with real money. This is the largest flaw the game has, because after a certain point everything becomes blocked off except for a few main storyline quests.
I'm sure this game was great when it was first released, but now that it has gone "F2P" (which is almost a lie) everything revolves around getting Turbine Points to progress. By the time you've collected enough for one small thing, the enjoyment has been ruined.
My advice: Play for a bit if you must, but don't spend too much time farming TP, you'll just regret it. Also, If you're considering spending ANY money on this game, please don't. Look at the bigger picture, and go buy a complete experience elsewhere.

It's exactly what it says on the tin. It's a dating sim and a clicker/idle game. Nothing more nothing less. So let's just get down to it.
Pros:
+ Gameplay, while inherently simple, is fairly interesting with the addition of the dating sim elements, and a time block management. So you need to train up stats and earn money to actually be competent at wooing the girls, instead of just mad clicking skillz (autoclicker). The game also makes it clear that it is only storing your idle activities for up to 7 days. So you can schedule ahead if you're that type of person.
+ Clear requirements for getting the girls. So the game has you wooing the ladies in a couple of "stages", and each stage has very clear requirements, like needing to give her a drink as a gift, or going on two dates with her. It makes progression feel special in its own little way and does just enough to stave off monotony. That said, this system also comes with its own drawbacks.
+ The girls are cute, and the way they get introduced to you can be mildly funny, that said don't expect much from the personality department. They're archetypes and that's that. Their dialogue can also give you a chuckle or two though.
+You can prestige ASAP and the speed boosts from that prestige reset is nothing to sneeze at. Way more generous with this than most clicker games are.
+ It's free and everyone likes free games.
Cons:
- So that drawback with the requirements system? Well, the requirements are gigantic. There is a huge leap in requirements from stage to stage and it gets kind of ridiculous and grindy because of that. I know you can leave the game to idle so that it grinds up stats and money for you, and that's the point, but seeing the numbers go from around 100 to 8000 in one stage transition can be very discouraging. In fact the clicking requirements will get so huge that you probably will need mad clicking skillz (Autoclicker) in the end, or you know you can just leave it for a week and maybe you'll have finished it all.
- Another big problem is that the game will only give you idle clicks on the girls if you fulfill a stats that they like. So girls who like Buff guys will not get idle clicks if your Buff stat isn't up to par. It's never explained in the game so you might miss it and go back to your game after a couple of days expecting a full heart but getting jack all instead. The game also doesn't make how you go about fulfilling these stats requirements. So you don't know if you need to have like 8 Buff or just 3 Buff for the girl to start getting them idle clicks. It does look like that you just need at least 2 or 3 though to get the idle clicks. Which leads to another problem...
- Idle clicks can never be improved. So yeah you have 3 Buff and you get 1 idle click per second for the girl, and that's it. Even if you have 16 Buff you still only get 1 idle click per second. So then what's the point of raising the skills? Well just to meet the stage requirements that's all. That's kinda where the game starts to wilt, when it becomes grindy like that, and it doesn't take too long for it to get to that point. Also, the prices of gifts are ridiculous. Again, huge leaps from item to item, which only makes the grinding waaaay more apparent and tedious.
Overall, I do like the game though, and I can recommend this to anyone looking for a lighthearted anime clicker. It can get tedious after a while, but it's one of those games that you can just leave and come back to whenever you feel like it. Its mechanisms work quite well together and there does not seem to be any major bugs or issues from my experiences. It's also still in Early Access, so the game might be improved later through patches and updates, and for an Early Access title, it's very functional. I have not encountered any major bugs or issues so far (which is probably not that far but eh).

Wow ... there is a a LOT of Hate for this game out there, but I dont think it deserves it. First off this is NOT an Epic Story Lined RPG/FPS MEGA MILL Game .... yeah, and I dont think it was suppose to be either. If you have watched the Rambo movies then you should have a pretty good idea of what to expect, minimal ... cheesy dialogue and excessive explosions. What you do in this game is play all the action scenes from the first 3 movies (4th film is not in this, though I wish it were). It IS a Rail Shooter, to those that may want more of an example, this game reminds me a lot of the Movie based rail games back in the late 80s and early 90s, I remember playing an Arcade version of Star Wars that was the same way.
You still have to take cover and shoot and there are some QTEs, you can get a perk in the game to make QTEs impossible to fail but you wont get any points for not doing them, with or with out the perk. A lot of peps hate that the perk is in there, my advice, if the idea of not being able to fail a QTE bothers you, then dont use the damn perk, its very simple. The combat is fun, the QTEs are fun and ... well your playing as Rambo and blowing everything in the game world up ... what else do you want out of a Rambo game?
Is it perfect? Of course not, but its fun.
Again, your gonna see and hear a lot of hate for this game and some peps are very good at hating everything, so I suggest you watch game play videos online with no commentary, come in to this game with out looking for the bad, because if that is your focus, then your gonna find it, dont care what game your playing.
If you like Rambo, and you want to play as Rambo and blow things up ... well pretty much everything up, then I can not recommend it more. If you dont like Rambo, rail shooters, the 80s or playing a game just for the fun of it, then stay away. This is not for you. To everyone else, have a blast :D

Sometimes simplistic, with puzzles that won't have you racking the brains for hours on end... But that's not the point. This is an adventure and a story, and put together with some of the most charming visuals and music/sounds that you will find. This is a game that draws you into its world (and it's a beautiful world), where you really feel a part of it.
Intriguingly you control two characters - brothers - one with each side of your controller. Occasionally I found myself getting confused over which I was controlling but you soon get the hang of it. And you need to, as both characters are required to progress past the numerous puzzles often involving climbing and jumping, with one character holding open a crank to allow the other past who, in turn, will help the first through. There are only a few times where you really have to think about what to do and how to get past the next puzzle, so it's not taxing but there's enough thought required that you keep going on.
But it's not really the gameplay that's the main draw; it's the story and the interactions of the brothers with the world and characters around them. Ogres, trolls, other people, dogs - each could be friend or foe, but nobody is extraneous. It really feels that, on your long journey, you're playing a brief role in other people's lives. They each have their own story, glimpsed so quickly, but it's enough to really bring the world to life. In many cases this leads to a very short mini-quest associated with one of the achievements, and it's not always obvious, so it pays to keep an eye on everything going on around you.
There are those games that are not just played but experienced. This is one of them, and, for me, it's utterly unforgettable.

Ubisoft packs a punch with the epic 80s action movie video game. Far Cry 3: Blood Dragon pushes the bounds of traditional fps with epic dialogue, brilliant combat, hilarious cinematics, and an over the top story.
You play as Rex, a Mark IV cyborg that is sent on a mission to clear out some hostiles. Upon arriving you discover the mission is a lot more complex than you originally assumed. Your partner Spider is killed right at the start and it’s up to you to get revenge and ultimately save the world. Dr. Darling is your female guide offering you more than just her brains. Sloan an evil super-villain has concocted a serum from the Blood Dragons that turns people into zombies. He’s going to unleash this concoction upon the world if you do not stop him.
Far Cry 3: Blood Dragon starts off with you flying into an blaze of glory only to end the same way. The campaign is ridiculously short, unless you go out an complete all other objectives. It took me 5 hours to complete the entire game (get every TV/Video, complete all missions, capture all the bases, kill all 12 animals, and upgrade every weapon). If you just ran the campaign I could imagine you completing it in under an hour and a half easy. There are about five actual missions, the one you play with Spider, the one where you blow up the dam, the one where you kill the scientist, the one where you complete the temples challenge, and the final one where you kill Sloan. The actual game takes place on an open-world map making you run between missions, but this is not a problem as you are a Mark IV and can sprint faster than the cars can drive, fall off cliffs without taking damage, and teleport to any of the captured garrisons.
The combat makes you a complete and total hero, even on the hardest difficulty you will still be able to run into a room full of people and slaughter them like a wolf amongst lambs. You have a healthbar, but you are able to heal yourself without medpacks. For combat, missions, and secrets you get CP which levels Rex. Each level offers Rex a new ability (usually increased health and self-repair), but every now and then you get a special something else thrown in. If you complete missions and find secrets you can upgrade your guns in special ways making yourself even more heroic than before. There are eight weapons (A.J.M. 9, Fzertron, Kobracon, Galleria 1991, Bow, Terror 4000, Flamer, and KillStar) and two explosives (Grenades, and C400). The first four weapons have upgrades, the last four do not. You will find yourself using different weapons over others, but based on the nature of the game you will probably want to go for the loudest guns you can find.
Far Cry 3: Blood Dragon is an epic first person shooter that brings the 80s action hero genre to life. It feels like you are playing Arnold Schwarzenegger from Commando as you blast through hundreds of cyborg soldiers, wild animals, dragons, and zombies. The game is coupled with a hilarious soundtrack, amazing cut-scenes, epic dialogue, and downright awesome explosions. You will not find yourself bored while playing this game, so make sure you’re ready to become an epic action hero. Because Far Cry 3: Blood Dragon is such a short game I would be wary paying full price if you are not 100% sure you want this title. This game is a great game if you can get it on sale.
Pros:
+Character levels which make you considerably stronger.
+Weapon customization which allows you to fully kit out guns making them even more destructive.
+Fast travel which allows you to move quickly across the map.
+Items you can buy from the store that reveal all the secrets on the map, saving you from having to actually look.
+Epic combat system with awesome melee as well as ranged.
+Lots of different enemies that keep you interested.
+Dragons obviously…
+Great graphics, scenery, and map design.
+Open-world Environment (I personally do not like open-world FPS, but for those who do this is a pro).
+Great dialogue, music, and cutscenes
+You do not need Far Cry 3 in order to play this game.
Cons:
-You have very little control over saving until after the first two missions, which is incredibly annoying.
-Finding some of the animals is near impossible (also the stingray is classified as a civilian?)
-You will spend more time traveling between objectives than you will actually playing the game.

Trine 2 is a puzzle/adventure platforming game as ingenious as it is stunning. If you like puzzles, thinking outside of the box, and... bopping goblins? You will probably fall in love with Trine 2 in a heartbeat!
Below is a list of attributes pertaining to Trine 2, and some personal opinion in regards to how they did.
I'll give Trine 2 a cookie for being relatively unique compared to most other games. The execution is fine, though the game does leave you feeling like there should be more. Additionally, some aspects of the plot can be seen coming a mile away. Fortunately, there's at least one or two good twists in store. For the sake of spoilers though, I won't disclose them here. The story of Trine 2's is not one to be taken seriously.
Of course, you weren't looking to play this for the story, were you?
Earning a few extra points for its fairly clever implementation of skills and the three heroes, Trine 2 really lets you play the game in your own style, be it through finesse, sheer force, or stuffing boxes into sacred places they clearly don't belong! If you get stuck at some point or confused, the narrator offers some clues on how to proceed. Compared to most games that babysit you along, this is much more preferrable.
Admittedly, the controls do take a little getting used to, and even Normal Difficulty can be downright brutal if you're new to the game. Thankfully, a lot of the achievements (if you're OCD like I am) can be obtained without getting your rear end handed to you. Some are possible right at the main menu! *Hint, hint.*
Trine 2 is outrageously beautiful. Beautiful to the point of losing sight of your character on the screen! ... Seriously, this happened to me playing it. But that's okay because Trine 2 is a literal slideshow of eye candy and scenic splendor. Rewarding to watch just in its own right. Being able to play in it, let alone interact with it, is an added bonus.
Perhaps the nicest part about its shiny graphics is that you don't have to cash in on your life insurance policy to make a system capable of running it. Even with a simple dual-core PC, Trine 2 runs magnificently at high detail.
Normally, I detest games that emphasize graphics since they usually have horrible gameplay and/or story about as in-depth as a piece of cardboard. Trine 2's storyline isn't the greatest, but it makes up for it in its unique and fluid style, gameplay, as well as the lovely panoramic scenes the game immerses you into. It's a game that isn't trying to sell you some epic story or brand-spanking new mechanic... It's just fun to play!

Deus Ex: Mankind Divided is almost everything I wanted in a sequel to Human Revolution. The graphics aren't earth-shattering, but are gorgeous in their own right. Aside from a few stutters here and there, I was able to run the game at 1080p 60fps with the recommended specs. The gameplay has been polished to a beautiful sheen, with multiple violent and nonviolent, stealthy and obvious paths through every mission. There is only one boss in the game, but there are multiple ways to deal with him this time around, a great relief from the horrendous bosses of Human Revolution.
The choices you make matter one way or another, and the environment and NPCs react dynamically as a result. The main hub of Prague is jaw-droppingly detailed, with a seemingly endless supply of nooks and crannies for you to explore and dig through. While the main story missions aren't a marked improvement from Human Revolution's, the side mission really shine as some of the most creative and intriguing ones in the series. All of the old augmentations are back, along with a few new ones that are completely over-the-top and gratuitous. The voice acting is hit and miss with the side-characters, but Adam Jensen takes the spotlight once again, with a slightly more affected tone adding a lot more depth to his character.
The only area the game disappoints in is with the story as a whole. Out of all the Deus Ex games, this is easily the weakest story that covers the least amount of ground. Nothing really gets accomplished, and the story just abruptly ends without really resolving any of the overarching goals and problems set forth. Also, instead of finding a way to encorporate your ending choice in Human Revolution, the game just kind of ignores the idea that there was a choice to begin with and never really mentions it again. It does this by taking place 2 years after Human Revolution's ending, which is a true shame considering how much important events happen in that time.
And yes, the microtransactions are the biggest load of ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥t you can possibly imagine. There was never once pressure to buy anything though, and supplies and Praxis come at a steady enough stream that I never felt the need to buy more.
Avoid the multiplayer at all costs.

Yet another example of a nice, creative indie game with an extreme lack of players. There are usally about 3~7 populated servers.
8.5/10
There are 10 modes and 10 maps. In other words... One mode for one map. You can't play other game mode with said map. Every one of them is designed for their specific game mode. Everyone of them has their own (nice, happy) BGM too.
Gunplay: You have one rifle, shotgun, sniper, RPG, grenades and flamethrower.
Unless you die easily, you will be forced to use your rifle. The other weapons have a reasonably big lack of ammo (the game has ammo regen) while your rifle will have 200+ bullets. I didn't notice any bullet drop, but there is a max distance. When you are way too far apart, you won't deal damage with any weapon other than your sniper.

TL;DR at bottom
This game is great if you're playing alone and is a solid choice if you're in the market for a sub $20 shooter.
THIS GAME IS ABSOLUTELY AMAZING IF YOU'RE PLAYING WITH FRIENDS, THE MORE THE MERRIER!!!
...I mean it though seriously, this game is soooooooo much fun with friends!!!!!
As far as strengths and weaknesses go, heres my list:
Pros:
-All maps are fun and super creative, offering different "gamemodes" like CTF. TDM. DM, King of the Hill, and... soccer?
Yea seriously theres soccer/fusball, it's pretty damn cool! Also in one of the game modes titled "Deeo Freeze" the goal is to defrost a toy T-Rex with your flamethrower!
-Artstyle is super fun and has this certain air to it that just makes me sooo happy whenever I play!!!
-Playing with friends is the greatest thing ever, this game feels like it was designed for it!
-No unlockables so everyone is super balanced, and it just comes down to your overall skill level
-Super casual, if you're looking for a game to sit back and relax with for a couple of hours, this is definitely for you!
-Controls are super snappy and responsive, and I'm playing with a wireless mouse and keyboard so that's saying something! (I can't even tell if there's input lag or not)
Cons:
-Might get a little repetitive if playing alone as there is nothing to work towards in this game due to the aforementioned lack of any sort of unlockables.
-Noone plays this game, the servers are always empty it seems :( (Atleast that's how it is here in Canada)
-The soccer/fusball game mode could be super fun, but it's just too finicky, the servers aren't mature enough to handle the ball. Also the lack of static cover is kindof bothersome.
Now I'm going to list some improvements that could be had for this game (I hope you're listening Virtual Basement)
-UPGRADES/UNLOCKABLES: This game is sooo much fun and super balanced, but I feel as if this game just needs a bit more variety. Whether it be costumes or new guns (hopefully both) it could give this game that extra something that it desperately needs. The guns could be done in a TF2 fashion where they are the same type of gun but with wildly varieing stats (ALSO PLEASE GIVE US ROCKET JUMPING IT WOULD BE AMAZING IN A AGME LIKE THIS)!!!!
-SINGLE PLAYER: It would be very cool to see a story based campaign where there is a war going on over the playroom or something cool like that. This could also cater to those gamers that like single player games more.
-ADVERTISING: Yea, I know, I know, it cost alot... but this game could be soooooo awesome with a larger player base. You could even just contact some big youtuber or something and ask them to play your game if you give them a free copy,  it would work and im sure the current playerbase would appreciate more people to play with :)
TL;DR: This game is amazing! While I don't have many hours on it, it doesn't mean i haven't enjoyed every one of those hours. This game is just such a good time, and even more so with a group of friends. If you're not sure about this game just keep an eye on it, I'm sure it'll be worth you're time ;)

Brothers is a remarkable game for two reasons - the dual-character control system, and the thoughtful plot.
The former, in which you use a single pad to control the two titular brothers, seems at first to be fiddly. I was surprised how quickly I adapted though, and it allows the game to present the player with some very clever and satisfying puzzles.
The latter only really comes into its own later in the game but is well worth the wait. Throughout though, the world and its story is presented by means of the environment and incidental detail, illustrating an unusual and colourful fantasy setting. It manages this without a single line of dialogue, which is all the more impressive.

I bought it on summer sale back in the 2015. It was not worth of it.
Game begins with long training which is boring, and after that appears sequence of you and your squad riding in Humvee, with Megadeth's Symphony Of Destruciton being played by driver. I like the song, but hey the ride is way toooo long. It made me feel more bored than train ride to Black Mesa in first Half-Life game.
And this is main problem of Operation Flashpoin:RR. This game is just boring.
Every time when firefight happens, you just smoothly move from cover to cover and take down enemies. When you get hit, you will use fix-everything medkit. You also need to watch over you team's health-but it's just more of pressing "e" on your teammates.
Now let's talk about shooting; Guns have a good models. Sounds are far from being perfect, but the aren't that bad. Recoil is kinda... weird. I just don't have right words do describe it... It feels so... light...unrealistic. You just don't fell how the gun kick, and how it "sings". So; models of guns are great-but recoil and sounds are not.
But let's talk about the firefight, which is of course a core of this game. Enemies in early part of the game are talibian fighters, armed with Aks and PKPs. They also use granades, but most of fights happen on a range, so it is not a real threat. Every firefight looks boring-Talibians supress you with fire, you wait until they reload- and than you just pick 'em off when they try to shoot you. In later part of the game you engage North Korean soldiers, but rule is the same.
WAIT! You can give orders to your team! But this is just saying where they should go, so it is not worth of mentioning too, according to fact, that you can complete missions even without them. You just need to remember about saying "follow me" or "man that vechicle" or scripts won't launch.
Maybe i should mention plot, but it is just not worth of it. There are no any characters that I really liked, and tbh I remember only black Seregant, cuz he is swearing all the time. Duh, I don't even remember his name.
AFTER ALL-I do not reccomend it, unless you are a die-hard "realistic shooters" fan. Main issue with this release, is a fact that it's slow and boring. And everything takes just too long. Developers also wasted opportunity of making squad command a real thing, becouse giving orders could have been a core of game, while it is only a unimportant and un-enjoyable feature.

admittedly I write this without having played any other game in the far cry series, so maybe the experience would be different had I more familiarity with the mechanics and general gameplay of far cry.  that being said, this game totally sucked.  its biggest drawback was a technical failure or glitch (it seems hard for me to believe that the game had actually been designed this way) where the autosave didn't seem to function.  at all.  I played through three sections of the game, and every time I started the game back up, I had to restart with the same (AWFUL) tutorial section.  what made it worse was that the gameplay past the tutorial wasn't even much fun.  the game encourages you to use stealth, yet makes it very challenging to find a path you can take undetected (keep in mind that this is in the very first gameplay area).  once detected by one enemy, every other enemy in the area is alerted to your presence, forcing you into an open gunfight (despite having just trained you in the art of stealth).  if you, like me, decide to retry the area so as not to be detected, you have to start all over from the opening cutscene and terrible tutorial.  while the game would not let me manually save during the first area, I hoped that it had auto-saved for me after I reached the fourth section (a "protect a guy while he does a thing" section, which are never fun).  nope!  next time I started the game up, it was back to the opening cutscene and (did I mention AWFUL) tutorial.  there was some humor in the game that I enjoyed, and while I thought the graphical style missed the mark of what they seemed to be aiming for (in particular, there was an omnipresent neon haze that washed the life out of everything), overall I thought the setting of the game seemed appealing.  too bad the actual gameplay leaves nothing to be enjoyed.

This installment might create mixed feelings, but what it does deliver on is GTA content, regardless of you agreeing or not.
First off, the free roaming might feel more limited, however you get more detail on the fly. GTA: San Andreas had a wider area to offer, but with limited area to roam (albeit still a big area), you´ll definitely get more bang for the buck. GTA IV? Yeah, it´s probably on line with that franchise, albeit even there, might be smaller.
Missions are pretty good, and you WILL get challenged. No worries. The storyline makes good sense, and it doesn´t throw you off in the middle of nowhere like Vice City and especially GTA IV could at some points, losing some ends here and there. That sucked.
First-person mode. Yes. You heard me. That´s seriously an awesome idea!
What sucks? The police. In single player mode they have been tuned up so high that any small mistake will have you wasted in mere seconds. In online mode (which you´ll probably be playing the most anyway), they have been tuned a bit down to the levels of GTA IV police, albeit a bit better AI. They have brains - trust me.
You get bang for the buck. However the poop detail: You are facing a huge price. Sadly. Otherwise, if you can get it for cheap, you are looking at an awesome game.

DLC Quest takes the concept of DLC and skewers it with satire. While it is a short game (complete with speedrun achievements), it packs a fair amount of platforming fun into its two short campaigns, DLC Quest and Life Freemium or Die. In both, you must (eventually with the requisite DLC) jump and explore the nooks and cranies of the world to find coins to purchase DLC. There is a bit of Metroidvania imbedded here and it displays it proudly with its solid platforming mechanics.
There is a light story to each of the main quests: in one you must save Princess Macguffin from Bad Guy, and in the sequel you must save the villagers from a rampaging monster. Really, they're both flimsy and funny excuses for you to run around and collect coins for DLC.  Combat does not exist aside from a few sequences, and death only visits your character upon touching spiked pit traps. While Super Meat Boy it is not, the platforming is challenging enough for die hard completionists and speedrunners to enjoy.
The game doesn't have much lasting appeal unless you want to hunt down every missing coin or you have a burning desire to tackle the speed runs. That said, for its low price,  DLC Quest will offer a fun look at what happens when DLC goes too far.

I have only played the demo version that included only the first tower long time ago and ever since then I wanted to get my hand on the full game.
I really liked the graphic, the isometric layout, the puzzles, the unique mechanics of thirst and hunger and the look of the weird monsters.
In Mystic Towers You play as a wizard called Baron Baldric who is tasked to destroy 12 towers that are responsible for the monsters attacking Rimm village.
In this game, you must find in each tower a generator bomb which is the only thing that is capable of destroying the monster generator which is located on the 3rd floor inside each tower in order to stop from the monsters respawning after they are killed and then kill all the remaining monsters in the tower.
While you explore the towers, you will find offensive and utility spells which you will need to conserve for the right moment, for example using the offensive magic against the monsters to kill them is better to be done only after the generator is destroyed, also it is better to save the healing spell in case you will get poisoned.
Also, You will have to manage your hunger and thirst levels by finding scattered food and water basins.
The game is split into 6 apprentice level towers which are straightforward and let you understand the game mechanics.
The other 6 are wizard towers which are more challenging - you will have to use everything you have learned so far to beat them all.
The game is really fun and I recommend it to everyone.

You play as a 'zany' old wizard who randomly farts, picks his nose, etc, about 1 time in 20 when you want to cast a spell. That's not so bad, maybe even a bit charming. Supposedly there's puzzles and challenge, but really this game is just about balancing which tedious mechanic you want to prioritize before you starve -- Do you want to
A) Spend 4 minutes killing a single common monster
B) Spend 10 minutes backtracking for food / water
C) Push EVERY SINGLE VASE AND TILE around in case the thing you need is hidden under thiiiiiiis one?
So, there was this food on the floor while I was walking around on the 2nd floor of a tower. This game doesn't let you eat when you're not hungry, so I ignored it. I wound up doing that a lot. I was starting to panic a bit, because I was starting to run out of food, and it was taking longer and longer to backtrack for leftovers each time. I stopped playing when I finally found the key I needed underneath one of the many piles of food I had 'left behind for later', back on the 2nd floor...

I played Human Revolution 3 times through, the last of which included The Missing Link.  For regular content, each playthrough took me 27 hours (stealth pathfinder style).  I'm sure the FPS method takes a little less time.
I am on hour 30 of Mankind Divided and I'm not done yet.  Am I close? Probably.
The point is nobody has been exploited the way the reviews dictate.  We got just as much (if not more) content in MD as HR for the same price.  The only difference is that the story arc (lol) is longer in MD.
So you didn't get to see the final ending.  They split the Hobbit into 3 movies (whether you like the movies is inconsequential here), and fans said "3 movies!? AWESOME!".  The worst part of the split was having to wait for it, but it was always worth the time and money.
Fans of the series were not short-changed, they were given a game every bit as immersive and exciting as the last, only this time we have a guaranteed sequel.  Also, 30 hours in and I still don't know/need to know what microtransactions are offered, they don't matter...

This game made me somewhat conflicted about my impression of it - on the one hand, I like the whole Deus Ex universe (been enjoying it since the very first game in 2000) and I enjoyed the continuation of the story as well as the improved graphical effects (compared to the DX:HR), on the other - there are way, WAY too many drawbacks. The environments/level design felt pretty "cramped", there's not much location variety, you still can't do much with NPCs other than going through their very basic "main story progression" or "pointless fluff" dialogues (can't do much "romancing" as in other RPG games by Bioware/CDPR), there's not much "choices" to be made which affects the story (well, there's actually one major choice you're forced to make, the rest are pretty much irrelevant), the developers underpromised on the whole "DX12" part - yes, they have finally enabled this mode after many weeks, however by this time it is pretty much irrelevant for vast majority of players. Not to mention the ending was pretty abrupt and what's even worse - once again I was forced to watch "end credits" with a bunch of irrelevant (to me) names and photos of the developers of the game (and random people who were somehow related to it), without the ability to skip those (I just used Task Manager to force-close the game after about a couple of minutes). Come on, guys - let ME have a control of MY own PC, if I want to skip all this narcissistic fluff you put in "end credits" - let me easily and instantly do just that.
Long story short, the overall experience with this game was pretty... annoying and I'm glad I didn't pay a full price for it and neither should you. If you haven't played it yet, just wait for it to go on sale for $5-10 or so.

I'd like to preface this review by saying that this was a gift from AMD. I will, however, be considering this game from a $60 value point-of-view. Also, this is the first Deus Ex game I've played.
I liked it. A lot. It left me wanting more, clearly begging for a sequel. The gameplay and graphics are outstanding. However, I was disappointed how the game ended. Not only was it too short to justify the price tag, it didn't tie up any loose ends and hardly answered any questions.
This is one of those games that likes to reward you for going out of your way to unlock new areas. Exploration and hacking is encouraged in DE:MD. While the hacking may get old for some, I became quite good at it and didn't bother me as much once I upgraded my hacking augs.
There's a crafting system in this game. You can make useful things like health packs, biocells and automatic hacking tools. I never crafted a single thing. Instead, I used all my crafting parts to upgrade weapons. I had accumulated an abundance of the craftables just from exploring.
I also only used one "experimental aug" during my first play-through. The aug that allows you to slow-down time is useful when a cut scene ends abruptly and you need to take out three guys. Other than that, these augmentations seemed over-powered and, in most situations, unnecessary. I liked the idea of being able to change-up your play style according to the augs you select, but I really didn't think I would ever use them. I was sort of upset that Jensen is 90% machine yet doesn't have a flashlight.
As far as graphics, this game is beautiful. The worlds are so filled-out and gloomy. It's magnificent. Very rarely did I feel like I was confined to a small map. The world really isn't that big, but there's so much to explore it didn't really matter.
I think I only had two boss battles. One was a side mission, the other I cut short using a "beat-the-game" item I found a few minutes prior. All around very disappointing and anti-climatic. I stocked-up in case I actaully need to battle some OP augmented dude but instead I seldom dug into my inventory unless it was to drop one of my useless health packs in exchange for ammo.
Not worth the $60. Maybe I would pay $40 for it. I love it, but Square Enix could have done SO much more.
TL;DR: Awesome game; not worth the price.

Taking all of the above into consideration there is actually quite a good game in there. Yes its on rails, but its not that bad. There is quite a lot of depth to the game that some reviews did not mention because they were too busy telling us how bad everything is.
The cover system whilst taken right out of the likes of time crisis etc, does some quite good things. Hide behind a box and the enemy will shoot the box out leaving you with no cover, there is also quite a good system where by when being shot at by multiple enemies its advisable to wait for them to reload before you pop out of cover and take them down. Of course you can't also wait because  your cover may be getting destroyed affording you no time to wait for reloads.
You can also make choices such as killing or disarming cops rather than killing them, Totalbiscuit touched on this all be it he mocked it at least he noticed it so good on him.
The graphics whilst not earth shattering are not of PS2 quality and If you think that then please go back and play a PS2. There is lots of destruction especially when you get to fly the helicopter and "Blow Stuff Up" the buildings all blow up nicely and in a seemingly non scripted way and catch fire, enemies lose limbs and its very satisfying cutting them down with the guns mounted on the helicopter.
QTE's well what can you say? they do have a place in some games and I sense that they were added because of the on rails type of game play. Again some reviews have mentioned the perk you can get where you can avoid doing the QTE's as the game will do them for you, but what they did not mention was, that  whilst the game does them for you, it does them in the worst way possible as in you will never get a perfect timing hit. You can also still do the QTE's yourself with the perk and get them perfect often affording you a little more time to shoot the incoming nade or take up cover quicker or just avoid a mortar but you will still lose some life. So yes whilst the perk will do the QTE's for you its really only just getting you through the game its far more beneficial to do them yourself.
The game is also fairly hard in some places, sometimes due to bad design but more often its because its just hard. Of course the better you are the less hard it will be for you, I find it hard at times so this is just my observation.
If you like time crisis, good old fashioned guns and action with no need to worry about your path and clear objectives then you will like this game. There are lots of little things you will notice and think ah ok thats quite cool.
I am enjoying this game and I also think there is a lot of replay value to it. For people wanting a light gun experience you can use a wii controller but this is not supported by the game, however google is your friend.
Its not that bad IMHO if you get to try it you will be surprised.

One of the worst games ever. No joke. Rambo is an awkward experience with plenty of QTEs, short levels, frustrating difficulty spikes and/or checkpoints, moronic perks/skills and, well, it's just no fun. If you replace 'fun' with 'frustrating' then you absolutely have a good point. And I would agree with you all the way, no arguing here.
Rambo himself looks like♥♥♥♥♥♥ he looked like the melting man from the Robocop movie. The levels on the other hand look actually decent. You can clearly see it was done by seperate teams. The voice acting was ripped directly from the movies, as you can tell by the poor quality of it all.
As far as gameplay goes, this is an on-rail shooter, but without the light guns. And with a mouse.
Making headshots with your mouse is ridiculously easy, but reloading takes ages and it has the mechanic that games like Gears Of War use. So press the reload button at the right time and you'll reload your gun with double the ammo, if you fail it will jam your gun and if you do it the normal way you'll reloaded normally. It doesn't work a game like this, because well, it's about shooting people. I don't have time to try and reload at the exact right time when there are several enemies shooting at me, and staying behind cover doesn't do sh*t when one is still standing on the side of it, shooting at you.
Checkpoints are random. Sometimes it saves right after a scene, sometimes before. Sometimes it saves right before a big fight when you're extremely low on health and the first bullet that hits you kills you. Fine. Just restart the checkpoint then (you can retry 5 times per level). But what's this. The exact same thing happens, again ! And within a minute you wasted 5 continues. At least give a bit of health, or let enemies hit you less frequent. Sure, maybe I suck but that's not the point. Why add a mechanic that doesn't even do what it's supposed to do ? Who thought of this game in the first place ?
The QTEs are too fast, I had to actually look up my keyboard to see where the keys are supposed to be. I use the WASD keys automatically and never really think about what I'm actually pressing. This game made me feel like someone who just starts working with computers. Great job !
I'm going to stop now, I don't want to waste any more time on this game. I've already done that enough.

This isn't Rambo the Photo Editor, or Rambo the Audio Mixer, this is Rambo: the VIDEO GAME!  Its on rails, this is Rambo!  Rambo doesnt wander around willy nilly looking for things to kill, all a Rambo does is KILL KILL KILL so on rails kinda works, check youtube for gameplay videos to see if it is a good fit first....   On rails shooters are not a bad thing, most games just trick you into thinking their open world because you press forward but that is just a trick!!!  Look at Splinter Cell Blacklist it is so heavily scripted with walk cycles, it might as well be on rails.  This game has ALOT of QTE's, some levels are all QTE's but dont worry their easy, and the first time you level up there is a perk called "No QTE fails", so its no big deal.
When first starting the game you are at Rambo's funeral, then the worst guy ever to give a funeral speech says, "I'm Glad Rambo is dead".  What a jerk, they couldnt find someone else?   That is pretty depressing is there any other way to start a game without the death of the main character and the US military mocking him?  Turns out Rambo faked his own death.  Then at the end you are in Afghanistan, at first I thought Rambo was helping the terrorists by getting revenge and killing all the US military people for being jerks.  But it turns out Rambo is fighting Russians for some reason.  Was that why he faked his death?  Im not sure and it's never explained really in the game at least, maybe in the movie it is.
The gameplay is kind of cheap and unfair during the last mission.  There are guys that toss grenades from behind cover that you cant dodge you have to shoot them out of the air.  Sounds easy right, but its not easy when there are helicopters, mounted machine guns on jeeps, and ten thousand other things trying to kill you.  Those grenade guys are real unfair that they can hide meaning you need to wait for them to throw a grenade to shoot them, but good luck dodging every thing else while trying to do it.
The games graphics are old school, the forest scenes are great, lots of vegetation, I was real surprised.  The audio in the entire game is way to low, whats worse is the audio is already set at 100%, so you cant turn up the volume in game.  If you get a sound notification for a steam message from a friend, its like a nuclear explosion going off.  Other parts of the game I cant hear the dialog at all, for example this one part Rambo is in a patrol car, and the music and car engine are so loud that it covers up the dialog.  The game is on rails, but it is fun, I had a good time with the game.  The game runs at 60 fps, but oddly in cut scenes they drop to 30 fps for some reason.  While playing I encountered no bugs or crashes.  There is replay value because you can play it anytime, the controls are real easy and intuitive, so no need to relearn controls everytime you play it.
Rambo has a waifu in this game, waifu is a slang term used that means wife or something.  This girl shows up like in the movie to help Rambo.  In the game everyone looks sorta real, or using human models, but oddly Rambos Waifu, I call her that since she looks like an Anime character, big eyes and all that.  Often she comments on how strong Rambo is, or how Manly he is, it is quite amusing actually, I was surprised she didnt shout out that Rambo must be very virile or she is looking forward to their masculine children.
The co-op hmmm well its the worst co-op ever made but its the most fun!  Rambo is a two player game so grab a friend and get ready to RAMBO together!  What makes the coop terrible is its local coop, meaning your playing with your friend next to you.  This game is a cover game like Time Crisis, or gears of war.  There is NO split screen, so if either player ducks to cover both players end up ducking, there is only one health bar, meaning once its gone both players are dead.  There is a thing called wrath in the game where you hit a button to trigger a period of time where you shoot enemies to get health,  if either player hits the wrath button, both players end up doing it.   Which can be real bad if its hit while one player is reloading and the wrath period ends before their done reloading.  What makes it the most fun, is due to these terrible mechanics it means talking, or yelling like a Rambo at your friend.  This game brings out the Rambo inside all of us.  especially when you lob a grenade only to have your friend duck as you pull the pin throwing the grenade at the cover watching it bounce back killing both of you.  This is very fun, and even better with beer, or other things...
*Bridge-Tip: Turn off auto aim, Rambo doesnt aim he just shoots everything!  Before doing the last map, do the Trautmans challenges and get the E3 M60 Heavy machine gun, it will make the last map easy.  Also on timed parts like the helicopter battle, make sure to use the perk +25% damage to take out that helicopter easy peasy.  To level up fast, just keep doing the jailhouse break mission and get over 200k xp real fast since its just qte's, maybe a minute or so long.

I definitiely recommend this game. You WILL have to get through GFWL, however. It was a real pain to set up for the first time, mainly becuase I had forgotten my password to my account. It takes a few minutes to get past the humps, but once you are in, there are no issues whatsoever.
To preface, you may have a sound issue. I am running on Win 8 using a Toshiba Satellite L-55B. Going into my sound settings in the control panel and disabling the microphone solved the sound issue for me.
After almost 40 hours into the game, 1/3 through my third playthrough, I can say there is a slight learning curve. It is unlike some FPS games where you can basically rush in. It is all about tactics, or you will make it harder for yourself. You must utilize fireteam orders, even better if you can manage ordering specific fireteam members during engagements. Especially when you get about halfway through. For those that haven't picked this game up yet and haven't researched it yet, I will leave out spoilers.
Biggest con about the game, and I personally wouldn't consider it a deal breaker, is that the AI classes do not gain experience during the campaign. Your very first playthrough is going to be rough, becuase you have not gained access to any good equipement or B-Mods. To sum it up, the only way to gain expereince with a class is to play as that class in the campaign.
I did my first playthrough with the default starting class, the Rifleman. My second playthrough was with the Scout (sniper), and I can say I'd recommend doing your first playthrough as the Scout. You will definitely learn how to compesnate for bullet drop much quicker, your main weapon deals max damage (very handy when it comes time to deal with armored enemies), and is semi-automatic for quick, instant death shots regardless of placement. Again, that will come in handy later on in the game, becuase it will get very hairy every mission. The Autorifleman is also a good one to start with (my third and current playthrough) because your weapon will hold 200 rounds, which helps with supression and large groups, without going dry quickly. That will allow you to get through just about any engagement without having to reload constantly.
That is really the only con. The repetitive dialogue is getting a little old, but it doesn't bother me. Now for the PROS!
This game has very good replay value. Even after my third playthrough I still get excited when accomplishing the mission goals, and it is rewarding. Especially hearing that sound when leveling up. The is why I don't consider my above con to be a deal breaker, because playing through from the start as a different class allows you to gain experience for that class, allowing any AI playing as the class you had used from the previous playthrough to utlilize the unlocked gear and B-Mods which makes it worth it, as your fireteam will be kicking some serious butt with the increased accuracy and damage endurance. Since my Rifleman and Scout are max level, more often than not they will pick off kills before I even have a chance, whereas compared to my first playthrough I was basically doing all the work.
I could keep going, but I'm heading back to the game now. It's worth the $9.99 and effort to get through first time setup with GFWL. And don't worry, your game will save.
Good hunting!

What I've always appreciated about the Operation Flashpoint games is that you really aren't the hero of the game. You're just another cog in the wheel surrounded by other cogs in the wheel of a fully functional fighting team. Red River is the third (and maybe last in the series) and I really enjoyed it. You're a marine fire team leader thrust into a conflict in a fictional desert country on the border of China. You take control of three AI squad members who you can give simple orders to. You can flank, suppress fire, hold positions etc. When given the opportunity you'll have access to mortar fire and airstrikes. The complaints about the AI being pretty dumb are unfortunately pretty spot on. Guys will run in front of you, I've had armor wipe out my team and I was run over by HMMWVs more than once. Graphics are servicable and the maps are large but you're also given checkpoints that tell you where to go so they feel limited in that aspect.  Mission variety...well you're in a fire eam so you're going to take and defend buildings, rush the enemy, destroy AA etc. There's a mission where you're falling back position after position because wave after wave of enemies are coming to get you. It can be frustrating but satisfying when you finish. The gunplay is a bit different since you have to account for bullet drop etc. It gets a bit easier as you go along since there's a level up system which allows you to put points towards gun handling, accuracy etc. There is an absolute ton of voice acting and while there were times it was a bit much I didn't mind it too much. Whoever played the Staff Sergeant was very good and reminded me of some of my leadership when I was in the Army. I also got lucky because I had zero issues with the GFWL setup. Saves worked perfectly and got plenty of achievements.  Overall I recommend OF: RR. OF: Dragon Rising is still the superior game but I've seen where you can get both games for $5. That's a great deal. 7.5/10 from me.

Here we go.
is the fifth installment - obviously - of the GTA series, released by Rockstar Games. The story mode centres upon three indivisuals; Trevor Philips, Michael De Santa, and Franklin Clinton. The 'story' generally consists of them entering - and returning to - the life of crime. Through out the 'story', the three protagonists deal with the hardships and gains from being a criminal. This 'story' is actually better than it seems. It is very fun and, for the first half only, very addictive. However, it gets really boring after about 2-3 weeks of playing the game. And once it gets boring, you - or at least I - won't find that spark that lit the fire of addictiveness that drove you to play GTA V for hours on end in the first place.
Furthermore, this game crashes. A lot. For me at least, I am lucky to even get past the loading screen without crashing.
As for the online mode, I haven't really took a gander at it at all. So the following will be objective. Online mode is fun only up to an extent. If you are new to online mode - or GTA V for that matter - you will be lost, confused, and you will die. A lot. As well, and I cannot be certain about this, Rockstar Games decided to remove modding in GTA V. For some, not me, this was the driving factor that made them addicted to the game in the first place.
To conclude, when you play this game for the first time, you will be in awe. This is due to the fact that GTA V is a visual masterpiece and a landmark in gaming. The close attention to detail is significantly evident. As stated before, you will probably get bored within a month of playing the game. And once you do, I wouldn't advise you to switch to online mode as that can - not only be more boring as you are somewhat stripped of your freedom due to the endless killing that will occur, but can be frustrating. And good luck with the consistent crashing that may occur. Oh yeah, the game has♥♥♥♥♥♥in it.

At first glance this is just a sprite based Smash Bros clone. It has the same aspects of basic play including a variety of characters, items and stages.
They make no attempt to hide the fact that this was inspired by the design of Smash Bros, but what they do somewhat hide is just how different and unique the game can be.
Easy to learn, but hard to master. Those who start to really learn the game will find that one thing really makes it unique by comparison, the weapons system. Unlike Smash Bros, where items are incredibly varied and random, Brawlhalla maintains items and reduces RNG by centralizing the battle on weapons.  With each Legend having access to two weapons and a variety of unique attacks, the games roster has a character to suit any playstyle.
The most exemplary part about this game are by far the developers, who are constantly adding new things and show a dedication to their playerbase rarely seen these days.
You have very little reason not to at least try this game.

Brawlhalla, a game where you can get hopelessly lost in, as you can tell by the amount of hours I have ingame, keep in mind, very few of them were afk/idle hours.
I started playing this game from when it was in closed beta around a year and a half ago, and I can still manage to have a pretty good time while playing.
However if you don't make any friends/don't have any friends already that play this game, it can get a little boring after awhile. The reason I managed to stay playing for so long was my slight involvement in the community, joining a clan, participating in a few tournaments, all of which helped pass the time quite well.
Whether you're playing competitively or casually, beware that there will be a bunch of bad apples out there trying to ruin your experience, just ignore them and move on, the majority of the community is filled with lots of well behaved, nice people if you manage to stick around long enough.
The game itself will have you crying of laughter from the weirdly funny things that can happen in game, or even pulling your hair out in frustration while trying to make that grind to the next rank, all in all, it was and still is an enjoyable experience. Not to mention that it is free, even if the skins aren't, and look damn good, do your best to hold yourself back. I tried, and failed miserably, but I don't regret it and you probably won't either.
Definitely would recommend to anyone looking to pass the time, just don't lose track of it.

Here we go.
is the fifth installment - obviously - of the GTA series, released by Rockstar Games. The story mode centres upon three indivisuals; Trevor Philips, Michael De Santa, and Franklin Clinton. The 'story' generally consists of them entering - and returning to - the life of crime. Through out the 'story', the three protagonists deal with the hardships and gains from being a criminal. This 'story' is actually better than it seems. It is very fun and, for the first half only, very addictive. However, it gets really boring after about 2-3 weeks of playing the game. And once it gets boring, you - or at least I - won't find that spark that lit the fire of addictiveness that drove you to play GTA V for hours on end in the first place.
Furthermore, this game crashes. A lot. For me at least, I am lucky to even get past the loading screen without crashing.
As for the online mode, I haven't really took a gander at it at all. So the following will be objective. Online mode is fun only up to an extent. If you are new to online mode - or GTA V for that matter - you will be lost, confused, and you will die. A lot. As well, and I cannot be certain about this, Rockstar Games decided to remove modding in GTA V. For some, not me, this was the driving factor that made them addicted to the game in the first place.
To conclude, when you play this game for the first time, you will be in awe. This is due to the fact that GTA V is a visual masterpiece and a landmark in gaming. The close attention to detail is significantly evident. As stated before, you will probably get bored within a month of playing the game. And once you do, I wouldn't advise you to switch to online mode as that can - not only be more boring as you are somewhat stripped of your freedom due to the endless killing that will occur, but can be frustrating. And good luck with the consistent crashing that may occur. Oh yeah, the game has♥♥♥♥♥♥in it.
Verdict: 5.2/10
