A very well designed, historically accurate tactical strategy game whose clean interface and ease of play nicely implement the constantly deeper and more challenging game that it becomes with each update.These frequent updates include new features, improvements to the interface and AI, etc. and many of them are based on player feedback and suggestions. The game could benefit from a greater variety of weapons and units (scouts, partisans, engineers, etc.), the ability to entrench in place, bonuses for flank attacks or ambushes and finally, a map and scenario editor would be an awesome addition since it would essentially allow players to re-create any battle they wish.
Unfortunately, after the first update, the game no longer ran on my Dell tablet (it continued to run fine on my pc) so I contacted tech support. I've been a pc gamer since the days of DOS and I must say that the customer service has been some of the best I've ever received be it from a behemoth like Electronic Arts or an indie like HexWar, with personalized responses addressing my issue in particular and their efforts to fix it with each new update. So, considering the price, the ease of play, the fact that you can pick it up for a few minutes or a few hours, the deep and varied gameplay and the excellent customer service, I can highly recommend this game.

Jensen's Stories remind me of The Missing Link from DXHR in that they seem to take place during the main plot, but are offered as stand-alone missions which, while good on their own, would definitely benefit from being placed within the game's larger narrative. I'm a big fan of Deus Ex and cyberpunk in general but I'll keep this as neutral as it can be particularly when it comes to technical issues, I'll try to keep things short, I'm sure no one wants a TLDR.
I've really enjoyed the story and characters in the game, some might not be as fleshed out as you might want but they feel human and relatable, I intentionally didn't use any augmentations that would allow me to read their moon or what would work on them so I could try to use their body language and my intuition to know what to say next and I have to say it worked out well most of the time.
The gameplay felt solid to me I finished the game on "Give me Deus EX" at no point did it feel too easy or too hard, there's plenty of augmentations to play around with and enough weapons/gadgets. Stealth mechanics are solid, gunplay was also solid as was hacking and exploration. Overall I think gameplay along with the story are some of the game's strongest points.
Graphically the game looks really good, the lighting is fantastic, the assets are high poly/high res, unfortunately character models don't quite cut it, even though they can be very detail and have great looking hair, the faces seem a bit low poly and the animations aren't the best.
Performance is where the problems begin, the game seems to be having trouble keeping the framerates up even in very powerful builds, there have have been a huge number of complaints about technical problems such as stutter, low framerates even on really high end hardware such as a GTX 1080, crashes, and even game breaking glitches that will now allow you to progress in the story, I've experienced all of the above myself. These problems have been mostly fixed at least for me but they stopped me from playing the game at launch and even weeks after, the DirectX 12 patch still seems to be work in progress and performs worse than DX11 for the most part including in bizarre things such as loading times.
I've also found the game to be short, the main story is short and at least, and I didn't find as many side quests as I would like, even though the ones that are there were pretty good. At the time of writing this review I've got 53 hours in this game, I've had to restart the game once I got to Talos because of a game breaking glitch, I've also crashed numerous times and spent a long time messing around with settings and benchmarking, together with loading times and idle times in-game I'd say I got a good 30-35 hours of actual gameplay out of it which isn't really satisfying after playing the Witcher 3.
In the end I'd still recommend this game to anyone thet enjoys the genre and setting, the game has been and is continously being patched and improved, hopefuly there will be some good story DLC in the future.

Nixxes did an amazing job with the PC port, and Eidos did excellent recapturing Human Revolution.  I can't say the main plot is particularly strong because of how relatively short it is.  You'll find the majority of the gameplay in exploring and the side missions.  That said, the side missions play back into the main narrative, and despite the abrupt ending, I really enjoyed this game.  Augs 2.0 were tasteful and not too over the top, and while I know Square demanded Adam return for this game, I actually like following 'him' since his perspective fascinates me.
I played on a 2700K @ 4.6, 16GB, and a GTX770 4GB, the game was extremely playable at medium to high settings.
My only real comlaints would be what Square did.  And shame on them for that.  They'll literally bet the company on their piecemeal FF7 remake, which has to sell something like 15 million units to break even, but Deus Ex can't stand on its own.  So they'll milk us for more money via more games and throw in a multiplayer minigame.  Whatever will stick.  If you come at this as a single player game only, and can somehow ignore SquareEnix milking us for every dollar they can, it's an excellent game.
Also second shame callout for the DLC stories all being separate from the main story.  You can't be bothered to integrate with the other side quests?  It'd be genuinely fun to play the game and do all these current and upcoming DLC stories in the middle of a second playthrough.  Don't get me wrong, the first one was actually really good with Pritchard, but it sucked I couldn't bring 'my' Jensen into the DLC.  Just "here's a few praxis points and a pistol, enjoy!"  FFS square.  You did this in HR then re-released integrated.  I'm sure I'll have to pony up for that as well.  Shame on Square, but Eidos did a good job despire this absurd demands.

This game is fun, if you have friends to play with you will have a lot of fun, or if you like something better than the For Glory on sm4sh then this game is great.
The characters and the gameplay: each character has two weapons each, at the start of a match every character will start without a weapon, in this form you have aerial attacks, a recovery move, a few jumps until you have to land, heavy attacks, etc. However, the place of differentiation betweem the characters comes from their weapons, the weapons have very similar move inputs however react very differently, for instance, just because two characters have an axe, doesn't mean that their forward heavy attack (or smash attack) will have the same animation or hitbox (start-up frames, etc.)
The best way to describe the gameplay itself is fast, it only takes a few heavy attacks on you to get you to kill damage (varies by defensive stat), some combos are quite easy to pull off once you are famliar with a characters moveset you may find one yourself mid match. The differences between this game and smash bros. are that it has no grab input (it does have grapples on some characters, just depends on the move, but not every character has a grab unlike smash bros. where every character does) and there is no shield button, there is a dodge, which can be combined into a directional input to gain momentum, or move out of an area, you can also use this method in the air, this will not cause you to go into freefall (if you don't touch the ground you are dead). There is also the differences in recovery, this game you have an up heavy input in the air (aka a recovery move) and three jumps and a dodge mid air (or multiple, this is on a timer) before you must touch the ground or wall slide (since there is no ledges, similar to Rivals of Aether), wall sliding resets your jumps and recovery move.
There are a lot of settings to mess around with and the gameplay is really fun and exiciting, practise also feels really rewarding when you land a combo on an opponent after many attempts.
The characters do lack personality (although this game doesn't really need that, I just thought I should include it anyways.)
Since this game is free I would highly reccomend at least trying it for 1/2 hour or so to get a feel for it, that is if you like Smash Bros. or Rivals of Aether.

Greetings!  The last of the Original Dawn of War Expansions; how I absolutely love this game.  It summed up the series with even more factions (though no Tyranids) and a revised take on the previous campaign map.
You’ve seen this Before:  The campaign is okay, just like the last one.  It really could have been done much better and even now feels like a tack on campaign that would be provided as a secondary way to play verses a normal story campaign.  Though I do appreciate a lot of the fixes that allowed laughable easy progression (even on hard) the style of using multiplayer maps only vaguely masked the problem of next to no storyline.  Again, if you are a hard core Blood Ravens fan every bit helps to craft their tale but I would have preferred a real story based campaign not multiplayer map list with a few ‘challenge maps’ that don’t even really have a story either (other than non-custom banter between the commanders).
A Step Back:  The technical issues are pretty bad now.  I don’t remember if they were this bad upon release but for my computer as of today I’ve had many game ending crashes.  An odd mouse bug that prevented it from moving to certain parts of the screen and a currpption bug that required me to start the campaign half way through it all created an unplayable experience that was a step above all the minor visual ones and camera view issues from the previous ones.
But Should I Buy It:  The honest answer is yes, I still love this game but if you can’t handle the bugs then I wouldn’t.  Buying this for the purpose of a modern RTS then I’d avoid it.  With DOW3 coming out you may be thinking about it for the sake of story or living the games past…then I’d so go ahead.
I’m going to have to give this game that I love so much a ‘do not recommend’.  Understand, this was one of the best RTS I’d ever played at the time but the consistent bugs (especially the game / campaign ending ones) prevent me from recommending this to anyone right now who is just looking for a new RTS.  And I hate that…because this game is still awesome.

As someone who plays 'Super Smash Bros. Melee' in a comepitive setting, I thought Brawlhalla wouldn't even get a kick out me. By appearance, it looks just like a F2P version of SSB's formula with a cast of original characters. And I can tell you first hand, that I was wrongly mistaken.
Brawlhalla innovates upon what makes SSB great and delivers a lot fun. It even satisfies comepetitve gamers, such as myself, with 1v1 matchmaking. I guess this is a... Review to a Kill...
That will be the one and only cheesy pun in this review of Ubisoft's Standalone Expansion 'Far Cry 3- Blood Dragon', as anymore will leave you feeling a little bloated when you get into the madness that is this game. You see, Blood Dragon is a spoof-game on so many levels: It spoofs the 80s VHS Action Movie Genre and perhaps most impressive it spoof's Ubisoft's gameplay style to perfection!
I have a question to ask: Have you seen and enjoyed the following movies?
Aliens
Rambo
Terminator
Transformers?
Do you enjoy movies starring the follow actors?
Jean Claude Van Damme
Michael Biehn
Arnie
Do you tell all your friends that all the best music was made in the 80s? Do you still dream of a world where synths and neon lights in a not-so-distant dystopia society rule over the masses? Well I might just have the game for you..!
It's a FPS based around the Far Cry 3 engine, so if you've played Far Cry 3 than you should know what to expect. If you haven't then be prepared to be dropped on an 'open world' Island that you're free to explore at your will. There are various collectibles, unlockables, etc (such are Ubisoft Games), as well as your standard enemie types.
It's a fun game that really embraces the subject material it's lampooning from the very first moment the game boots up.
The actual gameplay itself is tired and nothing new, yet it's the character and the world around you that keeps you playing. The one liners drew me back to a day when Duke Nukem was considered a master piece, and thankfully this game has as many one liners as it does bullets and mindless violence!
In fact, it's perhaps all the supporting material that keeps Blood Dragon feeling like a breath of fresh air in a very worn out genre void of much originality. The strange neon visuals look stunning at times as you storm into Garrisons to kill the Biker Helmet wearing nameless bad guys to a very satisfying Synth based soundtrack. The little details make the big experience worthwhile, so if you're not too fond of those details you'll perhaps not enjoy the game as much as I did. If, however, you find yourself going back to the stack of movies you have starring Action Heros from the 80s than this game might just help reignite your interest in FPS.
+ 80's Action Hero Genre
+ One Liners
+ Spoofs
+ Doesn't Out Stay It's Welcome
- I have no idea if they'll make a follow up to this genre!
- Worn out gameplay
Overall a satisfying short experience for 80s Action/Sci-Fi Movie Buffs, but it might not be for everyone's tastes.

Let's take one of the greatest classics in computer gaming history and ruin it.
The revamped graphics, music, and sound effects are just plain awful. The originals were so much better.
You would think that the now-'smoothed' movement would make the gameplay more seamless, but in fact it makes it unncessarily tedious and more error prone. In the original, movements were fairly discrete, so there was no ambiguity with regards to timing of movements. Whereas in the original I could hold down the arrow keys without too much fear of overstepping, in this version I find myself tapping the keys because of how aggressive the game handles movement. The lack of an undo feature means that you could easily waste half an hour on a puzzle that otherwise takes 3 minutes to solve, simply because you accidentally held a key for two long, or accidentally tapped the wrong key. (No, I do not believe the level skip feature makes up for this inexcusable omission.)
The game is intended to be a puzzle game, not an action game; I should not have to micromanage my movements in relation to enemies apart from general high-level strategy!
I loved the original, but this remake is so very disappointing. As far as I've concerned, I've paid for the game, so I feel entitled to download a bootleg of the original and play that one instead of this ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ized version.

My only complaint is the audio. The sound effects are a bit too loud, moreso than the background music; with a few of them being rather annoying (I personally opted to import some of the sound effects from the earlier Windows version, but the game does offer the option to disable sound effects entirely if you'd like). As for the music, what they used just seems ill-fitting for this game; sounding more like music from a silent movie than a game about a nerd trying to impress the head of a computer club.
Still, it's worth a purchase; it's a classic.

Sorry Tolkien fans, but sadly this is a big No-No.
This game is basically World of Warcraft reskinned to look like Lord of the Rings. With some "cameos" from classical characters from the saga.
I was a fan of Tolkien's work when I was a kid, read pretty much everything there is to read, and watched the movies when I was almost outgrowing Middle Earth. And to a lesser degree, I was a fan of pretty much everything Blizzard did up until recently. This is to clarify that I am more than aware of the "lore" differences.
The problem is with the "feel" of the game. The gameplay feels clunky, the LotR lore feels heavyhanded, and the graphics barely offer anything remarkable (but they get the job done).
And eventually, if you really want to experiencie everything there is to experiencie, you will have to pay... so it's not really "free" free. Now, I'm not saying that you cannot play without paying, or that this is a pay-to-win game. The system is fair and honest about what it offers.
It's not a "bad game". It simply fails to hold any charm or provide a different experience than any other game of the same genre.
The final veredict is: Not worth the time and effort....
Unless you are a die hard fan of the franchise, or you had some very bad experiences with WOW, I doubt that you'll find anything in this game that is worth your time and money.

This game is an odd one. Charming yet flawed.
*IMPORTANT NOTE*: 2 new maps both with vehicles! (jeeps on the first and planes on the 2nd)
As someone who has played the old Army Men games such as Sarges Heroes 1 & 2 I can recommend this title to anyone who enjoyed those even a little, as its essentially a multiplayer only version of those with far superior controls. (nostalgia goggles will never hide the horrible controls of the army men series)
It has 12 maps each with their own game mode and gimmicks which makes it quite a refreshing title to play for an hour or so. However the map "Off The Rails" is not quite well optimized and is the only map my PC struggles with. (which is quite low spec I will admit)
Besides "Off The Rails" the only other map that gave me trouble was "Barnball" this map is focused on a Table Football field where the objective is to score goals by rolling the ball into the enemy barn. while that sounds great in theory it rarely works out and usually devolves into team deathmatch/ a spawncamp scenario and gets boring rather quickly.
It has all the weapons you would expect in a game about the Green and Tan (Red on the sandbox map) base-bound warriors: Assault rifle, Sniper rifle, Shotgun, Bazooka and a Flamethrower.
While fun to use they come across as inconsistent, especially the flamethrower which while having been heavily improved does not feel very fun to use. This does not hurt the game much however as its main purpose is to complete objectives eg. melting ice and lighting candles.
The game is quite fast paced with a very low time to kill on all the weapons and short respawn times. this usually works in its favour until teams become unbalanced resulting in a near endless massacre of one side until the round timer runs out. (especially on more open maps where snipers dominate.)
All in all  its great value for its price but the devs are going to have to put some work in to iron out some of the issues. but compared to most indie multiplayer titles at this price its one of the best.

I'm a big fan of Deus Ex and cyberpunk in general but I'll keep this as neutral as it can be particularly when it comes to technical issues, I'll try to keep things short, I'm sure no one wants a TLDR.
I've really enjoyed the story and characters in the game, some might not be as fleshed out as you might want but they feel human and relatable, I intentionally didn't use any augmentations that would allow me to read their moon or what would work on them so I could try to use their body language and my intuition to know what to say next and I have to say it worked out well most of the time.
The gameplay felt solid to me I finished the game on "Give me Deus EX" at no point did it feel too easy or too hard, there's plenty of augmentations to play around with and enough weapons/gadgets. Stealth mechanics are solid, gunplay was also solid as was hacking and exploration. Overall I think gameplay along with the story are some of the game's strongest points.
Graphically the game looks really good, the lighting is fantastic, the assets are high poly/high res, unfortunately character models don't quite cut it, even though they can be very detail and have great looking hair, the faces seem a bit low poly and the animations aren't the best.
Performance is where the problems begin, the game seems to be having trouble keeping the framerates up even in very powerful builds, there have have been a huge number of complaints about technical problems such as stutter, low framerates even on really high end hardware such as a GTX 1080, crashes, and even game breaking glitches that will now allow you to progress in the story, I've experienced all of the above myself. These problems have been mostly fixed at least for me but they stopped me from playing the game at launch and even weeks after, the DirectX 12 patch still seems to be work in progress and performs worse than DX11 for the most part including in bizarre things such as loading times.
I've also found the game to be short, the main story is short and at least, and I didn't find as many side quests as I would like, even though the ones that are there were pretty good. At the time of writing this review I've got 53 hours in this game, I've had to restart the game once I got to Talos because of a game breaking glitch, I've also crashed numerous times and spent a long time messing around with settings and benchmarking, together with loading times and idle times in-game I'd say I got a good 30-35 hours of actual gameplay out of it which isn't really satisfying after playing the Witcher 3.
In the end I'd still recommend this game to anyone thet enjoys the genre and setting, the game has been and is continously being patched and improved, hopefuly there will be some good story DLC in the future.

I played on a 2700K @ 4.6, 16GB, and a GTX770 4GB, the game was extremely playable at medium to high settings.
My only real comlaints would be what Square did.  And shame on them for that.  They'll literally bet the company on their piecemeal FF7 remake, which has to sell something like 15 million units to break even, but Deus Ex can't stand on its own.  So they'll milk us for more money via more games and throw in a multiplayer minigame.  Whatever will stick.  If you come at this as a single player game only, and can somehow ignore SquareEnix milking us for every dollar they can, it's an excellent game.

It'd be genuinely fun to play the game and do all these current and upcoming DLC stories in the middle of a second playthrough.  Don't get me wrong, the first one was actually really good with Pritchard, but it sucked I couldn't bring 'my' Jensen into the DLC.  Just "here's a few praxis points and a pistol, enjoy!"  FFS square.  You did this in HR then re-released integrated.  I'm sure I'll have to pony up for that as well.  Shame on Square, but Eidos did a good job despire this absurd demands.

This is the Chip's Challenge you remember... mostly. I say mostly, because there are some minor changes. First off, the music has changed from the original, but it is still the ragtime piano type music that helps make this game relaxing. Sound effects? They're pretty terrible, and while the "Bummer!" on a loss is still great, I have to mute them because of the other annoying sounds.
If you've never played Chip's Challenge before, it is a fairly long puzzler. However, puzzles will definitely not all be around the same length. You may complete a stage in 20 seconds (seriously, there's stages with a timer that short)... or you may be in for a slog with one of the no-time-limit dirt-block pushing puzzles. It does a lot with the simple tileset and rules of the world, creating some very unique puzzles when all's said and done.
I recommend the game, but mostly for nostalgia purposes. It was fun then, and it's still fun now. Restarting a no-time-limit puzzle because you held a direction too long isn't that fun, though.

“The Mean Greens - Plastic Warfare” is a fun little shooter game that is the result of our imaginations combining Toy Story and Small Soldiers.
The maps hold a lot more detail than I was expecting and each map has its own personality and feel. There are several different game modes that give great variability and offer a nice twist on the shooter genre. Are you capturing the flag in a bathtub or fish tank? Maybe you need to light candles on a birthday cake (which is huge to these little guys). Or perhaps you are on a Foosball table and are trying to push the ball into the other team's goal while shooting at each other. It is the little things like that which warrant a tip of the cap for respect.
Pros:
- The Unreal Engine is great for this (the flamethrower will melt you and the rocket launcher shoots your limbs off)
- Great attention to detail in the maps and character models
- Nostalgic and fun and plays pretty quick (longest a match can go is 10 minutes)
- Good replay value
- Refreshing and doesn't get stale or repetitive
Cons:
- Some connection issues are there (Devs have said they are addressing it. Once connected to a server, I've never lost connection. Just initially getting in can be hard sometimes)
- The hit boxes don't seem fully there at the moment (just need some fine tuning)
- Weapon balance seems off (the rocket launcher was recently nerfed to help, but the flamethrower probably needs the same then)
- The matchmaking can be hit or miss. I don't like adding ranks with experience and all but sometimes it just isn't fair
Despite the technical cons, the fun-filled pros still outweigh it for me. I like this as a nice casual filler if I only have 15 min or so to play something. In the future, I obviously would like the technical issues addressed, but for some maps a vehicle or object that can be used would be interesting to implement. Transmissions: Element 120 puts you in the role of an unknown fighter, probably during the events of the Seven Hour wars or shortly after that; it is unclear wether you are, or you are not, Dr. Gordon Freeman (and the ending does not really solve the question, even with... (SPOILER),
. There is a resistance against the Combine, but you do not really get to have them fighting by your side. You are alone, pretty much as the majority of the HL games in which you feel an overwhelming solitude (except when Alyx Vance goes with you, or the army of citizens of City 17).
During your adventure, you get to find a strange device in the shape of a Gravity Gun, but this one casts a strange energy sphere wich explodes with contact on any surface; also, you discover something about the zombies (which you have to discover during the game as it's part of the challenge), and probably one of the most interesting things not only in the game, but the whole HL universe and many other games, is the inclusion of the QRC (Quick Response Codes), which have been sprayed on different walls as hints or help for the hero. By whom? I take, the resistance, but this is also unclear.
There are not too many weapons, but you don't really miss them. And actually the game is so short, you don't really get to use them that much.
Physics are flawless as you could expect from a HL game. And something cool, for serious players, is that the developer doesn't fill you with hints or tutorials or marks or signs telling you what to do. It is you against the enviroment; the player versus the world. Use it; find your way, explore, don't be afraid of squeezing into a tight sewer pipe. Yeah, you'll probably die, or not, but that's how you find the way out (or in).
There are Combine and Zombine (as Alyx named them), and those terrible Stryders. The end comes too fast and unexpectedly, but that doesn't make the game bad, or even feel rushed; it only leaves you with a bitter cliffhanger and, at least in my case, waiting for a sequel or more future content with this little jewel.
This game is basically a perfectly well balanced addition to the universe, and it could hade easily been another episode just like The Lost Coast, which was so well paced and mooded to fit into the saga (with all the mystery and melancholy need to be part of it).

Brothers - A Tale of Two Sons is a short, but fantastic game. There is not much to tell about the plot of the game - it is about two brothers who lost their mother in a sea accident, and desperately trying to save their dad from a sickness by finding the "tree of life" after this accident.
The game forces you to play with both of the brothers simultaneously, which is a very nice feature IMO. You have to learn to control both of the brothers at the same time, and think quickly in most occasions. Puzzles are not that hard, but fun to solve. Graphics and music are satisfying. Ambiance and color palettes are fantastic.
The ending is really, really sad. The game already makes you miserable in the beginning, and just when you were putting things right, more just keeps coming.
Overall: a brilliant short indie game. 10/10, would play again.

The mechanics and controls are fun, and while a controller is mandatory, it quickly becomes second nature. You control each of the brothers with with a separate analog stick, something I hadn't heard of before this game.
While it only took me about 2 hours to complete entirely, I would still recommend this experience to anyone just looking to get lost in a truly wonderful and inspirational world. The range of emotions it brought to me is something I'm looking forward to replaying some time in the near future.

Chip's Challenge is a puzzle game where you die a lot. It's a puzzle game in the same vein as Portal, in that you progress by beating levels instead of arranging blocks or jewels. You don't beat levels by thinking so much as trial and error (and dying and restarting), and no two levels or challenges are the same.
In a modern gaming world of procedurly generated indie games where you have a 1/10 chance of generating a level that isn't purely awful, it's also great to see designed stages in both this and the sequel. Every level was hand made back in 1989, and it shows in terms of quality and even humor.
Excellent time waster, with interesting mechanics and levels. Is noted to have a "one-more-level" quality of addictiveness that keeps people coming back.

I'm reliving my childhood one chip at a time
As a player of Chip's Challenge long ago, I truly enjoyed playing this game. And the best part? When you lose the game, you will hear the iconic "bummer." Bonus.

Chip's Challenge is a tale of the indomitable spirit that burns in the hearts of men. The long road stretches before all of us, obscured by great oceans, blazing wildfires, frozen wastelands, and one-way directional floor tiles. Our dreams are hidden behind closed doors, and only the most courageous among us seek out the appropriately-colored keys. Chip is one such courageous individual. He will not rest until his demons are conquered and the challenges set before him lie as blazing piles of ash in his wake.
He endures the pain and the sorrow, he fights through tears and blood, and he hits reset for the one-hundredth time after pushing a block into the wrong water tile. He does this for love, for the hand of Melinda the Mental Marvel, but he also does this for himself. In conquering the insects, the rocket ships, and the chattering teeth, in walking across the fires, sacrificing the technological relics, and traversing the transdimensional portals, he ascends beyond his own mortal shortcomings and into the realm of gods. His chains unfettered, he is unstoppable. He is the hunter, and block puzzles are his prey.
This is not merely a game. This is a rite of passage into your own potential. This is the mountain that stands in your way, the path you must build with your own two hands. This is your Andre the Giant. This is your King George III. This is your Apollo Creed. When the chips are down and it's your call, are you all talk or do you have something to show? Does the blood of the warriors pulse in your veins? Are you one star shining in the night sky brighter than all the other stars?
Just who the hell do you think you are?

As someone who really enjoyed Human Revolution despite its flaws, I was prepared to start Mankind Divided with a pretty optimistic view. Despite that, I was surprised how much less enjoyable Mankind Divided was. It seemed like about half a story and what was there wasn't very satisfying. The premise isn't very compelling and the central moral theme wasn't at all believable. It was also very hard to suspend disbelief when there are so many immersion-breaking bugs occuring. I constantly ran into strange animation issues and character pathing bugs, plus strange camera behavior in cutscenes and occasionally mission status flags triggering at the wrong times. It gets hard to take the rest of the game seriously when an NPC is walking against the side of you through an entire dialog interaction.
The biggest game-breaking bugs have been resolved, but that's really the least that could be done. This game could have really used several more months of QA iteration to be considered release-quality. The remaining issues I've seen are the kind that aren't likely to ever be addressed, so I can't really imagine recommending this title unless it reaches 50% off or more.
I regret purchasing this before other reviews were available and I plan to be less trusting of Square Enix titles in the future.

The Last of Us, Witcher 3, Dying Light, Assassin's Creed Black Flag, Dishonored, to name a few have all transcended what's expected of triple A titles.  Again, while I like a lot of the ideas in this game, the execution is poor and was found lacking (especially lip synch and a lot of the animations).  Here's hoping Cyberpunk comes out soon.

Get the game. but get it for the mods. If you know how to handle yourself and are happy to jump through a few hoops, Install Titanium Wars, If your looking for a ezy install mod go do Ultimate Apocolypse. I won't be reviewing the game itself, there are other reviews for that, and my opinion is frank, Its the best RTS out there next to Starcraft, and not as outragously competative.  What I will be doing is compairing the two top teir mods for the game.
Ultimate Apocolypse;
Races it adds; Tyranids, Deamons, Ordo malleus
Stuff it fixes; Not much (as far as I can see)
For unit comparisons I will be using Space Marines, For easy refrence.
Apocolypse adds in a selection of units from table top, as well as 2 titans and fair selection of the bigger tanks. However it feels like things are missing For example, specalised heavy weapons squads along with Dreadnaught Mortis.
Notes; it is easy to install however it feels like a somewhat paired down version of Titanium Wars
Titanium Wars;
Races Added; Tyranids, Administratum, Ordo Malleus, Wictch Hunters (Semi-conversion of the Sisters Of Battle to bring them on level)
Stuff it Fixes; Removal of unbalanced Air units, AI pathing, Donatioins, and High speed calculations put in, AI is also capable of using the new units to their fullest.
Unit Comparison;
Almost every unit from table top, However against Apoc it only adds 1 titan for balanceing reasons. However it does allow for thing such as thunderhawk deployment of super heavy tanks alongside far more unit customization.
Notes; Administratum and Ordo Malleus are huge, they feel like they should and have unique units to themselves, The voice acting isn't amazing (the mod-maker is russian) and installing it is a pain due to a complicated series of events that involved a spat between mod makers.
Conclusion, I would go for Titanium wars, mainly because it has a larger selection of units and it makes some armies playable in multiplayer, However if you are not after balanced and just want to feild the largest army imagenable and do silly things. go for Apocolypse.
In short; Get the game. For The Emperor, For the Dark gods, For the Greater Good, whatever battle cry you so choose, but mod it. get a few friends together, get them the game, get them the mods and proceed to smash titans against each other.

Getting a new rc car has been a thought that has been tempting me for years. I knew this is what the pros use to practice so I figured I'm not a pro but I can practice too. It took no time at all to realize I do not need a new rc car. There is no longer a desire to get plastic flex tubing to outline the track that surely would have destroyed my backyard and part of the property value. This will not replace real racing but I have no business on a real rc track anyway so this is a win for everyone. The only difference (to me) between the way these cars handle and real rc cars is one is on the screen and looks like a simulator. I recommend this to anyone who is even remotely curious about professional radio controlled cars and trucks for racing. I also recommend this as a supplement to any controller based driving you are doing now. This could also make for interesting "team building" excercises around the office. Single player, multiplayer, vehicle setups, and more make this the complete rc land racing solution. You could just ignore this review and note that Team Associated cars and trucks are in here which is more than reason enough to buy this.

No penalty for using it, even if you're hunting achievements.  Production value is better than most in this genre.
Voting it up as a game, but I wouldn't pay $15 for it.  Wait for a sale/bundle.
Achievement hunters:
-There are in-game achievements, but no STEAM achievements (yet?), which is lazy & dumb of them.
-I think you'd be able to get them all on a single playthrough on casual difficulty, but I didn't bother.
-The dreamcatcher she wears is not one that you have to find, in-fact if you click it, it uses one of your hints so you lose access to the no-hints achievement!
-You cannot travel backwards in this game, so make sure you get all of the badges & dreamcatchers before leaving an area
-a lot of the achievements are for completing one of the puzzles with no mistakes, so plan ahead.

Disregard haters - Acquire Praxis.
I'm basing this review off a simple premise - you are one of those people who is not mortally offended by the inclusion of microtransactions in a game, where said microtransactions are not important to complete said game.
Pros:
- Good graphics and runs reasonably well, some glitching but no crashes for me in my playthrough
- Incredible variety in approaches to challenges - I don't recall a single mission where there was a gunbarrel I had to run down.
- Augments have been balanced, CASIE makes sense now, glass shield is actually reasonably balanced. Praxis is scarce but valuable. Hacking remains challenging even at higher levels and doesn't give massive exp.
- A very interesting story that ends with enough closure (for me) but still leaves us something to anticipate.
- Game is much more challenging.
Cons:
- Physics engine is ♥♥♥♥ed. Completely. KO'd enemies get stuck in the floor so you can't move them, boxes move stupidly, collision detection is broken, particularly with edges.
- Adam Jensen is still ♥♥♥♥ing boring.
- Some character arcs fall flat.
- Load times are on the long side even off an SSD.
Overall
Good game, would recommend if you liked Human Revolution - it's superior visually and in terms of gameplay (physics excepted). The story is comparable, overall I think it is weaker but a better resolution (it feels like your decisions actually matter).

Overview
Adam Jensen is back and on a new case. One in which he is trying to investigate one terrorist attack and stop a forthcoming one.
Trigger Warning(s)
Everything you’d normally expect from an M rated game
Play Through Time
Approximately 48 Hours Total
Storyline
After around 2 years since the events of Human Evolution, Adam finds himself now working for Interpol as Serif Industries has fallen thanks to what is universally called “The Incident.” The historic moment when all Augs became murderous and has since led to distrust of the augmented and high levels of prejudice across the world. But specifically in Prague, where the game primarily takes place, the distrust has reached new levels as a segregated ghetto of a city has been built for the augmented and a train station bombing happens. All of which is blamed on the pro-Aug rights group ARC. Thus leading to Adam to take part in a multitude of missions to investigate the bombing, an incident that happens in Dubai, which serves as the tutorial level, and an investigation into the accusations of ARC being responsible for multiple terrorist attacks.
Review Summary
-Rental-
Highlights
Let me begin by saying, being that I have never been necessarily good at shooters, even on what could be considered Normal difficulty, I struggled. But thankfully the game isn’t a straight forward shooter. With the ability to hack, hide, cloak, and other means of avoiding combat, for those of us who don’t have the patience to duck, cover, and shoot, or aren’t the type who like to run in guns blazing, there are options. In fact, playing a non-lethal game is entirely possible. Granted, it is a bit difficult, but even the final, if not the only boss in the game, can be taken down without firing a bullet. A quite neat option considering video games have come to a point where there is an increased desire to give the player options. Though while most game simply provides dialog choices, which this game offers and to a certain degree makes important, it seems almost revolutionary to offer the ability to simply knock out everyone and press on with your objective.
But I would be remiss if I didn’t note how enjoyable both the story and side quests were. Now, I don’t believe, even with around 2 days of gameplay, I found and played every last side quest and found every last item. I did try, but for reasons below I eventually came to a point where I just wanted to finish this game. With that said, be it doing a murder investigation, in which every clue mattered, to convincing people to trust Adam, much less the main plot in which I was led around to investigate ARC and the plans of some of its members, I did ultimately enjoy myself. Though what I especially enjoyed was the hacking mini-game which I almost wish was a mobile game in of itself.
Low Points
I played this game on a Steam controller and, as usual, at this point, the game wasn’t necessarily optimized for it. But besides that control issue, perhaps the main problem of this game is as vast as it sometimes seems, you feel so restricted. Though that is the problem of any game which tries to be open world. It has all these buildings, alleyways, and NPCs, but most of it is an illusion, something to be seen but not fully interacted with. But that is a general issue, my specific issue is how the game will have you travel all the way over here, take a train, and continue your journey, only to go back to where you original was. That was annoying as hell and without a quick travel feature, I often found myself more so interested in exploring the sewers or the few buildings I could walk into vs. continuing the story.
But, in general, I wouldn’t say there are any real major issues with this game. It did stutter on me sometimes, the load times between locations seemed a bit longer than I would like, and sometimes subtitles didn’t show up, but there aren’t any major issues.
On The Fence
As many already know, and I mention, part of the game’s, for a lack of a better term, atmosphere is about the rights of Augs and this has led to many bringing up the Black Lives Matter movement. To me, I would say the issues Augs are facing more correlates to the plight of Muslims across the world. But that little tidbit is an article I haven’t the mind to write.
Overall, perhaps what has me feeling this is a rental is that outside of the option to play non-lethal, and the fun hacking mini-game, Deus Ex: Mankind Divided feels like any other open-ended action/adventure/shooter game. Yes, it tries to be political, but that aspect of the game isn’t something strongly done. It is like Square-Enix wanted to use those hot topics for advertisement but not for serious exploration. Hence the rental label for while, I’m sure, DLC will extend many people’s play times, this just doesn’t have the replay value to really put down $60.

+ The game itself is good so far. Story, sound, gameplay - I like it. Not as much as I like Human Revolution, but still... Graphic is not as good as one may expect looking on system requirements, but I can live with it. I'm not finished the game, so I can't comment entire story.
- The game is buggy. Usually I don't care about it (unless there is game-breaking bugs not patched for long time), but in this case, patching process was developed by some guys who don't care about customer at all (see next paragraph).
- Publisher just lying about system requirements. Minimum requirements says "45 GB disk space", recommended - 55 GB (with DLC), but in fact game folder size currently reaches 64 GB, and you need another 25 GB (at least) to install patches. Yes, EVERY single patch preallocates 25GB disk space. So, actual minimum game requirements is about 90 GB (not a big deal if you have 4TB HDD, but it may be unpleasant surprise for some SSD owners). Today I got 123MB patch, and still this crappy patcher required 25GB free space to install it. It took almost half a hour on 4-core 16GB RAM system with SSD. Looks like every patch repacks major part of all game resources. What the hell, really? This is not a technical fighter.  It's a "reaction" and spamfest.  Reaction is in quotes because the way the game is designed it is impossible to react to the majority of played characters in ranked (or otherwise).  Dodge has a cooldown, attacks only have their animation as a down time.  Swords have no downtime, some characters heavies have no downtime.  You'll dodge an attack only to be spammed to death in endless combos with less than half a second to react in the small, small amount of leeway you have to dodge out.  Of course this assumes your dodge is even available.
They can't even get the respawn immunity design right.  Sometimes I get hit as soon as a get out of the spawn animation.  Sometimes I cant hit the enemy even a full two seconds out of their respawn (they'll literally stand there for 2 seconds immune).  And sometimes I have .5 seconds of immunity.  This inconsistency applies to every single thing in this game.  Hitboxes?  Seemingly random.  Who hits who first?  Determined by dice rolls (or really whichever character is fastest because they'll have less wind-up frames period regardless if you hit the button first).  I'd say at best 10% of my matches felt fair.
I played this game a year ago and it was the same story.  Most matches involved swords, bows, or katars then.  It's the same story now.  This isn't a brawl it's a spam fest.  Now the characters who don't use those weapons do involve skill and (most) have downtime.  I only have fun against those characters.  I only see those characters 10-20% of the time compare to the spammers.
Do you want to have fun 10-20% of the time?  Go nuts.  Otherwise, play any other fighter ever.

This game keeps getting me aggressive, so a cool way to calm down and make skinny guacamoles with homemade baked tortilla chips :
Skinny Guacamole:
2 medium green sweet peppers
2 medium fresh poblano chile peppers
1 bulb garlic
1/2 teaspoon olive oil
2 roma tomatoes, seeded and chopped
1 serrano pepper, minced
2 medium ripe avocados, halved, seeded, peeled, and diced
1 teaspoon lime zest
2 tablespoons lime juice
1/2 teaspoon salt
Baked Tortilla Chips:
Corn tortillas
Olive oil spray
Salt
For the guacamole:
Preheat oven to 425° F. Line a 15 x 10 x 1-inch baking pan with foil; set aside. Quarter, stem, and seed the peppers. Place pepper quarters, cut sides down, in the prepared pan. Cut off the top half inch of the garlic bulb to expose ends of individual cloves. Leaving garlic bulb whole, remove any loose, papery outer layers. Place bulb, cut end up, on a double thickness of foil. Drizzle with the oil. Bring foil up around bulb and fold edges together to loosely enclose. Place foil packet on the pan with the peppers.
Roast peppers and garlic for 20 to 30 minutes or until pepper skins are charred and garlic cloves feel soft. Allow to cool about 15 minutes. When garlic head is cool enough to handle, squeeze garlic paste out of the individual cloves.
In a food processor combine roasted pepper quarters and the garlic paste. Cover and pulse until combined, but still slightly chunky.
In a large bowl, combine tomatoes and serrano pepper. Add roasted pepper and garlic combination and stir to combine. Add diced avocado, lime zest, lime juice, and salt. Gently toss to combine.
Serve immediately or cover the surface with plastic wrap and chill for up to 1 hour.
For the chips:
Cut corn tortillas into wedges and place on a foil-lined baking sheet. Spray lightly with olive oil spray and season with salt, to taste.
Bake in a 350° F oven for 8-10 minutes or until lightly golden brown.

The controls are very poor, and were clearly designed with consoles in mind. For example, looking around in a vehicle using the mouse is difficult as the camera constantly tries to revert to its default position (which makes sense if using an analog stick, but not with a mouse). There is also a substantial amount of mouse acceleration, making aiming extremely awkward and difficult. Menus are clunky - console like - and are meant to be navigated using the arrow keys and enter instead of the mouse.
Graphics-wise, the game is unimpressive, especially for a 2011 game. There is heavy pop-in of vegetation, low quality textures, and excessive amounts of blur.
AI is dumb, especially your teammates which do practically nothing. They only come in handy when you get shot and need healing. The gameplay as actually quite linear, and not nearly as open-ended as it might seem. The large scale of enemy units in many cases can make for some entertaining shootouts, but by the end if actually felt much more like Call of Duty than a military simulator.

It was nice to see Mankind Divided start to try and tie in more with the original Deus Ex. The original is probably my favorite game of all time, so seeing Morgan Everett, Beth DuClare, Bob Page and Lucius DeBeers in a conversation was a bit thrilling. Seeing the formation of Silhouette, I assume TF29 will eventually become UNATCO and such was nice. The Janus character could be an early version of Deadalus, or maybe Morpheus. Each little nod to the original gave me a little smile.
But I don't quite see why a bunch of people were raving about it. There were a lot of different paths and methods to accomplish everything, but it felt like a lot of stuff had been added that you just never had to even look at. For example they added a crafting system to create items that I never felt I needed. This was possibly due to then non-lethal problem Dishonored had, where all of the cool gadgets and abilities were designed for a lethal playthrough and I was just stuck punching people in the face forever.
The story just didn't draw me in as much as Human Revolution, I think it was their attempt to have a 'no one can be trusted' vibe to the story, but instead it just felt like Adam wasn't really invested with anyone. If you're essentially working for both sides from the very start of the game, then noone can really betray you because you never actually trusted anyone. It is also quite short, very much feeling like the first half of the story trying to leave you on a cliffhanger.
Performance was also an issue. I would range from in running smooth as butter to about 10 fps depending on what I was looking at at times, and the loading times were atrocious. There is a transit system to hop between different parts of the central hub, but what I assume were meant to be quick transitions would sometimes take 5 minutes to load. When they have a repeating animation playing while it's loading it gets old VERY fast.
All in all it was an enjoyable game which had a huge amount of insignificant detail added to every small section of every map. I feel it was lacking in overall vision though, very much a game that was designed to try and make as much money as possible by dividing everything into individual parts after development was essentially completed.

What can I say about this game that hasn't been said already?
Real talk, I love the new Deus Ex series (Human Revolution and Mankind Divided). I played and purchased Human Revolution twice because I thought it was that good. It had the right mix of "find your own solution" gameplay with a great story. Now, how does Mankind Divided stack up against Human Revolution?
Quite well, actually. But it's far from perfect.
For starters, It's weird to stay in one hub world instead of traveling to different cities to do different things. Sure, Prague is pretty and nice, but I miss flying and staying in China, then flying to Detroit, and all that stuff in between. It gives the game a nice pace, instead of "take a train to one part of the city; oops, now you have to take another train to get to a different part of the city".
Another gripe that I have is about the characters; all of them, besides Adam, feel like they're not important or memorable. Everyone feels like they're supposed to serve a bigger role, but it feels like they only serve to move the plot forward.
Speaking of plot, while the plot this time around isn't as good as HR, it's still pretty good. The idea of Adam being a double agent is a good one, but unfortunately, the game doesn't let you play around with this plotpoint much.
SPOILER ALERT
The ending kinda sucks, as you have to choose between stopping the forgettable hulking aug from blowing up some buildings and stopping Nathaniel Brown from being poisoned. After you make the desicion and do the deed, the game just...ends. Then there's a little cinematic that shows what you did and hints at DLC or a sequel, but it doesn't FEEL like an ending.
END SPOILER
All in all, the gameplay ROCKS and is absolutely a reason to play it. You feel like Aug Jesus and it kicks♥♥♥♥♥
I'd say this game is worth it if you enjoyed Human Revolution and want more of the same. As for people that haven't played it and are thinking of picking this up, PLAY HUMAN REVOLUTION FIRST, then make your decision if you want to play this or not.
tl;dr: GAME IS GOOD, STORY NOT SO MUCH

Originally I had written what was the only negative review of this game, not for the gameplay but rather for some bugs/omissions in the porting process. I developer though has been working very hard on improving the game since then, and these issues have now been resolved, so I am able to finally recommend this game to everyone. That said, there are some things worth noting about it.
This is very clearly a port of the original game. What this means for you, the player, is that it will not play exactly like the Chip's Challenge you love and remember. I will, however, play very close. The game is well animated, mimicing the old Lynx version a little more closely than the Windows version, though with the recent addition of support for mulitple skins and the ability to toggle movement animation, you can bring the experience closer to the Windows 3.1 style if you so wish.
These minor differences, however, do not detract much from a wonderful game, and will likely only be noted by people like me who poured thousands of hours into the originals as a kid. Whether you are new to Chip's Challenge or looking to reexperience one of your childhood favorites, this is a wonderful way to do so.

TL;DR: shallow game, mediocre presentation, good online, not worth a lot of money, 7/10
Despite the praise this game gets, I don't think it surpasses the level of a good free Flash game. Of course the choice of vector art and skeletal animation is an obvious parallel that says nothing about the quality of the game. On the other hand that's where the gunk begins. The characters' anatomy is broken, and the animations are often dull. You might say I'm nitpicking, but the publisher asks AA-tier money for the "full version". So here's how the versions compare: free version, ALL characters have to be unlocked with in-game points, 4 different characters are freely playable each week; normal paid version, get all (future) characters, and some extra skins, and some store credit; over-prized version, all (future) characters, a lot of skins, and some more store credit. The "store credit" can be used in-game purchases with real money for more skins (taunts, nameplates, KO-effects, etc.). I don't think the skins are worth the money, but the online services might be worth something.
Now on how it plays. The characters are very floaty, have wall jump, and get three air-jumps. This leads very early on to air chases of epic proportions, which is nice. There is a combo system that seems good: beginners can't combo, and very skilled players can do massive combos. Most attacks are 'capturing': they have a start-up move and, if they connect, automatically follow up with an undodgeable move. There is no guard, only a invulerable dodging, with optional directions. Each character has unarmed moves, and can randomly pick up two weapons. There's two attack buttons. The attacks can be modified with either down or forward input to perform another attack. All sideways aerial attacks are slightly tilted versions of the up/neutral attacks. All in all that's way fewer moves than Smash Bros. This leads to very unvaried attack patterns. On the other hand, a technique is presented that allows you to perform ground moves in mid-air; this works well, but it looks silly.
The variation of characters is bad. They all play alike. The moves that are unique to each character are the heavy weapon attacks on the ground: with two weapons available, six in total. The rest of the attacks characters (with the same weapon) share. Some weapons seem more powerful than others, and unbalanced.
The online part is great. You see little lag, and don't have to wait long for a match. For me the "great community" I heard about only popped up after joining that guy that said "pls join my clan". More common are salty and bitter people.
Then the rest. The music is OK, and can be turned off. The game immediately recognized my GameCube controller; the game doesn't have analogue input though. The game rules are good too, with some nice customizable variations. Offline single player bores quickly, because the AI just doesn't do anything interesting. Seems to take a stab at addiction with collecting "gold", and experience points. No bugs.

Not much to say for voice acting as the game uses a made up language, which is my only criticism as well.
I feel that this game would've gotten way more emotion from me if it had actual English voice acting, assuming the voice acting was good.
I also think they could've at least added a few more voice-lines, even though it is just balderdash hearing the exact same voice-recordings over and over is off-putting.
A lot of people do not properly appreciate the world, the art in games.
This game is a true reminder to those people that there is a very creative, and talented team behind the world you are in.
The soundtrack coupled with the world you are in is just fenomenal, at some points I got chills, some points I sat back and took a sip of my coffee to just take it in.
The actual gameplay mechanics are great, and I personally feel like they nailed the 'play co-op with yourself' concept, it was done in a way where it wasn't too overwhelming, and I got used to it after the first 10-20 minutes of playing.
But I do admit the first minutes it felt very alien and a little off-putting. But yes, I got used to it and I imagine most people will. I can't see a person quitting the game because they got frustrated from controlling 2 characters at the same time.

The premise of the game is simple. You are 2 brothers who's father is sick, you must go out on an adventure to find a potion, of sorts, to save him.
But this game is more dark and grim than it may seem on the surface. It has some unexpected, and indeed dark, turns in the story.
I belive everyone should go into this game blind, spoiling something may very well ruin the entire game for you.
Whether you buy this game on sale or not; it is worth it.
3-4 hours of gameplay with an amazing, powerful story, good game mechanics, a beautiful world filled with fenomenal music is worth it to me.
It almost feels like that the lower expectations you have going into the game will leave you more and more amazed at the end.

First and foremost, I'd like to start off by clarifying one thing. This game does NOT require a controller to play. It is a bit tricky to get used to the keyboard controls at the very beginning, but after a while it shouldn't be too difficult to get the hang of. I've personally only played this game on keyboard and have only had one or two experiences where it was kind of tough to pass a point in the game because of the keyboard controls. I'm not sure why the game's store page says having a controller is a requirement. Yes, a controller would probably make the game more enjoyable as it would be easier to control both brothers, but not having a controller doesn't make playing the game anywhere near impossible. If the only reason you're hesitating to get this game is because of the "controller requirement" on the store page, get this game. Especially when it hits around $1.5 during sales, there really isn't any reason not to get it.
Moving onto the game itself, it's a nice little adventure game that you can apparently finish in 4-5 hourse (I don't know how I managed to squeeze 13 hours out of it on a single play-through). The artwork is visually stunning. Really nice soundtrack. Gameplay is fun. Provided there is virtually no comprehendable dialogue between the characters, the story was also fairly good. The story gets even better near the end. The ending itself is really nice (won't go into any details to avoid spoilers). Somebody dies and unlike the million other videogame deaths you've experienced, the game makes sure that you're really affected.
Overall, I'd say this game is a must-play, especially because it doesn't even take that much of your time to finish. I don't know if the full price is really worth it considering the amount of content you get, but on sale at a bit over a dollar or as part of a bundle, this game is a must-grab.
Taking all things into consideration, I'd give the game a 9/10.
The biggest thing that really drawed me in was it's artwork. The game even has benches where you can just sit down and enjoy the view. Another reason I loved it was the ending. The only reason I didn't give it any higher is because I think they could've worked on the story a tad bit more and also make it longer. But again, like I already said, there isn't any comprehendable dialogue that goes on between the characters, and I understand that by doing this the game-makers wanted to show you the story and make you see it for yourself rather than have the characters tell you about it. Taking that into regards, the story doesn't dissapoint.
If this game has just been sitting in your library and collecting dust, or you've been eyeing it every sale but haven't decided on actually getting it because you aren't sure whether you'll actually enjoy it, give this game a chance. I promise you it'll be a very unique experience from what other games have to offer.

A simple take on the "Metroidvania" formula, DLC Quest is a game with an agenda. It is a scathing satire on what our industry has become with references to "Early Access" DLC, cosmetic items, one time use items, day one patches, and product placement. The main mechanic of the game is exploring the world while collecting coins in order to pay for the newest "downloadable" content packs. These come in the form of cosmetic items, zombie packs, and even necessary components like animations, music, and the ability to jump. It is all presented with its tongue firmly planted in cheek, but it is a lampoon on the increasing monetization of the industry. There are few games that critique the medium as well as this game has, and for that reason it is important.
*There are no refunds for this recommendation.

The game is fun and well balanced. While it may look like smash it doesn't play like it (although some terms and skills do transfer) with a intersting combat system. Each character or "legend" has 3 movesets. Unarmed which is shared among all the characters, Weapon A which is 1 of the many weapons in the game and weapon B which is another weapon your legend can use. ach weapon has standard attacks and each legend has a unique signiture move (will be reffered to as "sig") to go along with it. Each weapon light attack is identical to the others. for example a sword Neutral light (Nlight) is multiple swipes infront of the legend for every sword. what makes each sword  diffrent is the sigs and stats that go with it. to use swor as a example again on one character the Neutral sig (Nsig) on Koji is a cross slash diagnally in front of him while for hattori the Nsig is her teloporting up and swiping down in front of her. Each stat on the legends is diffrent. There is attack, Dexterity, defence, and movement speed i assume you can guess what each does. The game is a load of fun can can be run even on the weakest of PC's. It can fill the needs of both casual and competitive players while staying fun for both.
Now on to the bad things. The game does include micrtransations although they are purely cosmetic like a new skin or costume for a character of weapon. Nothing major you don't need to buy anything to progress in the game. The game's servers are not the best and have given out after a big update. although the devs say they are trying to fix it meaing this may become out dated soon. and that is about it for the promlems i have with it.

If I had to compare Brawlhalla to any other game it would Super Smash Bros. Brawl. Just a much, much simpler version. It's a fun game to play with friends, especially if you have a lot of friends, but playing online gets old pretty quickly. There isn't any sort of story to Brawlhalla, just raw multiplayer action. Playing the game for the first time, you'll notice that the characters are very floaty and that some of the weapons are clearly better than others.
My main complaint about the game is that there isn't any way to unlock characters other than purchasing them. If you do well in online matches or collect your daily reward, you'll be given gold coins, which makes you think that you'll be able to unlock characters or cosmetics by playing well online. However, in order to unlock characters and cosmetics, you need to pay with mammoth coins, which can only be bought - not earned.
Overall, I absolutely recommend the game, especially since it's free to play. However, I don't think that Brawhalla is worth $20, which is what I paid to unlock all of the characters. I would only recommend paying to unlock all of the characters if you play avidly, or if you're competing very seriously online.

The game description itself and almost every review I've read about this game mentioned how this game was such a great nod to 80's action flicks. Sure enough, there is an 80's action flick atmosphere here but ultimately it all comes down to the game being cheesy for the sake of being cheesy. It feels uninspired. The game has way too many cutscenes that are horribly executed. They're meant to imitate pixelated graphics from the 80's but are just out of place here altogether. They simply feel like an excuse for the developer not to create a specific game sequence. Instead of having to flee a secret lab using a stunt jump yourself, you get to watch a set of pixelated images of the event in question. Enemy variety is non-existent either: you're basically fighting against Daft Punk all the time. Weapons are extremely unbalanced. A Daft Punk guy may take about five bullets to the head or a whole magazine to the chest in order to die, though you could also hit it with an arrow to the knee to get him down. All in all a pretty bad game capitalizing on the success of Far Cry 3 on the one hand and 80's nostalgia on the other. Cheesiness alone is not enough to make a game good. On a side note I've had no problems with UPlay whatsoever.

Fantastic hidden object and puzzle game with a couple of "didn't see that coming" twists.
In
, you play the part of Angelica Weaver, psychic detective. Your mission is to solve a murder by hunting for clues in both the past and the present. This is done, unsurprisingly, by finding objects and solving puzzles.
The puzzles aren't too difficult, but a lot of them are quite challenging and require patience and "thinking outside the box". As far as graphics and story, this game is actually among one of the best I've played in this genre. The graphics are smooth and good quality, and while the voice acting won't win any awards, it's still quite good, especially compared to a lot of other games in the hidden object/puzzle game genre.
I wouldn't recommend paying full price for this game, as it's quite short (I finished it in less than 3 hours), but if you see it at 50%+ sale, then it's worth grabbing.

The production values are pretty high, graphics look good and there are plenty of locations. But the story is a rather unintersting murder mystery without even much of a mystery, as all the victims were more or less random anyway. The puzzles in this game are also of the unlogical kind, e.g. use a mouse trap to splice an electric wire together or you run into situation where you need a stick-like thing and have three in your invetory, but only one works. The game never manages to establish a proper flow and you end up either trial&error through the puzzles or using the hint system, it's just not much fun to play.

A hidden object game is designed to be one giant iteration of I Spy, so it feels petty to pick on the plot. I’m going to pick on the plot. It’s so wildly convoluted. Angelica uses her mystical dreamweaver powers to travel through time, because today’s serial killer is copycatting a serial killer of a hundredish years ago. She must solve the mystery in both timelines, of course, making bad calls and chasing red herrings and through sheer trial and error of set piece, I guess arriving at the right conclusion? I can follow Ace Attorney. I can’t follow Angelica Weaver. All I can remember is that she walks into a surgeon’s place of work, and decides, based on the presence of surgical tools, that he fits a serial killer’s profile. Also, she is unable to enter a locked room until she finds thirty pieces of fabric, because the serial killer demands it. I’m not sure how the serial killer is enforcing this.
I can also tell that Angelica Weaver can fit fifteen benches in her backpack.
But really, for what it is, it’s fine and short enough. You’re here to click on objects. Objects will be clicked. Crimes will somehow be solved. Shoes will be matched. Ghosts will ascend to happier planes. What other pleasure is there in life?

If I had to compare Brawlhalla to any other game it would Super Smash Bros. Brawl. Just a much, much simpler version. It's a fun game to play with friends, especially if you have a lot of friends, but playing online gets old pretty quickly. There isn't any sort of story to Brawlhalla, just raw multiplayer action. Playing the game for the first time, you'll notice that the characters are very floaty and that some of the weapons are clearly better than others.
My main complaint about the game is that there isn't any way to unlock characters other than purchasing them. If you do well in online matches or collect your daily reward, you'll be given gold coins, which makes you think that you'll be able to unlock characters or cosmetics by playing well online. However, in order to unlock characters and cosmetics, you need to pay with mammoth coins, which can only be bought - not earned.
Overall, I absolutely recommend the game, especially since it's free to play. However, I don't think that Brawhalla is worth $20, which is what I paid to unlock all of the characters. I would only recommend paying to unlock all of the characters if you play avidly, or if you're competing very seriously online.

Hit Detection | verb | /hit dəˈtekSH(ə)n/ | - the computational problem of detecting the intersection of two or more objects. While the topic is most often associated with its use in video games and other physical simulations, it also has applications in robotics. In addition to determining whether two objects have collided, collision detection systems may also calculate time of impact (TOI), and report a contact manifold (the set of intersecting points). Collision response deals with simulating what happens when a collision is detected. Solving collision detection problems requires extensive use of concepts from linear algebra and computational geometry.
Hitbox | noun | /hit bäks/ | - an invisible shape commonly used in video games for real-time collision detection. It is often a rectangle (in 2D games) or cuboid (in 3D) that is attached to and follows a point on a visible object (such as a model or a sprite), though circular or spheroidial shapes are also common. It is common for animated objects to have a set of hitboxes attached to one moving part each to ensure accuracy during motion.

The Mean Greens is a nostalgic and briliantly crafted shooter. This is how you imagined your little plastic army men battling it out when you were a kid.
Pros:
Each map has such attention to detail that it shames AAA shooters of today. Maps like Art Table look like somone took time in laying out each map piece, unlike the boringly similar maps we see all too often. The game also looks very good, graphically. It's running on the Unreal 4 engine, so it's certainly no slouch in the technical deparment. The lighting is great, physics are fantastic, and the models are all very well made.
The development team is very active. They frequently ask for player feedback and I have seen various Devs interacting with the community on Twitch. This game is 100% a passion project, and the Devs are clearly devoted to delivering a quality experience to its players.
Cons:
This game is still in developement, so it is far from perfect. As of right now there are several glitches to be fixed and various tweaks to be made. Notably, the match making and conectivity is a bit wonky, hit detection is bad and surely needs a revamp. Also I would not say this game is very well optimized, I have seen plenty of random fps drops even on high end rigs. However, all of these issues can certainly be fixed and I have no doubt the Dev Team is hard at work.
Additional Thoughts: This game is very refreshing, I have not played such a fun and unique online shooter since the first time I played the Ratchet and Clank series. Nor have I ever met such a passionate Dev Team, these guys really want this to be the best game it possible can. No DLC or f2p gimmicks, the Devs actually want you to have a fun time instead of the shady tactics we've seen from AAA companies lately.
